It provides students with an understanding in respect to project charters, project management plans and associated documents. It also introduces various tools and techniques as well as providing an overview of project management lifecycles, processes and knowledge areas.
learning_outcomes: Define the role of the project manager in general and specific terms
Identify and describe fundamental project management knowledge and concepts
Explain the value of project management processes, tools and techniques
Describe recognised project management documents
Describe in general terms the value of the PMBOK®Guide
antirequisites: N/A

title: Digital Solution Methodologies
overview: The aim of this course is to engage students with the frameworks and methodologies associated with implementing digital led business transformation opportunities, and to equip students to undertake value case analysis. Transforming business with digital technologies requires the use of different frameworks, approaches, and techniques. We will introduce different methodologies commonly used when implementing digital technologies. Approaches for defining value will be used to assess potential digital transformation opportunities. Examples from Accenture projects and initiatives will be used to demonstrate how the methodologies are used to implement digital opportunities. Use of methodologies in business for digital transformation Introduction to frameworks and approaches used when implementing digital technologies in business Application of different methodologies Examples of where methodologies have been used when deploying digital technologies in business Criteria used to evaluate which methodology to apply Methodologies, Frameworks and Approaches Design Thinking (DT) fundamentals: Approaches-Discover, Describe, Ideate, Prototype, Test, Bring to Life, Retrospective and Reflection, DT tools like affinity clustering, round robin, concept poster etc. Agile fundamentals: Planned and Unplanned Agile approaches, Bundles and Sprints, Scrum, Kanban Metrics, Waterfall vs. Agile, Roles DevOps fundamentals: Optimise, Organise, Empower, Align Value case creation Data driven insights and data visualisation
learning_outcomes: Describe how different frameworks and methodologies are used for implementation of digital technologies.
Apply selected frameworks and methodologies to resolve business problems in case scenarios.
Evaluate the benefits of applying different delivery methodologies to business challenges.
Define the value case for a digital transformation opportunity.
Derive insights from data.
Illustrate the data driven insights using visual techniques.
prerequisites: must have completed all of BUSI1014 Exploring Digital Technology in Business/BUSI1015 Introduction to Digital Disruption in Business
antirequisites: must not have completed BUSS2089 UO Digital Solution Methodologies at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed BUSS2090 Digital Solution Methodologies at the University of South Australia

title: WIL/ Profession
overview: This course is designed to provide students with an industry opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge gained in their academic studies to real-world professional settings through a placement or internship experience. Students will engage in hands-on learning within organizations relevant to their field of study, gaining practical skills, industry insights, and valuable networking contacts. Additionally, the course will support students on career development, including resume building, interview preparation, and professional networking, to enhance students' employability and career readiness.
learning_outcomes: Perform appropriate tasks in a professional business and management context
Link management concepts, techniques and practices to the practical operations of enterprises
Develop personal goals to enable them to increase personal skills and competencies through observation, discussion and practices in a workplace setting
Communicate effectively in a professional setting
Identify the complex practical and ethical considerations that affect decision making processes in professional business practice
Demonstrate skills in Self-Management, Problem Solving, Ethical Awareness, Oral and Written Communication at advanced level
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Decision Making, Communication and Organisational Practice
overview: Students will investigate the professional communication and decision making for contemporary organisations. They will develop skills in problem solving, analysis and communication, equipping them with the practical application of critical thinking for managers, communicating professionally with impact, and challenging beliefs and information.
learning_outcomes: Identify and explain the characteristics of different types of management problems and decisions, problem solvers and decision makers and approaches to problem solving and decision making
Examine different approaches to problem solving and management decision making through various methods, including business meetings and technology-aided communication
Discuss strategies for the effective management of organisational communication, including intercultural and intergenerational communication and feedback
Apply team communication and development strategies to the critical analysis and solving of contemporary business problems
Apply communication knowledge to common practical contexts in organisations
antirequisites: N/A

title: UO Digital Business Solutions
overview: The aim of this course is to provide the opportunity to students to create a minimum viable digital solution to address a business challenge facing industry today and to determine how the product could be scaled and implemented into a business environment. Many factors can influence the successful implementation and adoption of a digital solution in business. Managing the change, negotiating with stakeholders and managing timelines, budget and risks are all critical for successful implementation and adoption. A minimum viable product will be developed. An implementation roadmap, change plan, and sustainment plan will be developed. In developing the project outcomes, real world examples of issues and challenges experienced on Accenture projects will need to be addressed. Solutions for the business challenge to be provided by learners in this course: Creating a digital product design to address a business challenge Planning a digital transformation Change impact and change strategy Risk analysis and mitigation strategies for digital transformations Scaling and sustaining the implementation of a digital solution Real-world references to approach the business challenge in this course: Further details on the business case: stakeholder requirements, operational challenges etc Further data on the business organisation (fictitious): business performance, employees etc Sources and industry references for creating a digital product design and roadmap for digital solution Industry insights, industry reports and expert recommendations on change management for digital transformation Industry examples and client cases on scaling and sustaining digital transformation
learning_outcomes: Create a digital product design to demonstrate how a proposed digital solution could address an industry challenge.
Create a roadmap for implementing a digital solution within an organisation considering the requirements of the business and stakeholders.
Define a change strategy.
Describe the key risks with implementing the solution and the mitigating actions that could be taken.
Estimate the requirements on the organization to scale and sustain the digital product design if it was put into production.
Team effectively to work independently and collaboratively as a member and leader of diverse teams.
prerequisites: Must have completed 1 of BUSI1019 UO Exploring Digital Technology in Business/BUSI1020 UO Introduction to Digital Disruption in Business/BUSI2014 UO Designing Digital Solutions/BUSI2015 Digital Solution Methodologies
antirequisites: Must not have completed BUSS3116 UO Digital Business Solutions at the University of South Australia

title: UO Digital Business Value
overview: The aim of this course is to extend students' understanding of the value of digital business transformation by identifying potential digital disruptors that could be implemented to address a real-world business challenge, evaluate the different proposed digital disruption solutions, build a value case, and produce a recommendation that could be taken to stakeholders. Develop a value case to demonstrate the value of implementing digital technology to address a business challenge similar to those that Accenture works on for clients. Defining the value case and recommendation will include research of industry challenges, assessment of different digital technologies, definition of prioritisation criteria and assessment against the criteria, development of the business case and presentation of the solution. Solutions for the business challenge to be provided by learners in this course: Industry challenge evaluation Digital Innovation Digital solution identification Value case development Stakeholder identification and management Tailoring messages for different audiences Real-world references to approach the business challenge in this course: Industry analysis and insights Analyst reports Industry point of views Industry examples and client cases on value creation through digital transformation Industry insights, industry reports and expert recommendations on implementing a digital solution.
learning_outcomes: Plan an approach to define value case for implementing a digital solution to address a business challenge.
Research industry challenges where digital technology could be applied.
Propose a digital technology solution based on financial analysis and development of a value case.
Justify the proposed digital technology solution.
Produce a recommendation that could be taken to a stakeholder describing the benefits of implementing a proposed digital solution.
prerequisites: must have completed all of BUSI2014 UO Designing Digital Solutions/BUSI2023 UO Digital Solution Methodologies
antirequisites: must not have completed BUSS3117 UO Digital Business Value at the University of South Australia

title: Strategic Management
overview: Using case studies, the course aims to equip students with a practical understanding of relevant concepts and frameworks needed to make better strategic decisions in the context of dynamic and fast-changing business and management environments. Students can expect to critically explore how continuous and accurate analysis of essential strategic tasks and an analysis of the interaction between the internal and external environment contribute to a successful strategy.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the internal and external environments in which businesses operate and assess their significance for future initiatives
Apply understanding of the theories, concepts and tools that support strategic management in organisations
Individually and collaboratively evaluate and synthesise information and existing knowledge from numerous sources and experiences
Apply appropriate tools, theories and concepts to analyse strategic issues in organisations and to develop potential implementation options
Participate constructively in team situations to complete shared tasks and meet agreed deadlines
prerequisites: must have completed BUSI1002 Management, Organisations and Leadership
antirequisites: N/A

title: UO Designing Digital Solutions
overview: The aim of this course is to enable students to apply the frameworks and knowledge of digital disruptors to solve a business challenge by working through a case study that has them analysing business challenges, assessing different digital technologies to address the challenge, prioritising solutions, and defining key milestones for implementing. Using a case study based on Accenture project scenarios, students will analyse business challenges, assess different digital technologies to address the challenges, prioritise solutions and define key milestones for implementing. The use of methodologies and frameworks will be demonstrated in working through the case study tasks and activities. Case study-based learning activity: Evaluation of business challenges Identify digital solutions to address challenges Ideate, test, and iterate on potential solutions Develop proposal for proposed solution including value case Pitch proposal Approaches, tools, and methodologies that will be applied by learners in this course: Agile Design Thinking Evaluation techniques Value case development Business Communication
learning_outcomes: Select appropriate digital technological frameworks and methodologies to address a given business challenge.
Apply the appropriate frameworks and technologies to propose a solution for the business challenge.
Evaluate the financial and change impact of implementing a digital solution to address a business challenge.
Formulate recommendations based on outcome of preliminary evaluation and using the appropriate tools, techniques, and frameworks for the given business challenge.
Communicate the recommendations effectively through a presentation using appropriate business language.
Collaborate effectively as a team.
prerequisites: must have completed all of BUSI1014 Exploring Digital Technology in Business/BUSI1015 Introduction to Digital Disruption in Business OR must have completed all of BUSI1019 UO Exploring Digital Technology in Business/BUSI1020 UO Introduction to Digital Disruption in Business
antirequisites: must not have completed BUSS2088 UO Designing Digital Solutions at the University of South Australia

title: WIL / Profession
overview: This course is designed to provide students with an industry opportunity to apply theoretical knowledge gained in their academic studies to real-world professional settings through a placement or internship experience. Students will engage in hands-on learning within organizations relevant to their field of study, gaining practical skills, industry insights, and valuable networking contacts. Additionally, the course will support students on career development, including resume building, interview preparation, and professional networking, to enhance students' employability and career readiness.
learning_outcomes: Perform appropriate tasks in a professional business and management context
Link management concepts, techniques and practices to the practical operations of enterprises
Link management concepts, techniques and practices to the practical operations of enterprises
Communicate effectively in a professional setting
Identify the complex practical and ethical considerations that affect decision making processes in professional business practice
Demonstrate skills in Self-Management, Problem Solving, Ethical Awareness, Oral and Written Communication at advanced level
antirequisites: N/A

title: Research Methods in Media and Communication
overview: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of media and communication research methods, methodologies, processes and approaches, and their use and application across academic and industry perspectives in a variety of forms of research. The course will provide students with an understanding of the nature of media and communication research and the research process, including issues such as planning research, aligning aims and expectations with methods, and thinking about resources, ethics and equity. The course will also teach students specific methodological skills and tools that are applicable across a range of sectors and industries.
learning_outcomes: Possess an understanding of media and communication research, including the nature of different types of research approaches and how to plan and carry out research
Understand and apply a range of research methods to a range of media and communication and in response to needs across academic, industry and government settings
Develop a coherent research plan that could, if needed, be applied to a contemporary issue or problem within the field of media and communication
Reflect on, in an informed way, some of the key ethical questions and considerations in media and communication research

Develop the ability to critically evaluating existing media and communication research through an understanding of the strengths and weaknesses of different methods and best practice in planning research projects
antirequisites: N/A

title: Media Law, Policy and Ethics
overview: This course explores the legal, ethical and policy regulations and issues affecting media practice. Students will examine how legal and ethical considerations align, intersect and conflict, and consider their impact upon media practitioners, industries and society. Students will analyse approaches to media governance and ethical decision making and analyse the effectiveness of current policies and approaches in adapting to technological and societal change.
learning_outcomes: Understand and analyse the media laws, policies, and regulatory frameworks in Australia, explaining how they enable or constrain effective media environments.
Understand the legal obligations, rights, and ethical considerations affecting media practitioners in the execution of their professional duties.
Critically evaluate the challenges and limitations of applying existing media laws and regulations and ethical codes and guidelines to emerging digital and new media environments.
Develop critical thinking skills to identify and navigate the complex issues associated with media regulatory frameworks and ethical practice.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Promotional Culture
overview: This course enables students to critically examine theoretical and applied approaches to promotional culture in contemporary society.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the development, use and role of promotional culture in society
Explain how promotional texts are constructed to position or influence audiences
Apply theoretical concepts and textual analysis techniques to a range of promotional materials
Evaluate and critique promotional communication, its creative elements, media strategies and social impacts
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of MDIA1018 Key Concepts in Media and Communication/MDIA2101 Creating Content for Media
antirequisites: N/A

title: Strategic Planning for Media and Communication
overview: This course equips students with the theoretical and applied skills required to research, develop, implement and evaluate media and communication projects, campaigns and activities. The course consolidates foundational knowledge and professional competencies acquired through earlier courses in the media and communication core and majors, extending this to the integration, planning and management of media and communication projects in a range of professional contexts.
learning_outcomes: Understand the theoretical knowledge, frameworks and skills that inform strategic planning
Conduct and analyse formative research, and use this to inform the development of goals and objectives
Develop and identify the scope of a strategic project, taking into account relevant legal and ethical considerations
Identify and implement project management techniques, including budgets and schedules
Understand techniques for coordinating work teams, and apply these to groupwork
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of MDIA2101 Creating Content for Media/MDIA2102 Promotional Culture
antirequisites: N/A

title: Digital Design Principles and Methods
overview: This course aims to introduce students to industry-standard software and help them attain proficiency in its use. As a foundational level course, it will explore the application of digital tools in designing outcomes for both screen and print. Students will develop skills in document creation, management, and output, as well as in colour management, image creation, composition, resolution, and layout. This course enhances students' ability to produce outcomes for other courses in their program.
learning_outcomes: Attain proficiency in industry-standard software tools for creating, editing, and managing graphic elements for print and screen
Develop proficiency in text and page layout design, including organising content, structuring visual elements, and optimising layouts for readability and visual appeal
Attain proficiency in raster image editing, including resolution management, image retouching, compositing, and colour correction for print and screen applications
Gain proficiency in creating and editing vector-based graphics, including drawing shapes, applying effects, and managing colour for diverse design projects
Understand principles and techniques of colour management to ensure accurate colour reproduction and consistency across different output formats and mediums
Attain techniques for optimising designs for print and screen outputs, including file format selection, resolution settings, and colour mode adjustments, to produce professional-quality outcomes
antirequisites: N/A

title: Scheduling and Cost Management
overview: This course presents important concepts in respect to time and cost as related to projects. The area of time management will be covered with some emphasis on the scheduling of activities and durations and their sequencing. This includes studying the critical path method, project evaluation review technique, project schedules and Gantt charts, milestones and reporting. The cost management component will look at a wide array of cost related measures. This will include cost planning, project feasibility, cost forecasting and estimates, budgets, earned value management, project cost accounting, cost control and reporting.
learning_outcomes: Outline important concepts in respect to project time and cost
Explain how project managers manage time and cost on projects
Demonstrate how project schedules are used to control project timelines
Describe how cost management is utilised on project work
Make use of tools and techniques as relevant to these areas
antirequisites: N/A

title: Project Logistics and Supply Chains
overview: This course aims to build an understanding of system support planning and logistics support over a project life-cycle. Furthermore, the implications of an extended supply chain are to be considered. The course will teach topics in respect to the components of logistics, logistics engineering and management, system design for supportability and continued assessment. Other areas that are covered include supply chain integration, information flows, materials, services, human resources and supply chain monetary aspects, tiered suppliers and technology coordination, supply chain enterprise architecture and waste minimisation.
learning_outcomes: Describe the concept of “systems” across the logistics and supply chain project life-cycle
Plan supportability requirements for the development of logistics and supply chains systems
Identify design techniques and technologies that support logistics and extended supply chains
Work effectively in teams on logistical systems and supply chain development
Recognise ethical, social and cultural issues within logistics and supply chains
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: eChallenge
overview: This course aims to systematically assess the viability of innovative project ideas, a skill essential for any career, not just entrepreneurship. Evidence suggests that university is an optimal time to develop such capabilities. The eChallenge course is specifically designed to allow you to understand customer pains and gains, craft innovative solutions using creative strategies, test these ideas through interactions with customers, mentors, and industry experts, and ultimately present your ideas to a panel of industry investors. Additionally, networking during industry interactions offers further benefits. The course also features various cash and in-kind prizes, culminating in a black-tie awards dinner with industry veterans and investors. It serves as an initial step into entrepreneurship for many, leading to significant entrepreneurial successes, and provides a valuable learning experience to accelerate their career progression for all participants.
learning_outcomes: Identify and evaluate a potential innovative project as an entrepreneurial opportunity using a systematic process
Determine a practical and innovative resource strategy to exploit an entrepreneurial opportunity in an innovative manner
Build an effective entrepreneurial team to develop strategies to exploit the entrepreneurial opportunity
Communicate and present a entrepreneurial opportunity as a new venture concept to relevant stakeholders including investors
antirequisites: N/A

title: Business Lifecycles
overview: This course uses a lifecycle perspective of the firm to develop students' understanding of the interrelated nature of the different business disciplines required to start-up and grow a business successfully. Using an online business simulation game, student groups compete with each other in growing a business in a virtual world while learning about the role of entrepreneurship, strategy, marketing, finance, business structures, management, accounting, taxation, and exit and succession planning. The course will appeal to those who are interested in starting up and/or owning a business managing a business, as well as those intending to become business advisors, leaders or policymakers.
learning_outcomes: Analyse business data and market trends within the simulated environment, and make informed decisions and recommendations.
Develop strategic plans, anticipating market dynamics, comprehend competitive forces and assess long-term business performance.
Solve problems and develop creative solutions in response to changing market conditions and competition.
Effectively collaborate within a team environment, and communicate strategies clearly and succinctly
antirequisites: N/A

title: WIL (Procurement and Supply Chain Management)
overview: This course enables students to develop a practical understanding of their particular field of study as it applies to a work environment, enhance their employability through investigating career options and pathways, and explore the impact of the labour market and an individuals values, interests and other competencies on career satisfaction. An industry placement is carried out under academic and industry supervision. By undertaking a project or placement within a discipline specific organisation, students apply the knowledge of their discipline gained through their studies to work related tasks and gain valuable experience related to their future career. Students are assessed through a proposal, reflection and report.
learning_outcomes: Perform appropriate tasks in a professional business and management context, with course readings and activities by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, reflection and report

Link management concepts, techniques and practices to the practical operations of enterprises, with course readings and activities by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, reflection and report

Develop personal goals to enable them to increase personal skills and competencies through observation, discussion and practices in a workplace setting, with course readings and activities by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, reflection and report
Communicate effectively in a professional setting, with course readings and activities by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, reflection and report

Identify the complex practical and ethical considerations that affect decision making processes in professional business practice, with course readings and activities by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, reflection and report

Demonstrate skills in self-management, problem solving, ethical awareness, and written communication, with course readings and activities by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, reflection and report
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport Practicum 1
overview: This course provides the opportunity for students to gain practical experience in a relevant industry environment and to begin to apply some of the theory and skills developed in courses during their program of study.
learning_outcomes: Link academic research techniques, practices and discipline to the practical needs of industry
Formulate, implement and explain objectives for a field placement which directly links academic learning with industry needs
Develop personal and career goals and identify steps to realise these goals
Develop skills and competencies which will assist in securing suitable field placements
Reflect and derive learning outcomes both from a personal and organisational perspective
Identify and develop skills and behaviours that will be beneficial in the sport industry workplace.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport Practicum 2
overview: The course offers students a secondary placement in the third year of their program of study. The course and placement requirements and assessment extend on Sport Practicum 1 and are geared towards students nearing the completion of their undergraduate studies. Accordingly, the assessment has a large focus on reflective practice and the application of learning outcomes towards future job application processes. Students are encouraged to consider placements that provide opportunity to further enhance previously developed skills and knowledge or to consider a previously unexplored potential career pathway.
learning_outcomes: Link academic research techniques, practices, and discipline to the practical needs of industry
Develop personal and career goals and identify steps to realise these goals
Reflect and derive learning outcomes both form a personal and organisational perspective
Identify learning outcomes applicable to future job application processes
Align placement objectives with future career aspirations
antirequisites: N/A

title: Integrated Marketing
overview: In this course students will integrate their knowledge of marketing developed through participation in various courses into a comprehensive understanding of marketing as a part of overall business management. It also exposes students to the vagaries of competition and provides practical experience in dealing with this fundamental issue. The course provides students some real-world experience of working as a Product Marketing Manager, exposing them to both the highs and the lows resulting from their business and marketing decisions. Students reflect on what they have already learnt and integrate all their business and marketing thinking, in a team-based competitive marketing strategy simulation - StratSim (Strategic Management Simulation).
learning_outcomes: Integrate the many concepts learned in specialised marketing courses into an overall understanding of marketing and business in a competitive environment
Integrate marketing knowledge with other business concepts from economics, finance, accounting, human relations, and business management
Design and apply a strategic marketing plan
Develop and apply skills in oral and written presentation and negotiation
Demonstrate the ability to work successfully in a team to achieve autonomous and organisational objectives
prerequisites: must have completed all of MARK2000 Marketing Analytics/MARK3005 Marketing Planning
antirequisites: N/A

title: Strategic Communication in Practice
overview: This course explores the strategic communication function across various industry sectors, such as sports, arts, events, not-for-profits, finance, fashion, hospitality, defence, essential services, and agriculture. Strategic communication specialisations, such as internal communication, leadership communication, sponsorship, community engagement, and event management may also be covered. The course also enables students to apply the concepts and skills acquired throughout their program to real-life strategic communication scenarios, further strengthening their professional competencies and career readiness.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the characteristics, opportunities and challenges of different specialisations and industry sectors within strategic communication.
Apply the professional competencies and skills required of strategic communication practitioners.
Demonstrate knowledge of different communication strategies and tactics and apply these to a strategic communication scenario.
Analyse internal communications and leadership communication styles within an organisation and make recommendations for improvement.
antirequisites: N/A

title: WIL
overview: The course offers students a choice between a class-based experience or an internship with an Australian business, not-for-profit organisation, or government department. This allows students to gain simulated or hands-on experience in an environment where they can observe and apply the knowledge and skills acquired during their degree. If students opt for the internship, they must seek approval from the Internships Team on their proposed work placement so that a formal and structured work placement, which is relevant to their studies is arranged and participation in pre-placement activities can be undertaken.
learning_outcomes: Plan, coordinate and undertake a range of professional activities and engage in reflective practices to facilitate personal and professional growth
Identify skills and capabilities that intersect effectively with the needs of industry
Apply and practice good communication skills in a variety of professional and/or cultural contexts
Evaluate the course experience in relation to personal career goals
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Project Management Professional Practice
overview: This course allows students to pursue an industry or field as related to their interest, experience or background. The selected area shall be studied in detail in the context of project management. It will involve developing a project charter and comprehensive project management plan in respect to a conceptual project in the student's field of interest. This project will be investigated delivering outcomes that will assist students to understand the fundamentals and technicalities of a particular project as based within a professional process oriented project management framework.
learning_outcomes: Outline the requirements of a selected project in a concise way
Analyse a selected project and plan for its successful delivery
Document project management requirements in a professional manner
Communicate the project management plan to an audience
antirequisites: N/A

title: Negotiated Project in the Bachelor of Business (P and SCM)
overview: This course enables students to gain experience in research and equip them with knowledge and skills in preparation for potential further higher degree in research studies. In this course, students undertake a structured research project under the supervision of an academic staff member. The research topic is negotiated between the student and potential supervisor. It is expected that the research domain shall be in the business discipline of Procurement and Supply Chain Management. Students are assessed through a proposal, presentation and report.
learning_outcomes: Analyse procurement and supply chain research approaches with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, presentation and report
Evaluate procurement and supply chain research problems with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, presentation and report

Acquire, synthesise and apply information relevant to procurement and supply chain management research with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, presentation and report

Differentiate alternative solutions to procurement and supply chain problems with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, presentation and report

Recommend research-supported solutions to procurement and supply chain problems with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, presentation and report

Demonstrate skills in problem solving, oral and written communication, and applying an international perspective with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a proposal, presentation and report
antirequisites: N/A

title: International Human Resource Management
overview: This course aims to foster a critical understanding of the role and functions of human resource activities within multinational Enterprises (MNEs). It explores key issues about the challenges in managing people across diverse institutional contexts. Topics include globalisation and the management of work, managing people across different national business systems, how multinational people management is shaped and transferred, expatriate management, pay compensation in MNEs, Equality and diversity, and employee voice. Through an examination of the context, strategies, and functional aspects of HRM in international settings, students gain insights into global workforce dynamics, labour regulations, and the complexities of managing across national systems.
learning_outcomes: Apply the context of the international business setting to develop a critical understanding of human resource management across different institutional boundaries.

Critically assess and evaluate the complexities of managing human resources within international businesses and their implications for managers, workers and wider society in the global economy and the ethical implications of such approaches.
Reflect critically on theoretical and practice-based principles about the relationship between national and transnational institutions, and the implications of this for the management of people.
Demonstrate skills in self-management, problem solving, written communication when applying an international perspective to the management of people.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Project Procurement and Resourcing
overview: This course aims to develop student understanding in respect to making best use of internal and external resources on project-based endeavours. It will cover recognised principles in respect to sourcing goods and services as well as appropriate personnel for projects. Topics will include procurement practice and planning, delivery models, documentation, tendering and source selection, contract administration, human resources management, team planning, recruitment and development.
learning_outcomes: Explain procurement concepts in relation to projects
Analyse procurement strategies and apply to various projects
Describe and explain human resourcing in respect to the project team
Illustrate how to effectively apply resource management to projects
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Leadership in Stakeholder Management
overview: This course studies the nexus between project leadership and stakeholder management. It introduces students to leadership concepts, behaviours and traits in the project context. It also looks at stakeholder theory and concepts, defines internal/external stakeholders and highlights the importance of effective communications. It brings these areas together in respect to leading teams, project culture, problem solving, decision making, negotiation and conflict resolution in the project environment. The course also covers the concept of emotional intelligence in respect to leadership and stakeholders.
learning_outcomes: Describe concepts of leadership in project management
Evaluate the various ways to lead project teams
Describe concepts within stakeholder management
Outline stakeholder types and appropriate communication techniques
Explain engagement, governance and competencies in the delivery of projects
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Service Design and Marketing
overview: This course aims to equip learners with the knowledge and skills to integrate key service elements into service design in ways that create value for customers and sustain service excellence. The course builds on learners’ understanding of the marketing mix by introducing the additional elements that marketers must consider when effectively marketing services to buyers, including the effective design and management of people, processes and physical evidence. This course aligns with the program’s purpose of providing industry-relevant, contemporary teaching, especially considering the increasing prominence of service industries in global economies.
learning_outcomes: Identify and explain core services marketing theories and concepts, and leverage them to understanding customer experience in services

Apply services marketing research and course learnings to develop insights for customer engagement throughout the customer journey (purchasing, accessing, or using services, and including barriers to access)
Evaluate and identify service shortcomings and provide recommendations for service managers to deliver high-quality service offerings
Identify and discuss characteristics and challenges of managing service firms in the modern world including social and cultural implications
antirequisites: N/A

title: Training and Development
overview: To equip students with the knowledge and skills to analyse, design, and evaluate strategically aligned training and development initiatives that enhance workforce capability, support employee and leadership development, address contemporary learning needs, and develop a learning culture in diverse organisations through evidence-based, inclusive, and technology-enabled approaches.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate how training and development contributes to organisational strategy, workforce capability, employee & leadership development, and learning culture supported by reasoning that integrates relevant case facts, course concepts, and appropriate references, and maintains internal cohesion across the submission.

Interpret workplace and evaluation data using structured analysis methods, and use insights to recommend and justify strategically aligned, evidence-based learning interventions supported by explanation that integrates relevant, accurately cited case facts, course concepts, and academic sources, and maintains internal cohesion throughout the submission.

Design effective, evidence-based, context-specific workplace learning by applying instructional design and transfer principles, and adult learning, motivation, and behavioural change theories taught in this course, supported by explanation that integrates relevant, accurately cited case facts, course concepts, and academic sources, and maintains internal cohesion throughout the submission.

Select contextually appropriate workplace learning delivery methods and technologies, supported by explanation that integrates relevant, accurately cited case facts, course concepts, and academic sources, and maintains internal cohesion throughout the submission.

Assess the impact of workplace learning initiatives using evaluation frameworks taught in this course and contextual evidence. Apply findings to enhance organisational goals, workforce capability and development, and learning culture supported by explanation that integrates relevant, accurately cited case facts, course concepts, and academic sources, and maintains internal cohesion throughout the submission.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Learning Journal, Case Study, Design Project – 40%

title: Performance and Compensation Management
overview: This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to design, implement, and evaluate performance management (PM) and compensation management (CM) systems that support organisational strategy and effectiveness. Students will examine and evaluate key appraisal methods, performance alignment practices, and rewards systems, and apply relevant theories to analyse real-world PM and CM challenges. The course emphasises strategic integration, equity, and effectiveness in performance & compensation decisions.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and apply performance appraisal (PA) methods that align with organisational goals, identify appropriate performance dimensions, and develop measurable goals (KPIs) to support effective performance.
Analyse and compare efficacy of traditional pay systems and performance-based pay models.
Critically assess compensation system issues and recommend strategically aligned rewards that ensure internal equity and market competitiveness.
Apply relevant theoretical frameworks to analyse and interpret performance and compensation challenges in contemporary organisations.
Integrate performance and compensation strategies to support strategic alignment and enhance organisational effectiveness.
prerequisites: must have completed HRES1000 Foundations of Human Resource Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Employment Law
overview: This course develops students knowledge of the impact of laws regulating workers and their workplaces in the Australian context. The major areas of employment law include the common law and statute law. There are many 'sources' of employment law, which set out the rights and obligations of employees and their employer. An employer in Australia has many obligations arising mostly from federal law but also from state law and the common law. This course investigates these laws in terms of, inter alia, employer-employee duties, termination of employment, workplace bargaining and industrial action. Students will identify employment law issues as well as provide analyses and recommendations to solve workplace problems. Students are assessed through problem-solving exercises.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate between the creation of different types of workplace relationships.
Identify how Australia's workplace relations framework creates a variety of rights and obligations at work.
Interpret and apply legal obligations surrounding termination of employment.
Analyse the impact of employment obligations upon employers, including work health and safety, workers compensation, equality of opportunity/discrimination and adverse action legislation.
Develop lawful and ethical recommendations for effective management strategies relating to aspects of employment law.
Assess legal requirements to ensure lawful enterprise bargaining processes and lawful industrial action.
prerequisites: must have completed all of BUSI1001 Business Law/HRES1000 Foundations of Human Resource Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Recruitment and Selection
overview: This course provides students with an understanding of the current theory, processes and practices of recruitment and selection in organisations, equipping them with a working knowledge of the recruitment and selection literature and providing opportunities to develop and practice relevant recruitment and selection skills. For many HR generalists, recruitment and selection is a big part of their day-to-day work. For many CEOs, finding the right people is crucial to organisational success. This course is aimed at developing essential knowledge needed for professional practice. In this course, emphasis is placed on understanding the decisions that practitioners need to make when recruiting and selecting so that students can choose the right approach for the situation they are in. Students are assessed through a critical analysis and project.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine recruitment and selection strategies and workforce planning with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis and project
Plan and conduct a job analysis to develop a job description with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis and project

Critically evaluate internal and external methods of recruitment and selection, recognising social, legal, ethical and business issues and changing workforce demographics and technology with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis and project

Plan, manage, implement and evaluate appropriate recruitment and selection strategies for an organisation with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis and project

Develop practical skills in developing selection criteria, evaluating resumes, conduct of structured interviews, assessing candidates, making final hiring decisions and evaluating organisational effectiveness of recruitment and selection systems with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis and project

Demonstrate skills in self-management, problem solving and written communication with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis and project
prerequisites: must have completed HRES1000 Foundations of Human Resource Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Strategic Human Resource Management
overview: This course develops students knowledge about the central themes and diverse views within strategic human resource management (HRM) and skills in identifying appropriate strategic HRM responses to organisational challenges. Many organisations are undertaking all sorts of changes that require the adoption of new work practices and new approaches to decision-making and performance management. HR people have been leaders in identifying the organisation's particular challenges and in finding and implementing solutions. Some organisations are struggling to find sufficient employees. This course is concerned with broader questions, such as: what sort of training and development do we want What skills are we looking for Students are assessed through an essay, a presentation and report.
learning_outcomes: Apply operational HR techniques towards the achievement of organisational HR and business strategic goals with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report

Apply concepts and recent innovations in HR theory and practice towards the achievement of organisational goals with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report

Analyse an organisation's business and HR environmental context with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report

Evaluate an organisation's HR-business integration and the sophistication of its HR system with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report

Evaluate the organisation's internal, external and environmental fit with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report

Create an appropriate set of HR strategies and practices that enable the organisation to fully implement its business strategy with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report

Demonstrate skills in self-management, problem solving and written communication with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in an essay, a presentation and report
prerequisites: must have completed HRES1000 Foundations of Human Resource Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: HR Analytics
overview: This course aims to provide a preliminary introduction to the use of analytics in the context of human resource management in organisations. The use of analytics-based tools for identifying commonly encountered HR issues and basic statistical analyses to evaluate information are introduced along with ethical issues and future trends associated with HR analytics. HR Analytics approaches are increasingly significant in the current business context, and being data savvy is an important skillset for todays HR professionals. This course also highlights the ethical aspects of HR Analytics. Students are assessed through case study and data analysis.
learning_outcomes: Examine and evaluate the role of analytics in the context of Human Resource Management in organisations with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a case study and data analysis
Apply analytics-based tools for analysing HR data with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a case study and data analysis

Analyse and evaluate basic statistical tools for identifying common HR issues encountered in organisations with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a case study and data analysis

Design processes to create awareness of ethical considerations associated with data analytics related to people with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a case study and data analysis
Demonstrate skills in problem solving and ethical awareness with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a case study and data analysis
prerequisites: must have completed BUSI2001 Emerging Technologies, Data and Business Analytics
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Data Collection and/or Analysis – 50%

title: Design Thinking: Problems to Practice
overview: In this highly interactive course, students will develop a working knowledge of the design thinking methodology and numerous supporting frameworks, tools and techniques by applying human-centred processes to dissect project ideas into component parts, to redefine problems, generate ideas, and prioritise those ideas to develop and test a prototype to achieve optimal innovative solutions. Students will then assess steps to implement the solution through change management principles, and consider ways to monitor the anticipated impact achieved or whether further iteration is required. Working manually through these processes will help students to develop the skills to critically think through complex problems and conceive numerous innovative options as solutions.
learning_outcomes: Interpret and explain design thinking theories, concepts and processes.
Identify and analyse the relationship between design thinking, innovation and entrepreneurship and the value of innovation to organisations, economies and society.
Identify and evaluate core elements of the human-centred design methodology.
Justify effective team collaboration through use of conflict resolution strategies.
Identify and apply ethical and sustainable principles across the design process.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Innovation and Creativity
overview: This course introduces principles and practices of entrepreneurial creativity and innovation in various settings. Students will learn to implement creative processes for the development of innovation activities to solve problems in organisations and other contexts in relation to entrepreneurship. The course covers creativity at the individual, team and organisational levels, creativity in the context of entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation to address societal issues, barriers to creativity and innovation, building the creative environment and innovation capability in the organisation, and managing creativity and innovation in the organisation for growth and success.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate principles, models, approaches, and processes that support creativity and innovation in individuals, teams, and organisations.
Reflect on different aspects of creativity and innovation development and management in the organisational setting
Apply creativity tools to create innovative outcomes for relevant problems
Design processes to encourage creativity and innovation development beneficial to the organisation and society
Demonstrate innovative problem solving and communication skills
antirequisites: N/A

title: Creating New Ventures
overview: This course aims to equip students with the knowledge, skills, and analytical tools essential for navigating the process involved in initiating a new business venture. Through a systematic and iterative approach to idea generation and refinement, students will gain an understanding of entrepreneurship, learning to identify opportunities by actively engaging with customers, conducting thorough market and competitive analyses, crafting compelling value propositions, designing business models, and strategically formulating plans to acquire the necessary resources for sustainable growth and success.
learning_outcomes: Define the process and elements of launching a new venture
Recognise potential business opportunities
Conduct feasibility studies to evaluate business opportunities
Develop and present business plans to explore identified opportunities
Collaborate effectively in a team, demonstrating communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills
antirequisites: N/A

title: Enterprise Design and Value Creation
overview: The aim of this course is to guide students through the various strategic decisions necessary to design an enterprise model from abstract information and conceptual ideas for a proposed venture. Using frameworks for strategic growth decisions, value creation and business model design, students will confront the tensions and paradox in enterprise design and learn how to reconcile the entrepreneurial drive with the competitive business landscape. Further consideration will be given to how development and growth of an enterprise influences changes to the business model design affecting the value structure, resources, capabilities, and management challenges.
learning_outcomes: Relate the strategy and value creation processes to the context of enterprise design decisions.
Analyse and reconcile an enterprise's customer `value' offering with its operational value creating logic.
Identify and articulate the resources and capabilities that define and support a new venture's strategic positioning.
Identify and articulate the resources and capabilities that define and support a new venture's strategic positioning.
Appraise the risks to an enterprise design's value structure, resources, capabilities, and management imposed by growth.

Demonstrate Business Enterprise Skills: i) Problem Solving (advanced level); ii) Ethical Awareness (advanced level); iii) Teamwork (advanced level); iv) Written Communication (advanced level); v) Oral Communication (advanced level); and vi) International Perspective (advanced level)
antirequisites: N/A

title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
overview: As modern organisations increasingly demand entrepreneurial skills from their workforce, this course serves as a catalyst for enhancing students' understanding of how entrepreneurship creates and maintains competitive advantage. Through the exploration of theories and models of corporate entrepreneurship, knowledge from this course will equip students with the necessary mindset to innovate, grow, adapt, and thrive in dynamic corporate environments.
learning_outcomes: Define corporate entrepreneurship and its role in achieving competitive advantage.
Articulate the challenges and opportunities for large organisations in developing an entrepreneurial mindset.
Determine the key architecture required to support an entrepreneurial organisation.
Develop entrepreneurial behaviours and activities that align with innovation.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Technology Entrepreneurship
overview: This course explores the critical role of technologies in entrepreneurship, providing insights into online and technology-driven business creation, career navigation amid technological disruption, and strategies for leveraging digital tools for innovation, growth, and scaling.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the process of innovation and industry disruption
Determine the elements of technology innovation
Categorise different digital business models
Describe alternative technology growth strategies
Choose and articulate strategies for maintaining team relationships that facilitate flexibility, collaboration and quick decision making
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sustainability and Social Enterprise
overview: This course explores different social enterprise models and evaluates them in context of the local/global social and sustainability challenges they aim to address. The course aims to provide a valuable foundation for planning a career pathway in sustainability and social entrepreneurship through understanding what social enterprise is and its relation to sustainable development and social impact, and learning how to measure social impact, including pathways to create change through a startup venture, supporting social entrepreneurs in creative ways, or serving as a director of a board. From the public, private or not-for-profit sector, students will identify and develop a social enterprise opportunity that provides potential to scale.
learning_outcomes: Compare and contrast different approaches to social entrepreneurship and their effectiveness in addressing social and environmental challenges.
Develop sustainable business models for social enterprises that integrate principles of sustainability and circular economy.
Evaluate and measure the social and environmental impact of social enterprise activities using appropriate tools and methodologies.
Formulate theories of change and strategic plans for scaling social impact in social enterprises.
Conduct environmental impact assessments for social enterprise projects and propose mitigation strategies.
Analyse the challenges and opportunities in implementing sustainable development goals (SDGs) within social enterprise contexts.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance, Performance – 10%

title: Innovation Strategy and Systems
overview: This course provides a deep look at the concept of innovation strategy, exploring history, theory and modern tools of innovation strategy not commonly known. This course also covers the innovation system from an entrepreneurial eco-system perspective. Completing this course will help students better recognise the role of innovation, as well as offer powerful concepts to help embed an innovation process with students' venture or organisation, or influence the development of entrepreneurial eco-systems.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of a concept of innovation strategy, including its theoretical development, application and significance for innovation systems and organisational success
Recommend an innovation strategy for a new, emerging, or existing organisation considering its innovation capability, obstacles, and opportunities

Develop an innovation strategy evaluation plan for a new, emerging or existing organisation to measure the effectiveness of innovation efforts applying appropriate metrics and evaluation methods of ethics and sustainability

Examine the dynamics of entrepreneurial ecosystems and their influence on regional development or sectoral innovation strategy, analysing the roles of government policies, venture capital, support networks, and other stakeholders in fostering a conducive environment for innovation and entrepreneurship
antirequisites: N/A

title: AI for Business transformation
overview: This course equips first and second-year business students with practical AI skills and critical thinking capabilities essential for the modern business landscape. Students will progress from mastering personal AI tools to designing AI-powered business solutions, with a strong focus on hands-on experimentation and entrepreneurial application. Through collaborative workshops, real-world case studies, and reflective practice, students will develop the ability to leverage AI effectively while critically evaluating its ethical, social, and economic implications. The course emphasizes learning to work WITH AI as a collaborative partner, preparing students to create innovative business solutions in an AI-transformed economy.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in collaborating with AI tools across multiple modalities to enhance personal and professional productivity.
Analyse and evaluate AI implementation approaches across different organisational contexts.
Design and pitch an AI-powered business solution applying entrepreneurial best practices.
Critically assess the societal, ethical, and economic implications of AI adoption in business contexts.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Family Business Management
overview: Family businesses contribute significantly to economies and communities but face distinctive opportunities and challenges that set them apart from other firms. This course introduces students to their unique characteristics and complexities while developing analytical and problem-solving skills to address them. Through real-world case studies, students will engage with relevant theories and frameworks to explore family dynamics, governance, succession planning, entrepreneurship, and sustainability. The course also develops teamwork and communication skills essential for professional effectiveness. By combining conceptual knowledge with applied learning, students gain the confidence to contribute meaningfully to family businesses as future leaders, advisors, or professionals.
learning_outcomes: Utilise relevant theories and frameworks to explain the uniqueness of family firms.
Apply relevant theories and frameworks to analyse complex family business issues.
Develop strategies for fostering leadership, entrepreneurship, and sustainability within the family business.
Apply the interpersonal skills and processes required to work effectively in a team environment.
Communicate ideas, analyses and findings to an audience appropriately, persuasively and succinctly.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Tech eChallenge
overview: The Tech eChallenge embraces technology innovation and with the emphasis on product or service design leveraging technology. The development of a prototype that has market relevance for different streams including not limited to MedTech, AgTech, EdTech and FinTech. Receiving instruction and guidance from experienced mentors, underpinned by theory, students develop prototypes that address a market need and then present these to a panel of judges where they receive feedback about their innovations.
learning_outcomes: Identify a potential entrepreneurial opportunity by applying the Jobs to Be Done framework to systematically uncover an unmet need in the market
Develop a Prototype to satisfy the market needs leveraging enabling technologies
Build an effective entrepreneurial team to develop strategies to exploit the entrepreneurial opportunity
Communicate and present the new entrepreneurial venture to relevant stakeholders including investors
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Across Cultures
overview: The aim of this course is to provide students with a basic understanding of the fundamental principles and practices of International Management. The course focuses on the foundations of international management, the role of culture, cross-cultural communication and negotiations, MNC strategies and structures, and international human resource management. There will be a focus on appropriate theory and the course will aim to provide opportunities for the practical implementation of the main concepts covered.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the drivers and consequences (political, economic, socio-cultural, technological, legal and ecological) of globalization, its impact on specific regions and the emerging concerns about its influences on countries around the world

Understand and appreciate the need for ethics and social responsibility in international management, and the growing pressures on firms to act in an ethically and socially responsible manner in their global business operations

Compare different theoretical approaches to the concept of culture (at national, regional and organisational levels) and implications of these differences for international and cross-cultural managers
Apply theories of culture and management to address the challenges of managing individuals, groups and organisations in an increasingly diverse global context

Integrate and apply the basic elements of international strategic management, including the pressures and cost/benefits of strategies that emphasise global integration versus local adaptation; evaluate the specialised strategies required for emerging economies and for international new ventures
Compare and evaluate practices related to the management, motivation and leading of employees in an international and cross-cultural context
antirequisites: N/A

title: International Business Operations
overview: This course aims to equip learners with the knowledge and skills necessary to analyse and effectively manage the international operations of multinational firms. This course focuses on the internal functions of multinational firms that shape their strategies and behaviour. This exploration lays the foundation for decision-making and management tools essential for operating in a dynamic international business environment. By examining the functions of multinational entities, learners will cultivate critical thinking and problem-solving skills crucial for developing impactful international business strategies. Moreover, this course aligns with the program's objective of fostering a comprehensive understanding of key areas in International Business. Ultimately, it aims to cultivate innovative, ethical, and sustainable solutions within the global market, preparing learners to excel in their international business endeavours.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical concepts and analytical tools to analyse cross-border business operations
Identify opportunities and risks entailed in various internationalisation decisions
Appreciate and explain the complexity of international business operations
Communicate analytical findings in relation to international business operations of a firm
antirequisites: N/A

title: International Business in the Asia-Pacific
overview: The aim of this course is to explore the diverse aspects of conducting business in the Asia-Pacific region, emphasising an exploration of its unique environmental factors, regional trade agreements, risk assessment methodologies, governmental regulations and policies, technological innovations, and supply chain networks. By scrutinising entry modes specific to the Asia-Pacific context, the course aims to equip students with the requisite knowledge and skills to navigate this diverse regional market environment effectively. Furthermore, the course aims to foster an entrepreneurial mindset among students, empowering them to identify and capitalise on opportunities within emerging Asia-Pacific markets, thereby preparing them for roles in the region or entrepreneurial endeavours.
learning_outcomes: Develop an in-depth understanding of the business, economic, and management landscape specific to the Asia-Pacific region, including macro and micro-level factors influencing organisations operating in this dynamic environment

Analyse and evaluate the strategic approaches and business practices of both Asian and Western enterprises operating in the Asia-Pacific region, identifying similarities, differences, and implications for organisational success

Apply cross-cultural business models and concepts specifically within the Asia-Pacific context to analyse and address real-world scenarios, and case studies, showcasing proficiency in navigating the diverse cultural landscapes of the region and tailoring business strategies accordingly

Demonstrate effective communication skills in a global business environment, along with other key attributes sought by employers such as teamwork, planning, self-management, initiative, and a commitment to continuous professional development, preparing graduates for successful careers in Asia-Pacific-focused organisations
prerequisites: must have completed all of IBUS2000 International Business Environment/IBUS2001 International Business Operations
antirequisites: N/A

title: Internationalisation of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises
overview: This course explores the opportunities and challenges faced by small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in today's globalised and technologically driven business environment. Participants will gain the knowledge and skills needed to navigate international markets effectively, exploring strategies for success, factors influencing performance, and risks inherent in global expansion for small and medium-sized enterprises. Emphasis is placed on understanding the impact of mindset on internationalisation decisions. Contemporary approaches like social entrepreneurship and digital business models are also examined, offering a comprehensive understanding of modern small and medium-sized enterprise internationalisation practices. The course aims to equip participants with insights to thrive in the ever-evolving global business environment.
learning_outcomes: Describe the economic importance and the need for SME internationalisation in today’s globalised environment
Identify and analyse the micro-foundation of SME internationalisation including attitudes, mindsets and cognitive approaches associated with exploring international opportunities
Evaluate the social, political, economic, cultural and ethical challenges of the internationalisation process, and design appropriate responses to overcome these challenges
Devise strategies for SMEs to acquire knowledge, partnerships, and networks for creating value internationally
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Ethics and Values in the International Context
overview: This course examines international issues in ethics and values and equips students with the skills and capabilities needed to make informed ethical decisions to assist organisations to embed ethical practice throughout all levels of organisational strategy and business conduct, including opportunities to address challenges relating to the SDGs.
learning_outcomes: Develop skills and capabilities to make informed ethical decisions, both personally and professionally in the business management context
Critically analyse and apply ethical practice to all levels of organisational strategy
Gain practical skills to assist organisations to become more ethical in their conduct
Apply principles of sustainability and sustainable living to business management in the context of international business
antirequisites: N/A

title: Contemporary Issues in International Business
overview: The aim of this course is to explore current challenges and trends shaping the global business landscape, emphasising their impact on multinational enterprises and strategies for navigating complex international environments. Students will develop nuanced understandings of a range of contemporary issues and debates in international business, and develop the skills and knowledge that will enable them to keep abreast of the rapid changes and developments in the global marketplace. The topics covered in the course will provide in-depth understanding of the political, economic, social and other contextual factors that influence the operations of businesses (from small-scale entrepreneurial ventures to multinational enterprises (MNEs)).
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a critical understanding of the drivers and consequences of international business
Identify and understand links between international business and contemporary political and economic structures
Apply international business concepts and theories
Critically evaluate contemporary debates about international business
antirequisites: N/A

title: Triple Bottom Line and Innovation
overview: The aim of this course is to develop students' understanding of the relationship between society, business, government, and the not-for-profit sector. It will enable students to identify a range of professional capabilities necessary for participation in a sustainable society. It provides the skills to think through complexity, transcend paradigms, learn through dialogue and communication, engage in deep reflection, develop worldview and values sensitivity, and assess when activities support or detract from achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
learning_outcomes: Identify ethical issues in business, government, not-for-profits and society
Describe different perspectives of the role of business in society
Analyse how these different perspectives impact on the duties and responsibilities of business, including responsibilities towards Indigenous peoples
Identify the features of their intended profession and professional life in the community from the perspective of a responsible manager
Relate the importance and relevant features of the United Nations Sustainable Development goals to business and society
antirequisites: N/A

title: Organisational Behaviour
overview: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of organisational behaviour theories, focusing on how personality and perception and group attributes shape organisational culture, ethics, and structure. By integrating historical insights with contemporary approaches, students will engage in experiential learning activities to develop skills in determining costs and benefits of teams and decision-making as well as applying various models of motivation. Students will evaluate the forces and methods associated with organisational change, preparing them for real-world challenges. Aligned with broader program objectives, students are equipped with essential knowledge and skills contributing effectively to diverse workplace settings and promote their overall professional development.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate an organisation utilising specific organisational behaviour theories and frameworks to inform recommendations for improvement
Apply relevant contemporary theories, concepts, and models to real-world scenarios, case studies and issues
Synthesise peer-reviewed research relevant to real-world business scenarios
Collaborate within a diverse team to contribute constructively to analyses and decision making
Communicate in oral format as appropriate for an industry relevant audience
