Analyse the impact of cultural diversity on organisational behaviour, considering international perspectives and their relevance in global management contexts
antirequisites: N/A

title: Applied Creativity for Business
overview: The aim of this course is to develop an understanding of the application of creative thinking methodologies and ideation, artificial intelligence and creativity, and the evaluation of creative ideas and decisions for value, to embed a culture of creativity in the organisation.
learning_outcomes: Understand ideation, creativity and applied creativity and their differences and implications to the organisation
Understand and apply creative process and creative thinking techniques and tools for organisational development
Understand the importance of creativity and creative leadership as business requirements, practices and skills for innovation development
Integrate various creating thinking approaches for project planning, collecting and managing ideas for problem solving and innovative solutions
Demonstrate communicative skills and application of technology that enhance creativity and its applications in different organisational settings
antirequisites: N/A

title: Organisational Leadership
overview: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of conventional and alternative perspectives on leadership and explores its practice in various business contexts. The course develops awareness of the different aspects of leadership, including leadership and leading changes, traits, behaviours, and relationships, leader personality and emotions, followership, motivation and empowerment, leading teams, and power and social Influence. Students will gain insights into building relationships, and developing, and implementing strategies to support the organisation and their followers to achieve their objectives. Students will develop critical thinking skills to assess and reflect on their leadership potential and formulate strategies for developing their leadership styles, aligning with program objectives.
learning_outcomes: Examine essential leadership principles and skills across diverse organisational contexts.
Apply organisational leadership theories and concepts to critically analyse organisational issues.
Analyse how leadership influences organisational outcomes, including performance and employee behaviour.
Reflect on and evaluate your leadership potential and identity.
Communicate effectively to prepare reports and analyses of organisational leadership in real-world business contexts.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Consumer Behaviour
overview: This course will cover fundamental knowledge about human behaviour and how this relates to buying behaviour. Students will gain an understanding of evidence-based theories to explain and predict consumer behaviour. Students will learn about well-established descriptive knowledge on patterns in buying behaviour that generalise over known conditions and how this fundamental knowledge can be applied to inform marketing decisions. Psychological, social, cultural and individual factors will also be investigated and how these influence buying behaviour.
learning_outcomes: Describe key aspects of consumer behaviour and market segmentation
Describe the complexities of consumer decision making processes
Demonstrate how well-established descriptive knowledge of consumer behaviour can be applied to marketing
Assess the value of scientific investigation of consumer behaviour issues
Display critical thinking and problem-solving skills
In a team, work effectively to address consumer behaviour issues within a specific context
corequisites: Must be enrolled in 1 of MARK1000 Marketing Principles/MARK1008 Introduction to Marketing
antirequisites: N/A

title: Marketing Analytics
overview: To provide students with the theoretical and operational tools of marketing analytics for decision making. Students will explore the intricacies of marketing analytics. They will develop the skills and knowledge needed to extract meaningful insights from data and drive effective data-driven strategies.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the knowledge and applications of analytical tools to various data sources in marketing
Communicate the results of marketing analytics to managers
Demonstrate an understanding of patterns of how businesses grow across different industries and countries using empirical data
Explain and illustrate how marketing analytics are used in an integrated manner to solve marketing problems
prerequisites: must have completed MARK1000 Marketing Principles
antirequisites: N/A

title: Advertising
overview: This course aims to prepare students to be questioning buyers and knowledgeable managers of advertising, from the advertiser’s perspective and/or to sell and manage such services from an agency perspective. Students will gain an understanding of the role of advertising across history and within contemporary society. Students will acquire skills and knowledge in working with media to develop campaigns, including campaign planning, media liaison, media planning and buying, campaign evaluation, and creative considerations.
learning_outcomes: Explain the structure of the advertising industry, including the roles and relationships of key players, such as agencies, media outlets, and creative professionals
Apply relevant advertising theories and concepts to evaluate and analyse advertisements
Identify and evaluate evidence-based information to formulate appropriate advertising recommendations, including objectives, strategies, plans and budgets
Develop skills in media and creative strategy by examining the different tools, options and approaches used by advertisers
Apply evidence-based advertising strategies using specific metrics and tactics to achieve measurable campaign objectives
prerequisites: must have completed MARK1000 Marketing Principles
antirequisites: N/A

title: Branding
overview: This course shall equip students with foundational knowledge of contemporary branding practices and to enhance their ability to understand various brand management strategies. Students will learn about how consumers process, store, and retrieve brand-related information. They will develop a clear understanding of the key brand performance metrics and benchmarks for your brand and come to understand how brands compete.
learning_outcomes: Examine marketing knowledge from the perspective of brand management
Compare the quality of evidence available to support branding theories

Identify brand marketing challenges and use of situation-specific evidence such as ethics, sustainability and cultural diversity, and factual data to make recommendations of how to grow a brand, including issues
In the context of the Marketing discipline, demonstrate business acumen, and skills in problem solving and communication
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of MARK1001 Consumer Behaviour/MARK5000 Marketing
antirequisites: N/A

title: Digital Marketing
overview: To develop students understanding of digital marketing, the course delves into marketing activities across the Internet and advanced platforms, contrasting them with traditional methods. It covers developing digital marketing strategies, encompassing web technologies, mobile, and online advertising, with reference to social media and influencer marketing. Additionally, it explores the execution and evaluation of strategies, leveraging technologies like digital analytics and AI. Legal frameworks are also discussed, emphasising privacy, data management, and cybersecurity, ensuring students are well-versed in navigating the complexities of the digital landscape.
learning_outcomes: Describe a range of digital marketing tools and strategies to improve business performance
Compare and contrast marketing and consumer behaviour in traditional (offline) versus digital contexts
Recommend and justify tools to formulate an appropriate digital media strategy
Analyse social and ethical issues in globalised electronic markets
Identify and critically examine emerging trends in digital marketing
antirequisites: N/A

title: Marketing Planning
overview: The course aims to develop students ability to identify and analyse strategic marketing issues, and to develop strategies to address marketing problems and capitalise on opportunities. The course builds on students previous understanding of a range of core marketing concepts and aims to support the synthesis of this understanding as they learn the processes involved in the development of marketing plans. The course builds students skills in critical- and creative-thinking in strategic contexts, both of which are becoming increasingly demanded in industry.
learning_outcomes: Describe the components of a marketing plan
Analyse data in order to develop informed strategies as part of a marketing plan
Apply marketing planning principles and frameworks to develop a marketing plan
Identify appropriate strategic courses of action for an organisation, along with the advantages and disadvantages of different strategies
Contribute to strategic thinking and decision making within an organisation
Solve marketing strategy problems
prerequisites: must have completed all of MARK1000 Marketing Principles/MARK1001 Consumer Behaviour
antirequisites: N/A

title: Social Media Audiences and Algorithmic Cultures
overview: As an introductory course for the major, Social Media Audiences and Algorithmic Cultures explores social media platforms from a historical, technological and social perspective, considering influence, capabilities, use, and possible futures. The course draws upon overlapping concepts and theory from media studies, sociology, psychology and computer science to understand audience behaviour, content and platform technologies. Students will develop skills in critically analysing digital content, the online presence of social actors, and broader cultural trends on social media. These knowledges and skills will help students become effective content experts and researchers of social media and its audiences.
learning_outcomes: Articulate how social media platforms and campaigns impact politics, activism, culture and communities
Critically evaluate social media practice as it relates to ethical action and social responsibility as a professional and citizen
Evaluate the use of social media and strategic communication for political and social issue campaigning purposes, applying logical, critical, and creative thinking
Demonstrate skills in using social media as a resource for learning and in practice
antirequisites: N/A

title: Introduction to Strategic Communication
overview: Introduction to Strategic Communication is a foundational course, introducing students to strategic communication and public relations theories. This course applies these theories to a range of professional contexts and sectors, providing foundational knowledge for courses throughout the Strategic Communication major or as an elective complementing other specialisations. In this course, students will learn how to communicate effectively using theories of public relations and strategic communication. Students will apply these theories in a range of professional communication contexts including organisational communication, promotional communication, and political and social movement communication.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of key communication and public relations theories and understanding of their application in strategic communication
Develop strategic communication for use in corporate, promotional, and political and social movement contexts
Demonstrate understanding of how different media are used in strategic communication, including paid, earned, owned and shared media.
Create strategic communication to help organisations reach their communication objectives using a range of media platforms.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Digital and Social Media Management
overview: The course will focus on strategic communication and promotional branding through digital and social media content. Students will gain both theoretical knowledge and practical skills, enabling them to develop expertise of digital and social media platforms and implement effective content strategies. The learning experience is enhanced by authentic assessments within the curriculum, which provide opportunities for students to develop professional and leadership skills relevant to various industries and contexts in digital and social media platforms. Students will deepen their understanding of branding and reputation management as it relates to digital and social media in strategic communication across diverse industries.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the role of digital and social media platforms in communication strategies across various industries.
Apply theoretical knowledge to analyse digital and social media practices to develop effective communication strategies.
Create and implement digital and social media content strategies to improve audience engagement.
Analyse and evaluate digital and social media content in the context of professional standards to enhance strategic communication
antirequisites: N/A

title: Creating Content for Media
overview: This course develops theoretical and practical skills in content creation for various media platforms.
learning_outcomes: Explain the principles of content creation and its role in contemporary society
Understand content creation as a media and communication strategy, and its different applications
Plan and produce content for a range of platforms
Demonstrate introductory technical and production skills relevant to content creation
antirequisites: N/A

title: Thinking By Design
overview: Design involves a range of different intelligences and approaches to thinking. This course explored creative thinking methods, alongside inclusive and empathic approaches with hands-on design skills used across design disciplines. It will introduce philosophical, historical, and ideological approaches to reflective and creative thinking in the design process. This will require students to reflect on their approaches to creative thinking and approaches to real world complexity, incorporating their own disciplinary practices into their own approach to the design process.
learning_outcomes: Develop an awareness of reframing design problems for creative practice
Apply creative thinking, methods, and processes in resolving a range of design problems
Evaluate theories and ideas about thinking for design practice
Incorporate individual approaches to documenting and expressing thought
Demonstrate idea generation methods in relation to design practices
Demonstrate the ability to articulate thinking processes and approaches
antirequisites: N/A

title: Principles of UX Design
overview: This course aims to provide a comprehensive introduction to user experience design (UXD) theories, methodologies, tools, and applications. Through a combination of theoretical concepts, practical exercises, and real-world case studies, students will develop a deep understanding of UXD principles and be equipped to apply them effectively in other courses and their design practice.
learning_outcomes: Identify the theoretical underpinnings of UX design, including core principles, prevailing best practices and challenges in UX design
Apply various user research techniques to gather insights into user needs, behaviours, and preferences.
Synthesise research findings to inform the design process and develop solutions that cater to diverse user groups effectively.
Utilise industry-standard tools to create interactive prototypes focusing on usability, accessibility, and intuitive user experience.
Adapt and integrate UXD methodologies, tools, and applications to address specific design challenges and project requirements
Work independently and collaboratively as part of a team to meet project challenges and requirements
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of COGR1001 Introduction to Immersive Media Technologies/GRAP1004 Digital Design Principles and Methods
antirequisites: N/A

title: Market Research and Customer Insights
overview: To provide students with an understanding of the essential role of market research in providing accurate and useful information upon which to base business decision-making, how market research is carried out, and the different sorts of market research data commonly encountered.
learning_outcomes: Describe various market research methods and their practical applications
Analyse the strengths and limitations of various market research methods and data sources and reports.
Prepare a brief for a market research agency
Interpret data or information to derive useful customer insights
Analyse ethical and international issues pertaining to market research and their impact on research practices
prerequisites: must have completed MARK1000 Marketing Principles
antirequisites: N/A

title: Distribution and Route to Market
overview: The aim of the course is to provide students with a theoretically grounded and evidence-based understanding of how retailers, manufacturers and service providers manage physical availability across traditional and emerging distribution channels. Students will develop an understanding of the role of distribution and physical availability in business environments; the different types of distribution channels and how consumers shop across these channels; managerial decisions about physical availability and the factors that influence these decisions, and emerging trends in managing physical availability.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and substantiate the role of distribution and physical availability in business environments.
Evaluate types of distribution channels and analyse how consumers shop across these channels.
Analyse consumer behaviour and interrogate the factors influencing decision-making at the point-of-sale across in-store/dealership/showroom contexts.
Evaluate and justify managerial decisions related to physical availability, including the dynamics of producers- distributors–retailers' relationships and the impact of channel conflict.
Critically review and extrapolate insights from evolving trends in physical availability.
Reflect on personal and professional learning, demonstrating critical thinking and awareness of the application of course concepts in real-world and collaborative contexts.
prerequisites: must have completed MARK1000 Marketing Principles
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Services
overview: This course is designed to enable students to understand the nature of services and service management, service concepts and the design of service delivery systems, the role of technology in services, the role of facilities management in designing the service experience, managing demand and capacity in services, service quality and performance systems, innovation strategies for services and globalisation of services.
learning_outcomes: Apply the principles and concepts for managing service-based operations in today's economy.
Examine process, employee and customer orientations of service delivery.
Evaluate the roles of people, technology and the servicescape as they relate to organisations.
Effectively communicate the strategies for effective and efficient service delivery.
Work autonomously and collaboratively in deriving service management solutions for organisations.
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, ethical awareness and written communication.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion – 10%

title: Supply Chain Intelligence and Analytics
overview: This course provides students with the essential knowledge and skills needed to leverage cutting-edge analytical tools and techniques in order to optimise and enhance the efficiency, visibility, and resilience of supply chain operations. Through a comprehensive exploration of key concepts, industry best practices, and hands-on application of analytics tools, students will gain the expertise necessary to make informed decisions, mitigate risks, and drive strategic improvements across the entire supply chain ecosystem. In this course, students develop their knowledge of the crucial role of data analytics in supply chain management and how it can contribute to an organisations overarching strategic goals and objectives. Students are assessed through an essay, a case study and presentation.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of analytics in optimising supply chain operations.
Apply techniques for collecting, cleaning, and preparing supply chain data for analysis, and conducting statistical analysis on collected data.
Utilise data analytics to enhance key supply chain metrics, including service levels, inventory turnover, transportation costs, and lead times.
Apply supply chain analytics concepts to solve complex supply chain problems.
Demonstrate skills in problem solving, oral and written communication, and applying an international perspective on supply chain management.
prerequisites: must have completed BUSI2001 Emerging Technologies, Data and Business Analytics
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion, Discussion – 15%

title: Fundamentals of Procurement and Supply
overview: This course provides students with a foundation in procurement and supply by introducing key concepts, activities, technologies, and processes within and between organisations that create value and enhance market position. It emphasises the importance of building effective relationships with stakeholders and supply chain partners. Students will develop an understanding of the role of procurement in supply chains and its significance for organisational efficiency and success in today’s highly competitive global business environment.
learning_outcomes: Discern the role and value of procurement in organisations.
Explain the procurement cycle and its contribution to spend management and categorisation.
Apply methods and tools to develop sourcing plans and optimised supplier base.
Assess models of buyer-seller relationships and evaluate the importance of supplier development.
Evaluate approaches to pricing and cost management in procurement.
Demonstrate problem solving, oral, and written communication skills, and an international perspective.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Integrated Supply Networks
overview: This course provides in-depth knowledge of the temporal and spatial processes that add value for customers in supply networks, the philosophies and techniques for the application of supply chain strategies, and the digital technologies that enable integrative efforts and competitiveness as an ecosystem. In this course, students gain insights into various strategies, value proposition for businesses, evolving technology applications and the synchronisation of processes and operations across the supply chain. With Industry 4.0 and artificial intelligence (AI) being embraced in today's digital era, supply chains are now evolving into networks and ecosystems enabling collaborative interconnectivity and integration among firms. Students are assessed through a report and an examination.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the value systems, competitive priorities and performance of supply chain ecosystems with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a report and an examination

Analyse the issues, risks and strategic approaches when operating in global supply environments with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a report and an examination

Examine the emerging concepts and evolving technology applications and recommend strategies for more integrative and collaborative supply networks with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a report and an examination

Demonstrate skills in problem solving and applying an international perspective with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a report and an examination
antirequisites: N/A

title: Procurement for Strategic Advantage
overview: This course equips students with a deeper knowledge of procurement structures and processes in both public and private sectors. It covers the theories and strategies for enhanced value, buyer-supplier relationships, and category management; as well as the analytical skills and competencies required in the realm of the digital age for strategic advantage. This course examines the processes and systems required for effective strategic, tactical and operational management of assets and resources in contemporary public and private organisations, including small to medium enterprises. Students are assessed through a critical analysis, presentation and report.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the procurement structures, processes, skills and complexities inherent in organisations and supply chains today with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis, presentation and report

Examine the impact of digitalization on procurement, manufacturing, warehousing and logistics with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis, presentation and report

Critically analyse the issues in sourcing and supply and recommend solutions to increase value and strategic advantage for businesses with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis, presentation and report

Demonstrate skills in self-management, problem solving, oral and written communication, teamwork, and applying an international perspective with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this CLO in a critical analysis, presentation and report
prerequisites: must have completed BUSI2302 Fundamentals of Procurement and Supply
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Sustainability in Supply Chains
overview: This course promotes an in-depth understanding of sustainability and its effect on the supply chain. It equips students with the critical strategic, managerial and ethical perspectives for developing, implementing and addressing environmental, social and economic value in the context of global supply chain operations.
learning_outcomes: Examine economic, environmental and social value in terms of sustainability standards, practices and issues associated with supply chain operations with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this course learning outcome in an essay and examination

Analyse sustainability planning and decision-making situations faced by managers in a global context and how they affect the supply chain with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this course learning outcome in an essay and examination

Recommend solutions for problems in sustainable supply management, operations, and logistics with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this course learning outcome in an essay and examination

Effectively communicate the strategies for achieving sustainable supply chains in today's competitive business environment with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this course learning outcome in an essay and examination

Demonstrate skills in ethical awareness and applying an international perspective with readings and class activities around the topics by completing the core requirements of this course learning outcome in an essay and examination
antirequisites: N/A

title: Project Management Methodologies and Concepts
overview: This course builds on the Foundations of Project Management course. It covers project management methods, agile project management, lean project management, soft systems, design management, total quality control and quality assurance, project communications, information and communication technologies (ICTs), project success/ failure, lessons learned and continuous improvement.
learning_outcomes: Explain advanced project management concepts
Compare and evaluate various project management methodologies
Describe project quality management and processes
Compare traditional and modern project communication on projects
Discuss broad perspectives in respect to project success and failure
prerequisites: Must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Project Risk Management
overview: This course covers the area of risk management in the project context. It highlights the importance of risk management and the need for project managers to think ahead in this regard. It contains essential risk management theory and concepts as applicable to project environments including project risk planning, preparation and response. It also overviews the areas of risk identification, assessment, monitoring and control. Qualitative and quantitative risk analysis techniques will be presented to students within this course.
learning_outcomes: Explain the benefits of risk management for projects
Outline the risk management process
Describe roles and responsibilities in the risk management process
Identify, assess and treat possible project risks
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Infrastructure and Sustainability
overview: The objective of the course is to develop an understanding of tangible ways to improve the economic, social, and environmental performance of urban infrastructure across the design, construction and operation phases. The course will cover a range of topics relevant to current sustainable infrastructure challenges with a focus on the integration of the development, transport and energy sectors. The course is delivered in an interactive industry style small group discovery model and provides students with valuable industry ready knowledge and skills.
learning_outcomes: Discuss how sustainability outcomes can be improved in particular forms of infrastructure that align to specific global and national best practice principles
Understand a range of factors that drive good outcomes in infrastructure sustainability with a focus on responding to climate change
Compare and contrast national government approaches to sustainable infrastructure planning
Discuss key sustainable infrastructure messages from the Australian Infrastructure Audit and Australian Infrastructure Plan and identify examples of best practice
Discuss the sustainability implications of electro-mobility and the integration of transport and land use planning
Identify specific implications for sustainable infrastructure from the transition from centralised to distributed energy networks
antirequisites: N/A

title: Systems Thinking and Projects
overview: This course introduces students to general systems theory and systems thinking in the context of project management and practice. The course goes on to explore complex systems and some key aspects including system evaluation and optimisation. It also looks at the benefits in managing complex projects appropriately.
learning_outcomes: Display knowledge of general systems theory and approaches
Explain how systems thinking can assist with project management problems
Describe the characteristics of complex project management
Draw from systems methodologies and tools to communicate project situations and resolutions
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Industry Based Applications
overview: This course focuses student attention on the everyday use of project management knowledge and practices within various industries and fields. This will allow students to gather a broader appreciation of project management and highlight unique aspects within different types of projects. It will also introduce students to areas such as industrial relations, health and safety, and sustainability as applied to projects. A series of lectures, workshops and invited industry speakers will deliver real life practical information and scenarios associated with various industry sectors and project management.
learning_outcomes: Describe project management practices as they exist between various industries and sectors.
Explain planning, constraints and commercial concepts as applied to projects.
Identify and describe various stakeholders within specific industries.
Discuss industrial relations issues and health and safety concerns on projects.
prerequisites: must have completed all of PROJ1000 Foundations of Project Management/PROJ1001 Scheduling and Cost Management/PROJ2002 Project Management Methodologies and Concepts/PROJ2005 Project Risk Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: PM Research Methods
overview: The course provides students with practical knowledge on quantitative and qualitative research methods, techniques for critical literature evaluation, and skills to execute a research plan. Students will identify a research problem of project management relevance informed by practice and theory, and consider various research approaches and methods. On completion of this course students will be able to effectively design, undertake and communicate research issues.
learning_outcomes: Discuss research theory in an informed and educated way
Identify a research problem and develop relevant research questions
Explain the difference between quantitative and qualitative research design
Develop a research plan designed to address identified research problems
Present a well-structured, informative, well-argued research proposal
antirequisites: N/A

title: Project Management Research Study
overview: The Project Management Research Study is the program's capstone course requiring students to deliver a detailed research report based on their nominated field of interest. The research study will follow standard research processes including topic selection and introduction, literature review, research methodology, results analysis and discussion, conclusion and recommendations. The course is intended to develop student research skills and enhance understanding within their field of interest.
learning_outcomes: Critically review relevant academic literature to identify current and emerging issues in project management
Identify and apply appropriate research methodologies
Collect, analyse and interpret research data to formulate conclusions and recommendations
Explain and defend research outcomes using both oral and written presentations
prerequisites: must have completed PROJ3002 PM Research Methods
antirequisites: N/A

title: Discovering Opportunities in Property
overview: The aim of this course is to introduce students to the opportunities and complexities of the property market. By examining the unique characteristics of property, including its legal, physical, and locational aspects, students will gain a foundational understanding of how these factors influence property-related decisions. The course will primarily focus on the perspective of the property consumer—individuals and organizations that use, buy, sell, rent, invest in, and speculate with property—enabling students to evaluate and navigate the property market effectively.
learning_outcomes: Apply key practical and legislative principles to scenarios involving the buying, selling, leasing, management, development and investment of real property
Analyse market, investment and development opportunities for real property using basic property economics and valuation concepts
Evaluate legal, physical, economic and social factors that influence real property decisions
Identify, collect, interpret and present relevant primary and secondary data to support decisions about real property
Apply Business Enterprise Skills in the Property discipline at a foundation level: i) problem solving, ii) written communication, and iii) oral communication
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions – 15%

title: Property Asset Management
overview: This course aims to equip students with specialist property asset management skills and knowledge, enhancing their broad property education. It covers principles and practices essential for effective property asset management from both traditional and corporate real estate perspectives. The course addresses contemporary issues such as sustainability, indoor environmental quality, and occupant well-being. It applies universally applicable principles, referencing South Australian legislation where relevant. Covering residential and commercial properties, the course emphasises superior management skills to optimise returns and enhance economic value. Recognising the pivotal role of property asset managers, the course prepares students for diverse career opportunities within the industry.
learning_outcomes: Understand and utilise various techniques and tools required to assess different types of properties and their facilities
Demonstrate a sound working knowledge of property documentation required in the sale, leasing and management of property.
Prepare and plan budgets and assess their potential effect on property income and values.
Discuss legislation and its application relevant to agency practices.
Establish strategies and tactics to operate and manage properties to ascertain clients' and consumers' strategic goals and objectives.
prerequisites: must have completed MARK1004 Discovering Opportunities in Property
antirequisites: N/A

title: Property Economics
overview: This course deepens Students’ understanding of economics and property concepts from ‘Discovering Opportunities in Property (DOP)’ and 'Principles of Economics’, while enhancing analytical skills from ‘Quantitative Methods for Business’. Unlike DOP, this course establishes theoretical foundations of property markets and values, applying principles using International Valuation Standards. Students will explore economic and geographical factors influencing property markets and solve practical problems faced by real estate professionals. The course develops Enterprise Skills, focusing on problem-solving, written communication, and international perspectives, with weekly Excel exercises. This foundational course is crucial for subsequent studies in valuation, marketing, management, and property development, relating material to global examples.
learning_outcomes: Analyse economic and geographical factors influencing property markets.
Apply property economic theory to the development and pricing of land resources
Compare the role of the free market and Government, in land resource management
Analyse the main characteristics of housing markets and the process of regeneration.

Apply Business Enterprise Skills in the context of the Property discipline at an intermediate level proficiency encompassing analytical thinking, structured communication, and awareness of international perspectives.
prerequisites: must have completed all of ACCT1000 Accounting for Decision Makers/ECON1000 Principles of Economics/MARK1004 Discovering Opportunities in Property
antirequisites: N/A

title: Property and Real Estate Law
overview: The Property and Real Estate Law course aims to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of property law's pivotal role in economic, legal, and social systems. Through exploration of key concepts such as real and personal property distinctions, estates in land, and the Torrens system of land title, students will grasp the intricacies of property ownership and protection. Topics include leases, tenancies, mortgages, easements, and restrictive covenants, offering insight into practical applications. By delving into these subjects, students will gain a deeper appreciation for the complexities of property law and its profound impact on daily life, fostering informed decision-making in various legal and professional contexts.
learning_outcomes: Apply the fundamental principles of property law from a theoretical and practical perspective.
Explain the Torrens system as it applies in South Australia and Australia.
Describe the concepts which underlie the reasoning for the protection of legal and equitable interests.
Describe the concepts which underlie the reasoning for the protection of legal and equitable interests.
Resolve property problems by identifying legal issues and by applying property rules and principles.
Demonstrate Business Enterprise Skills: i) Self Management (intermediate level); ii) Problem Solving (intermediate level); and iii) Written Communication (intermediate level).
prerequisites: must have completed BUSI1001 Business Law
antirequisites: N/A

title: Personal Finance
overview: This course undertakes a holistic examination of the set of financial decisions and constraints that learners face—personal spending, saving, income taxation, insurance cover, credit and debt, and investments—across stages in their (financial) life cycles. By focusing on personal financial planning as an evolving process and providing appropriate financial tools and techniques—time value of money, personal financial statements, comprehensive analysis of interest rates, returns and risk—it aims to improve their personal budgeting, tax management, insurance, consumer debt, and investment decision making.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate proficiency in the application of time value of money concepts and methods to personal financial management decisions
Evaluate borrowing and personal investment alternatives and their implications for the accumulation of personal wealth
Formulate and use personal financial budgets as devices for the planning and control of personal finances
Explain fundamental concepts related to risk and return and their relevance to personal investment planning, taxation, and financial management decisions
antirequisites: N/A

title: Real Estate Practice
overview: The Real Estate Practice course aims to equip students with the knowledge essential for establishing and managing a real estate agency, and effectively marketing various real estate, including complex commercial and industrial properties. Key objectives include understanding real estate marketing, business management principles, and statutory and ethical requirements for roles like Agent, Property Manager, and Sales Representative. The course builds upon foundational knowledge from prior property studies, fostering critical thinking and independent argumentation. While focusing on South Australian legislation, it also explores universal principles applicable across real estate agencies globally, providing a comprehensive understanding of the industry.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the market for real estate services and demonstrate an understanding of the requirements for setting up a real estate agency
Formulate marketing plans and apply the results of market analysis to the successful marketing of non-residential properties

Demonstrate and apply an understanding of the main obligations of the Land Agent under the South Australian Land Agents Act 1994 and its Regulations, or the appropriate legislation in the State or Country in which the student intends to practice
Select appropriate ethical responses to situational dilemmas, including the representational dilemma
Discuss, analyse and apply management and organisational behaviour theory to the management of the real estate office and sales force
prerequisites: must have completed BUSI2027 Property and Real Estate Law
antirequisites: N/A

title: Building Evaluation of Property
overview: The aim of this course is to develop skills in understanding the construction processes for both residential and commercial buildings, along with identifying and addressing faults. Additionally, it aims to provide a detailed comprehension of building services. Professionals involved in real estate, from market interpreters to property managers, play crucial roles in the property construction process. Therefore, a solid understanding of building processes and systems is essential for accurate reporting and assessing the impacts on property value. The course also covers contemporary topics such as population aging and the building evaluation process. Guest lectures and site visits enhance theoretical concepts with practical insights.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the principles of building regulation, particularly as they relate to a building's life safety systems
Apply a basic understanding of residential building structures
Apply a basic understanding of large scale commercial building structures
Evaluate the appropriateness of large scale building services
Recognise the most common building faults in residential buildings
Identify issues affecting sustainability of commercial and residential buildings
antirequisites: N/A

title: Fundamentals of Sport and Recreation
overview: This course will give students a sound understanding of the sport and recreation industry in Australia. Students will be introduced to key stakeholders within the sport and recreation industry and explore the key managerial skills, knowledge, and tasks of those responsible for the oversight and provision of sport and recreation opportunities. Students will also examine industry application of various theoretical models and concepts.
learning_outcomes: Discuss how the unique contextual aspects of the industry impact the role of the sport and recreation professional
Identify and explain the key managerial tasks and responsibilities of the sport and recreation professional
Identify and distinguish between the differing roles and responsibilities of the public, not-forprofit, and professional sectors in sport and recreation
Articulate the need for trend analysis and managerial adaptation
Apply key theoretical models and concepts to current industry needs
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport, Health and Wellbeing
overview: The aim of this course is to explore the concept of wellness in contemporary society and apply it to understand the importance of sport and recreation in positively enhancing health and quality of life. In doing so, it enhances critical thinking and analysis skills in students by considering the managerial and policy aspects of wellness in terms of individual and more general community health and the role that a variety of key stakeholders play in contributing to a 'happy' and 'well' society.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate how sport and recreation can positively contribute to improved health and wellness for individuals and communities
Analyse the role of policy in relation to enhancing health and wellness for individuals and communities
Discuss current trends and future issues in relation to health and wellness
Interpret and evaluate data on recreation and health from a management perspective
antirequisites: N/A

title: Commercial Operations and Marketing in Sport
overview: This course aims to provide students with knowledge regarding how the Commercial Operations of sport and recreation organisations, specifically how they manage their need to generate and maintain revenue streams and fund their operations and programs. The course also aims to develop knowledge of marketing principles as they uniquely apply to the sport and recreation setting. Individuals who can successfully assist sport organisations in this area are highly sought after. This course is designed to provide students with knowledge, skills, and techniques in the area of commercial operations that will provide an advantage when securing future job opportunities in the sport and recreation industry.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate previously developed sport management skills by applying commercial decision-making techniques to improve business acumen relevant to future employment contexts.
Independently assess marketing strategy needs of a corporate organisation and provide a sport sponsorship solution based on a detailed analysis of a specific sport organisation
Demonstrate critical thinking skills in solving complex and dynamic sport organisation commercial operations problems, including applying fundamental marketing concepts in the sport context.
Identify the importance of sales, networking and relationship building skills as they apply in the unique commercial sport setting
Demonstrates an understanding of the layers of sport delivery and the associated levels of government funding that are available
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport in Contemporary Society
overview: Analysing the important role sport plays in contemporary society, this course will provide students with an understanding of a range of conceptual frameworks, case study examples and topical debates that can be located in a social and cultural context. In doing so, it will enhance students’ knowledge and understanding of the problems and issues posed by the relationship between sport and society and the ways in which these are managed by clubs and governing organisations.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the role of sport in contemporary society and how it impacts on a range of key stakeholders
Explain the role of sport within society with an understanding of the key sociological approaches
Analyse key social and cultural issues in contemporary sport
Analyse specific policies implemented in sport and whether they have achieved their desired aim
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing the Athletic Pathway
overview: The aim of this course is to examine the athletic journey from grassroots participation through to elite competition, focusing on the managerial requirements that facilitate all aspects of this process. Students will examine a variety of applied approaches to recruiting and retaining sport participants before focusing on the elite performance pathway, gaining a valuable insight into the operational requirements of talent identification and development. The course concludes with a focus on elite sport, specifically examining the unique pressures and commitments required of the elite athlete during competition, how they are managed and the impact of retirement.
learning_outcomes: Understand the role the athletic pathway plays in the management of all the participating stakeholders in sport
Explain the role of sport development in achieving organisational objectives in relation to youth and grassroots participation in sport
Analyse the key issues involved in the creation, development and management of the elite athlete pathway
Identify the ways in which sports clubs and organisations manage and support elite athletes
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport Planning in Local Communities
overview: Focusing on application of data analytics, the course enables students to gain a deeper understanding of how local government plans sport and recreation opportunities for their communities.
learning_outcomes: Differentiate and critically assess the relevant data sources which supply information pertaining to Australian society, such as the Census, Sport and Physical Activity Surveys etc
Critically evaluate the difficulties inherent in public provision of a non-mandated service
Recognise and appraise a variety of planning tools such as maps, aerial photographs, GIS
Evaluate the available planning methodologies against criteria such as equity, ethics, accountability, efficiency and effectiveness
Critically assess the different international approaches to sport planning
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport Management and Digitalisation
overview: This course allows students to consider the impact of digitalisation on sport and how sport is managed, with a focus on the role of social media, analytics and the rise of e-sports.
learning_outcomes: Explain the important role that digitalisation has in contemporary sport management
Discuss the role digital technology has in sport organisations
Be able to analyse and interpret analytics relating to sport organisations and performance
Discuss the opportunities and threats that digitalisation has presented for the sport industry
Critically analyse the ethical and legal implications of digitalisation in sport
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sport Governance and Leadership
overview: This course aims to increase understanding of the sport governance concepts, and the ethics and principles of good governance and leadership. Designed to enhance awareness of both what is considered contemporary leadership, and also students will be required to explore their own self-awareness, preparing them for success as a team member, and in leadership roles as their careers progress.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish the characteristics of effective leadership and governance, and ethical practice
Critique the issues facing sport leaders in governance and management of sporting organisations
Apply theories of best practice governance, leadership and team building
Critically evaluate the major leadership and motivation theories
antirequisites: N/A

title: Fundamentals of Global Tourism and Hospitality
overview: The course aims to provide students with broad knowledge of tourism and hospitality and a foundation for further studies in the program. It equips learners with a holistic understanding of the field of study, including key terminology, origins and current building blocks of the industry, its impacts, and strategies for effective management. By using international case studies and applying relevant course theory to tourism context, the course fosters students’ international perspective and effective communication.
learning_outcomes: Define key terminology and correctly apply it in the context of tourism and hospitality studies
Explain the factors that led to the emergence of the modern tourism and hospitality industry
Based on different classifications of tourists, explain how their travel motivations and behaviour impact management and marketing
Analyse the main components of tourism and hospitality sector and identify factors that affect them
Assess the costs and benefits of tourism and hospitality
antirequisites: N/A

title: Foundations of Event Management
overview: This course aims to explore key concepts central to event management, enabling students to apply theoretical underpinnings to professional practice for effective event management. Serving as an introduction to the event industry and operations, it will establish a solid foundation for further studies in this field. Designed to enhance critical thinking and analysis skills crucial for effective event management, the course prepares students to succeed in the tourism, events and hospitality sector with a comprehensive understanding of event management.
learning_outcomes: Explain the impacts of events on host societies
Describe the diversity of events and the way they operate
Analyse the role of stakeholders in contributing to successful events
Discuss the unique characteristics of event experience that explain event visitor behaviour
Discuss key concepts in event studies for the development of effective event practices and procedures
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Hospitality Operations
overview: The course aims to prepare students for managerial careers within the hospitality industry, focusing on the management of business operations through the lens of key departments including marketing, finance, human resource management, risk and logistics. It is designed to develop students working knowledge of the hospitality industry and the operating tasks involved in managing hospitality businesses.
learning_outcomes: Explain the role and key operational functions of hospitality organisations, and challenges and demands facing managers in hospitality firms
Analyse the performance of key operations in hospitality firms -including risk, logistics, marketing and HR
Develop and interpret key financial statements and performance indicators to support managerial decision making
Analyse internal and external factors to make evidence-based managerial decisions
Discuss how sustainability practices in hospitality firms affect the triple bottom line of profit, people and environment
prerequisites: must have completed HOSP1000 Fundamentals of Global Tourism and Hospitality
antirequisites: N/A

title: Experiential Product Design for Tourism, Events and Hospitality
overview: The aim of the course is to equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge to propose creative experiential products in the highly competitive sector of tourism, events, and hospitality. The course integrates foundational tourism theory and design thinking to develop business strategy.
learning_outcomes: Research global and local market trends to identify business opportunities for development of a new experiential product in tourism, events, and hospitality
Propose a creative product idea and justify its relevance to the tourism events and hospitality industry
Devise an appropriate business and marketing strategy for the implementation of a proposed product
Apply relevant course concepts and theory to idea generation and implementation strategy
Communicate an idea for an experiential product as appropriate for industry and academic audiences
antirequisites: N/A

title: Eventful Cities and Event Leveraging
overview: This course aims to equip students with the skills to maximise the benefits derived from hosting events, while also providing them with a comprehensive understanding of utilising events as effective strategies for driving change. By expanding upon foundational concepts of event management, this course delves into approaches used by various sectors to leverage events, and the diverse ways in which they engage with them. Designed to master critical thinking, organisational skills and creativity essential for the strategic use of events, the course prepares students to excel in any field related to event management or involvement.
learning_outcomes: Discuss approaches used by different sectors to leverage events
Identify the diverse ways in which various sectors engage with events
Discuss sustainability and ethical issues in event management
Analyse real-world examples to illustrate the successful use of events for fostering positive changes
Propose strategies necessary for achieving successful and sustainable outcomes through events
prerequisites: must have completed HOSP1001 Foundations of Event Management
antirequisites: N/A

title: Sustainable Tourism Destination Management
overview: This course aims to equip students with the skill set for sustainable tourism development, with a focus on analysing tourism impacts and developing effective strategies to manage those impacts aligning with the sustainable development goals. Serving as an introduction to sustainable tourism development, it establishes a solid foundation for further studies on destination management for sustainable tourism. Designed to enhance critical thinking and analysis skills crucial for destination management, the course prepares students for the tourism, events and hospitality sector with a comprehensive understanding of sustainable tourism development.
learning_outcomes: Explain economic, socio-cultural and environmental tourism impacts
Discuss role of trust and power for sustainable tourism
Discuss importance of community wellbeing to promote sustainable tourism destination management
Analyse the importance of a multi-stakeholder approach for sustainable tourism destination management
Discuss key concepts in sustainable tourism to align with sustainable development goals
prerequisites: must have completed HOSP1000 Fundamentals of Global Tourism and Hospitality
antirequisites: N/A

title: Digital Technologies in Tourism, Events and Hospitality
overview: This course serves as an introduction to the digital transformation of the tourism, events and hospitality industry and establishes a solid foundation in this fast-evolving context. It enables students to critically reflect on contemporary strategies and concepts that currently shape the digitalisation of tourism, events and hospitality organisations. Designed to enhance technical skills and promote critical thinking and analysis, the course provides students with an understanding of the importance and application of digital marketing in general, and social media in particular. It equips students with innovative digital and communication skills for the tourism, events and hospitality sector.
learning_outcomes: Develop a critical appreciation of the nature, role and importance of digital technologies drawing on diverse perspectives
Critically investigate contemporary strategies, concepts and ideas related to technologies in tourism, events and hospitality
Critically evaluate the impact of digital technologies on travellers’ behaviour
Review the influence of digital technologies media on business strategies and operations
Identify opportunities and challenges of application of digital technologies in Tourism, Events and Hospitality business operations
prerequisites: must have completed HOSP1000 Fundamentals of Global Tourism and Hospitality
antirequisites: N/A

title: Tourism, Events and Hospitality Industry Research Project
overview: This course equips students with skills to work in the tourism, events and hospitality industry. It draws on the innovation, technology, business and sustainability in industry enabling students to critically reflect on these areas. Designed to enhance technical skills and promote critical thinking and analysis, the course provides students with an understanding of the importance of stakeholder engagement in understanding the business needs of, and developing relevant strategies for, an organisation.
learning_outcomes: Develop a critical appreciation of industry-relevant problems
Critically investigate contemporary strategies, concepts and ideas related to business problems in tourism, events and hospitality
Understand the importance of stakeholder enagagement in business operations
Critically evaluate the impact of tourism, events and hospitality businesses on sustainability
Discuss opportunities and challenges of Tourism, Events and Hospitality business operations
prerequisites: must have completed HOSP1000 Fundamentals of Global Tourism and Hospitality
antirequisites: N/A

title: Physiology Essentials 100
overview: The aim of this course is to gain an understanding of the physiological dimensions of body function in health and disease. Introductory biology: characteristics and classification of living things, homeostasis. Study of body functions and structure with emphasis on changes through the lifespan: blood and fluids, the cardiovascular system and circulation, haemostasis, the muscular, nervous, endocrine, digestive, respiratory and urinary systems; metabolism and nutrition; immunity. Integrative physiology: examination of systemic function, control and interaction between systems.
learning_outcomes: Apply a range of scientific and medical terminology to describe the functions of the human body.
Describe the normal structure and functions of cells and tissues and explain how cells and tissues are arranged into organs and organ systems.
Discuss the functions of the nervous, muscular, skeletal, integumentary, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, immune, digestive, and urinary systems, and genetic inheritance.
Explain how the organ systems interact with each other to sustain life, maintain homeostasis, and enable body function and movement.
Apply knowledge of normal body function to explain how specific diseases affect the function of cells, tissues, and organ systems.
antirequisites: must not have completed BIOL1051 Physiology Essentials 100 at the University of South Australia

title: Human Anatomy 100
overview: The aim of this course is to provide students with knowledge and understanding of the gross anatomy of the human body. Contents include: anatomical terminology, regions and planes; upper limb; lower limb; head, thorax; abdomen; pelvis; spine; bones; joints; muscles; soft tissues; organ systems, surface anatomy.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of anatomical terminology of directions, planes, motions and major tissues.
Use respectful language and behaviour in handling, positioning and palpating specimens and fellow students.
Accurately locate and name clinically relevant surface anatomy features.
Demonstrate knowledge of bone structure, major blood vessels and function of muscle groups, and nerve innervation of muscle groups of the limbs, spine, trunk and thorax.
Name and describe the function of the major organs of the digestive, respiratory, urinary and reproductive systems.
Identify and name the bones of the face and cranium.
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH1020 Human Anatomy 100 at the University of South Australia
assessment: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions – 60%

title: Aboriginal Health: Culture, Community and Country
overview: To develop introductory knowledge and understanding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures and languages, and impacts of colonisation in contemporary Australia, as the basis for developing reflective and culturally responsive health professionals.
learning_outcomes: Describe the diversity of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander culture pre-colonisation to the present
Discuss Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander concepts of health and wellbeing, including interrelationships with culture, family and connection to country

Describe the health of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Australians pre-colonisation and identify key events since colonisation that have impacted the health of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Describe the concept of strengths-based knowledge and communication and the application this approach to health and wellbeing of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
Examine the culture of health professions and the impacts of professional culture within the health system on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
Articulate the concept of cultural humility as a process of lifelong learning
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH1063 Aboriginal Health - Culture, Community and Country at the University of South Australia

title: Physical Activity and Health
overview: This course aims to introduce students to key concepts in waking movement behaviours (physical activity and sedentary behaviour), including definitions, metrics and guidelines. This course provides foundational knowledge relating to the interactions and relationships between physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and health in different populations. Students will develop an extensive knowledge base relevant to movement behaviours and health, in addition to the ability to apply guidelines to optimise waking movement behaviours in a range of populations. This course aligns with the programs intent to produce graduates who are knowledgeable and can think critically and ethically within exercise science and human movement practice.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the importance of movement behaviours for population health
Discuss population groups at risk of unhealthy movement behaviours
Develop interventions and strategies for promoting and evaluating movement behaviours in diverse populations across the lifespan
Describe the role of key stakeholders in the promotion of healthy movement behaviours in Australia
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 30%

title: Motor Development and Ageing
overview: The aim of this course is to develop learners’ knowledge of human growth and motor development across the lifespan with a focus on practical applications in exercise, health, and sport. This course delves into the physical, psychosocial, and cognitive changes that occur with human growth and development, with specific reference to their implications for physical activity and exercise. Learners will build an understanding of typical human growth and development, influencing factors, social determinants, and the role of physical activity and exercise in growth, motor development, pregnancy, and ageing. This course aligns with the program’s goals of developing a deep understanding of the role of exercise in supporting health and well-being across the lifespan, including the consideration of individual needs and perspectives to provide holistic advice and intervention.
learning_outcomes: Describe the stages of growth, maturation, and development from conception to reproduction and death across the lifespan.
Identify and describe structural, physiological, and psychosocial components of human development, and explore their interrelationships.

Identify exercises contraindicated for specific stages of growth, maturation, and development, considering chronological and biological age differences, and common injuries or conditions in the different developmental stages.

Formulate effective communication strategies and respond appropriately, to assist clients and service users from diverse populations to develop and maintain appropriate health and physical activity behaviours.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 30%

title: Functional Anatomy
overview: The course builds on the foundations of structural anatomy through the analysis of movement, by applying kinesiology principles and anatomical terminology. Muscle coordination and function; postural control and stability; effects of muscle imbalances on the musculoskeletal system and changes with the musculoskeletal system with aging. Students will be able to apply this knowledge through the practical assessment of strength, flexibility, anthropometric, posture and movement analysis of individuals, then interpret the findings to provide basic exercise programming advice.
learning_outcomes: Conduct musculoskeletal movement analysis using the principles of kinesiology.
Describe the role of the musculoskeletal system, including neurological and non-muscular components, and the effect of internal and external forces applied to these structures throughout movement.
Explain the effects of exercise, immobilisation, aging and injury on the musculoskeletal system of the human body, including the adaptations of the neuro-musculoskeletal system.
Discuss the role of body proportions in sports performance and talent identification.
Interpret results from movement analysis, including anthropometric, flexibility and posture.

Analyse movement during prescribed exercises, identifying which muscles are active in producing and controlling a movement of a particular joint. Integrate knowledge of functional anatomy with other exercise science sub-disciplines and apply this knowledge in health , exercise, sports and workplace contexts.
antirequisites: must not have completed HLTH1045 Functional Anatomy at the University of South Australia
assessment: Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration – 45%

title: Societal Issues in Clinical Exercise Physiology
overview: In this course, students will examine the complex interaction between society, the health care system and the role of the Accredited Exercise Physiologist, and gain insight into political, sociocultural, economic and individual determinants of health as well as an understanding of the current funding models within the healthcare system. Consideration is given to inequality, difference, social responsibility and social justice. Students will also be introduced to client centered practice, multi-disciplinary environments and practice models and ethical issues in health care practice.
learning_outcomes: Examine the Australian Health Care system and economic, societal and individual determinants of health and access to health care.
Apply knowledge of ethical practice, social responsibility and social justice as an Allied Health Practitioner.

Discuss the role of an accredited exercise physiologist (AEP) within the Australian Health Care System including, service models, legislation, regulation, rights & responsibilities and funding sources.
Examine the health consumers' position from different cultural and social perspectives including Aboriginal Culture and vulnerable populations.
prerequisites: Must have completed HLTH1017 Aboriginal Health: Culture, Community and Country
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH2029 Societal Issues in Clinical Exercise Physiology at the University of South Australia
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 40%

title: Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Research in Health Sciences
overview: This interdisciplinary course provides foundational principals, knowledge and skills for evidence-based practice in health sciences. This course focuses on the principles, philosophies and processes which underpin evidence-based practice. Research methods are reviewed: quantitative and qualitative research frameworks, methodologies and methods, and data interpretation. Statistical issues addressed include: hypothesis generation, concepts of probability (including sensitivity and specificity), variance and error and tests for determining differences and associations (such as descriptive and inferential statistics). Key steps in evidence-based practice are introduced including using established frameworks to ask an answerable question, structured searching of the literature, critical appraisal of the literature using a range of tools, including hierarchy of evidence, rigour and trustworthiness and concepts such as sampling and sample size, effect size, odds ratio and number needed to treat, and implementation and translation of evidence to clinical practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe principles, philosophies and processes which underpin evidence-based practice
Discuss key principles of quantitative and qualitative research paradigms, designs, methodologies and methods
Identify various forms of data, what it means, how it can be analysed and presented
Describe and apply key steps in evidence-based practice using established frameworks and tools (such as during searching of the literature and critical appraisal)
Identify potential threats to internal validity and what strategies can be used to avoid bias and improve rigour in research
Describe issues to consider when implementing and translating evidence to clinical practice.
antirequisites: must not have completed HLTH1049 Global and National Health

title: Motor Control and Learning
overview: To build a body of knowledge whereby the student can interpret the theoretical basis of motor learning and control to undertake motor skill analysis and assessment, and to implement evidence-based motor skill training programs with consideration for the learner, skill characteristics, and environment. Students learn the role of the neuromuscular and sensory systems in relation to the control and learning of movement, and the theories that underpin the control and learning of movement. Students gain hands on experience in assessing motor function and implementing learning design factors to promote learning for a diverse range of future learners.
learning_outcomes: Explain the theories and principles associated with the control and learning of movement.
Describe the structure and function of the neuromuscular and sensory systems as they relate to the control of movement and motor learning.
Describe changes in motor performance that occur with practice and motor learning across various life stages.

Apply principles of motor learning and control to select, design, and deliver evidence-based techniques for assessing motor abilities and performance, with consideration of their strengths and limitations.
Apply motor learning principles to design learning environments and strategies, and deliver plans, to facilitate learning for individuals or groups across diverse populations.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 25%

title: Exercise Physiology 1
overview: The course aims to introduce students to the theory underlying, and test procedures for evaluating, the physiological responses to exercise and how these impact on health and physical performance. The course builds on foundational information from human physiology courses to further students understanding of the physiological effects of exercise, together with relevant exercise and health assessments. Students will develop their understanding of the acute and chronic effects of exercise on a range of physiological systems and populations, in addition to developing their ability to conduct health and exercise assessments in a safe and effective manner. The course aligns with the programs intent to develop knowledgeable graduates that can design, implement and evaluate exercise and physical activity.
learning_outcomes: Describe the function of key physiological systems for exercise.
Describe the integrated response of relevant physiological systems to acute exercise training in healthy children, adults, and the elderly.
Describe the adaptations to chronic exercise training for healthy adults.
Describe the physiology of common clinical health conditions to justify the provision and adjustment of exercise programs to support health and fitness for relevant populations.
Conduct and analyse tests of health, fitness, and performance and compare results between time-points, individuals, and populations.
prerequisites: Must have completed BIOL1020 Physiology Essentials 100
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions – 60%
Data Collection and/or Analysis, Skills Demonstration – 40%

title: Human Nutrition
overview: This foundation level course aims to develop an understanding of the relationship between diet, nutrition, exercise and health and on completion be able to provide general advice to apparently healthy clients. This course aligns with the program intent to apply evidence-based skills and knowledge to assess and improve health and wellbeing within a community setting.
learning_outcomes: Identify and use current Australian guidelines to provide appropriate general advice on nutrition for health, performance and recovery.
Describe the basic functions of macronutrients and micronutrients, their common sources, and their role in energy balance, and general health and well-being.
Identifies implications of a basic dietary analysis for general health and wellbeing, with consideration of strengths and limitations of assessment methods.
Recognise signs of inappropriate dietary behaviours across a range of health and exercise contexts and identify appropriate referral options.
Describe the role of diet in the development and management of chronic diseases and obesity
prerequisites: must have completed all of HBIO1002 Human Anatomy and Physiology A/HBIO1003 Human Anatomy and Physiology B
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 40%

title: Exercise Prescription and Delivery 1
overview: This course will equip students with the ability to deliver exercise programs to meet the health, fitness and/or performance goals of apparently healthy clients.
