Additionally, graduates will be able to operate under the supervision of an appropriate health professional. Monitoring and progressing exercise load; delivery of appropriate exercise modalities to suit the needs and capabilities of clients; recognition and correction of unsafe/dysfunctional movement patterns; exercise to optimize client learning and execution.
learning_outcomes: Monitor, evaluate and progress as appropriate exercise load using mechanical, physiological and/or perceptual methods
Identify, describe, analyse and demonstrate a broad range of exercise modalities, and select exercise type and load appropriate to suit client needs and abilities
Safely deliver individual exercise sessions using a range of modalities and loads following achievement of course objective 2
Document and report progress and outcomes to clients and / or health professionals both verbally and in writing
Describe professional practices when applying programs from other health professionals
prerequisites: must have completed HLTH1051 Functional Anatomy
antirequisites: must not have completed HLTH2027 Consumption, Work and the Self II

title: Biomechanics of Human Movement
overview: To develop knowledge and skills to describe, measure, analyse and communicate the mechanical principles underlying human movement in the context of exercise, sport and health.
learning_outcomes: Describe biomechanical principles and apply them to the analysis of human movement in exercise and sport
Analyse biomechanical problems in human movement, exercise and sport science contexts and develop strategies that enhance function and performance, and minimise injury risk for different populations
Conduct quantitative analyses of human movement using appropriate tools and techniques in exercise and sport science contexts
Interpret and effectively communicate biomechanical data to clients and exercise and sport science professionals
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Interactive Questions, Interactive Questions, Interactive Questions – 45%

title: Exercise Physiology 2
overview: Equip students with the necessary skills to safely and competently perform health, exercise and sport-related physiological assessments. Further, the students will be able to apply knowledge of the physiological effects of exercise and training to the evaluation of assessment outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Describe the integrated physiological responses and adaptations to acute and chronic exercise in normal and various environmental conditions, and by external influences.
Identify and explain the common processes and select relevant equipment required to safely conduct accurate and individualised health, exercise and sport-related assessments.
Explain the scientific rationale, purpose, reliability, validity, calibration, assumptions and limitations of common health and exercise assessments and practices.
Safely conduct individualised exercise and health assessments, including the identification, management and reporting of contraindications, adverse signs and symptoms.
Interpret, explain and analyse physiological data obtained during health and exercise assessments, and compare such data between time-points, individuals and populations.

Record, analyse and interpret information from assessments and normative data, and effectively communicate the results in written and/or verbal formats to support clients and service users in understanding assessment outcomes.
prerequisites: must have completed HBIO1000 Exercise Physiology 1
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Skills Demonstration, Data Collection and/or Analysis, Interview – 40%

title: Health, Exercise and Sport Psychology
overview: The aim of this course is to extend knowledge in human movement and health science into the area of health, exercise and sports psychology in order to determine the social, psychological and environmental factors that influence exercise behaviour, sport participation and human performance, as well as other health behaviours, and identify and apply individualised and appropriate best-practice behavioural strategies and theories in working with individuals in health, exercise, and sport domains. Introduction to health, exercise and sport psychology; personality; motivation; arousal and anxiety; physical activity and psychological well-being; health behaviour adherence; behaviour change theories; motivational interviewing; behaviour change techniques and mental skills.
learning_outcomes: Describe psychological, environmental and social factors that influence sport, exercise and physical activity participation, adherence and performance, as well as other behavioural aspects of health.
Discuss how participation in sport, exercise and physical activity influences psychological aspects of the individuals involved.
Apply health, exercise and sport psychology related knowledge and skills for professional roles related to human movement, exercise and sports science, and other health professions.
Apply behaviour change theories and strategies in the health, exercise and sport context.
Design individualized behavioural interventions in the health, exercise and sport context.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of PSYC1001 Understanding Individual Behaviour and Cognition/PSYC1003 Health and Developmental Psychology OR must have completed HUMV1001 Motor Development and Ageing
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH3014 Health, Exercise and Sport Psychology at the University of South Australia

title: Exercise Prescription and Delivery 2
overview: This course will further develop students' knowledge and skills in prescribing and programming exercise for the broader community for future professional practice, including apparently healthy individuals of all ages. Exercise prescription process (including how to: conduct an initial consult and a pre-exercise screen, develop an exercise testing battery, and design an appropriate exercise program), aerobic and musculoskeletal exercise testing and prescription in healthy and 'special' populations, high intensity interval training, adaptations to aerobic and resistance training, exercise monitoring, periodisation, and advanced training methods.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate competency in screening participants using pre-exercise screening tools and procedures
Demonstrate competency in conducting health and skill-related fitness assessments
Design appropriate exercise/activity programs in a range of settings and for apparently healthy individuals to enhance their health and fitness
Demonstrate knowledge of professional practices in exercise prescription to apparently healthy individuals.
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC3050 Exercise Prescription and Delivery 1
antirequisites: N/A

title: Practice Education in Exercise Delivery
overview: This course will provide students with an opportunity to complete practice education through a professional placement relevant to the exercise and sport science areas. Placement expectations and preparation; completing a learning contract; completing a work experience logbook; practice education placement in organisations that provide exercise and sport science relevant services
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge and skills of exercise science in delivering client centred services that are within the scope of an accredited exercise scientist.
Use effective professional decision making skills and principles of evidence based practice in providing and justifying exercise based service delivery.
Use effective verbal and nonverbal communication skills in all situations as appropriate for a graduate level accredited exercise scientist.
Appropriately manage risk and safety and practice in accordance with codes of professional and ethical conduct and other policy as appropriate to the context of practice.
Demonstrate leadership through a willingness to take responsibility for professional behaviour including engagement in ongoing learning and reflective practice.
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC3050 Exercise Prescription and Delivery 1
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH3047 Practice Education in Exercise Delivery at the University of South Australia

title: Pain Mechanisms and Management
overview: The aim of this course is to develop an understanding of pain and introduce the principles of pain management within a multidisciplinary framework.
learning_outcomes: Describe the biological and psychological factors that contribute to a pain experience.
Describe the roles of the nociceptive, endocrine, immune, motor, autonomic nervous systems in the experience of pain.
Apply principles from the basic sciences to clinical examples using biopsychosocial models of engagement.
Identify the psychosocial factors that increase the risk of pain-related disability.
Formulate a collaborative multidisciplinary pain management program.
Explain pain to a layperson using jargon-free language.
antirequisites: must not have completed REHB3066 Pain Mechanisms and Management at the University of South Australia

title: Clinical Exercise Honours Project Design
overview: The aim of this course is to conceptualise and write a research or industry project plan that draws on advanced health, exercise and research understanding to address end-user needs. Writing coherent, investigable questions for either research or project; Ethical considerations of research or project work; Presentation skills; Peer review and feedback skills; Project and research designs; Research finding interpretation; Study scope and limitations; Evaluation of research/project designs; Using data bases; Endnote citation software; Academic writing; Sub-disciplines of exercise and sports science; Project resourcing.
learning_outcomes: Apply advanced health and exercise science knowledge and skills to plan a research project, which has the capacity to meet needs of the end-user.
Apply project conceptualisation and management skills to develop achievable aims and outcomes, and task scheduling.
Demonstrate an advanced capacity to critically analyse and synthesise information and communicate this in written form to suit the needs of stakeholders.
Demonstrate professional and persuasive verbal presentation skills.
Demonstrate skills in judgement and supportive critical feedback of peers' work.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of HBIO1000 Exercise Physiology 1/HLTH1016 Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Research in Health Sciences/HLTH3005 Health, Exercise and Sport Psychology/HUMV1001 Motor Development and Ageing/HUMV2002 Biomechanics of Human Movement
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH3071 Applied Exercise and Sport Science (Honours) at the University of South Australia

title: Advanced Exercise Assessment and Reasoning
overview: In this course, students will apply existing knowledge to understand a range of adverse responses to exercise testing and training and to learn the clinical skills to detect contraindications to commencing and adverse responses during exercise. Mechanisms of injury or dysfunction to musculoskeletal, neuromuscular, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory/ pulmonary, metabolic and psychological systems related to exercise testing, prescription and reasoning. Assessment and monitoring of the musculoskeletal, neuromuscular, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory/ pulmonary, metabolic and psychological systems related to exercise testing, prescription and reasoning including testing neuromuscular function, ECG testing and interpretation, point of care testing for metabolic parameters and the application of various questionnaires to assess health and function.
learning_outcomes: Discuss the absolute and relative contraindications to various types of exercise participation to determine the safety and suitability for a client to commence or continue exercise participation.

Explain the range and mechanisms of adverse responses to the musculoskeletal, neuromuscular, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory/pulmonary, metabolic and psychological systems to exercise participation.
Evaluate the health and function of the musculoskeletal, neuromuscular, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory/pulmonary, metabolic and psychological systems for exercise participation.
Explain the scope of practice of exercise, allied health and medical practitioners in monitoring and prescribing exercise.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EDUC3051 Exercise Prescription and Delivery 2/HBIO2059 Exercise Physiology 2
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH3056 Advanced Exercise Assessment and Reasoning at the University of South Australia
assessment: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions – 15%

title: Clinical Basis of Chronic Disease Management
overview: This course includes advanced application of pathophysiological bases, assessment procedures and health management approaches to target pathologies for an Accredited Exercise Physiologist (AEP). Pathophysiology and pathology, surgical and medical procedures, natural history, alleviating and aggravating factors, medical, surgical and allied health interventions for chronic disease management of AEP target pathologies. Development of clinical reasoning and knowledge synthesis skills through problem based learning.
learning_outcomes: Explain the pathophysiological basis and diagnostic procedures of Accredited Exercise Physiologist target pathologies.
Discuss stages of disease, risk factors and complications of Accredited Exercise Physiologist target pathologies.
Differentiate common surgical, medical and allied health treatments for Accredited Exercise Physiologist target pathologies.
Explain mode of action, indications, and effects of medications commonly prescribed for Accredited Exercise Physiologist target pathologies.
Access and appraise information on health conditions and their management to inform clinical decision making.
prerequisites: Must have completed HBIO2059 Exercise Physiology 2
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH4010 Clinical Basis of Chronic Disease Management at the University of South Australia

title: Clinical Studies for Exercise Physiology
overview: The aim of this course is to develop an understanding of the professional, ethical, and clinical aspects of clinical exercise physiology practice and to develop clinical skills in communication, clinical reasoning, behaviour change, exercise adherence and evidence based practice. Professionalism of the Accredited Exercise Physiologist (AEP) within the Australian healthcare system, evidence-based practice models, clinical reasoning, counselling, behavior change and self-management, approaches to long-term adherence, interpersonal communication and clinical documentation.
learning_outcomes: Perform and document subjective assessments with clients who experience chronic complex health conditions.
Communicate and liaise with clients, family, health professionals and other key stakeholders demonstrating an advanced level of interpersonal skills and social and cultural awareness.
Demonstrate clinical reasoning skills and evidence based practice in a client centered clinical environment.
Apply behavior change techniques to motivate clients to self-manage exercise and a healthy lifestyle.
Demonstrate an ability to practice in a socially and culturally sensitive manner for a diverse range of clients including Australian Aboriginal Peoples.

Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of national, state, and compensable scheme frameworks, policies and practice across the health care, aged care, and disability sectors, as they relate to the accredited exercise physiologist.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of HLTH2007 Societal Issues in Clinical Exercise Physiology/HLTH3007 Practice Education in Exercise Delivery
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH4015 Clinical Studies for Exercise Physiology at the University of South Australia

title: Musculoskeletal Evaluation and Exercise Rehabilitation
overview: This course will prepare students to deliver clinical exercise services in the area of musculoskeletal evaluation and rehabilitation as required for work, employment and activities of daily living, using the best available evidence. Contents include principles of rehabilitation, functional capacity evaluation, job task analysis, occupational performance, musculoskeletal assessment, design of exercise and conditioning programs to improve functional capacity, report writing in accordance with legislative and clinical frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of rehabilitation principles and clinical frameworks within musculoskeletal, occupational and disability settings, as they relate to an Accredited Exercise Physiologist.
Apply knowledge and skills in the evaluation of functional capacity for work, employment, ADL (Activities of Daily Living) and physical activity participation.
Demonstrate skills and knowledge in the prescription and delivery of exercise programming for musculoskeletal rehabilitation and functional conditioning.
prerequisites: must have completed all of HLTH1056 Advanced Exercise Assessment and Reasoning/HLTH4000 Clinical Basis of Chronic Disease Management/HLTH4002 Clinical Studies for Exercise Physiology
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in HLTH4001 Clinical Exercise Physiology
antirequisites: must not have completed HLTH4016 Musculoskeletal Evaluation and Exercise Rehabilitation at the University of South Australia

title: Clinical Exercise Physiology
overview: In this course, students will develop advanced knowledge and skills necessary for exercise prescription relevant assessment, development, delivery, monitoring and evaluation for individuals and groups with a range of chronic and complex conditions based on stages of disease, risk factors, complications, co-morbidities, medications, medical and allied health treatments and psychosocial factors. Exercise and pharmacological, medical and surgical treatments; assessment of clinical outcomes following exercise interventions; clinical data interpretation; risk factor stratification; assessment and monitoring of physiological responses to exercise; exercise capacity limits and thresholds; precautions and contra-indications for exercise; adverse signs of and symptoms during exercise and recovery; design of clinical exercise interventions and exercise leadership; application of communication for behaviour modification and client interaction, evidence based practice and best practice guidelines for Accredited Exercise Physiologists.
learning_outcomes: Apply appropriate assessment protocols and methodologies that are sensitive to specific sociocultural, individual and environmental contexts, for individuals with chronic and complex clinical presentations.

Design, implement and evaluate safe and effective, evidence informed exercise interventions for individuals with chronic and complex health conditions, particularly the Accredited Exercise Physiologist target pathologies.

Teach, coach and motivate clients to facilitate self-management of exercise and healthy lifestyle, using models of behaviour change, scientific evidence and clinical reasoning, and accounting for sociocultural, individual and environmental factors.
Access, evaluate and apply the best available evidence to inform practice, including adapting as required to suit complex multi-morbid clinical presentations and novel situations.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of HLTH1056 Advanced Exercise Assessment and Reasoning/HLTH4000 Clinical Basis of Chronic Disease Management/HLTH4002 Clinical Studies for Exercise Physiology
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in PSIO4002 Musculoskeletal Evaluation and Exercise Rehabilitation
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH4011 Clinical Exercise Physiology at the University of South Australia
assessment: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Report, Oral Defence – 25%

title: Health Science Honours Project
overview: In this course, students will design and undertake a professional project and disseminate the project rationale, process and outcomes to an audience both within and outside the discipline. Students will work under the guidance of a team of professional mentors to design, implement and report on a professional project of significance to their discipline. Coursework will include education on working in teams, project management and professional writing and presenting.
learning_outcomes: Identify the information and processes needed to achieve an agreed objective and design the necessary laboratory, field or computer-based investigation to obtain this, whilst complying with all relevant internal and external policy.
Justify the validity of the investigation devised, including consideration of any ethical concerns or approvals required.
Critically review and report on the process and findings of the project in a professional manner both written and oral, acceptable to a client, employer, or funding body.
Demonstrate professional planning, time management and organisational skills to complete the project on time and within budget.
Demonstrate the ability to work as a member of a professional team, displaying both leadership and self-reliance.
prerequisites: must have completed HLTH3016 Clinical Exercise Honours Project Design
antirequisites: must not have completed REHB4052 Health Science Honours Project at the University of South Australia

title: Health Science Honours Thesis
overview: The aim of this course is to execute a piece of research with some independence and to disseminate the findings of the research to an audience within and outside of the discipline of the research topic. Students will undertake and complete a research project which may be either quantitative or qualitative. Specific training and education within appropriate approaches relevant to the research project will be developed through consultation, discussion, problem-solving and liaison with more experienced researchers.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate health literacy skills by accessing, critically reviewing and synthesising literature relevant to the research project
Provide evidence of communication skills in scientific writing, which presents a clear and coherent exposition of the advantages and disadvantages of the student's chosen research methodology
Exhibit oral communication skills through a clear and coherent presentation of the student's study methodology and results to a diverse audience
Responsibly and accountably apply the principles of quality control to data collection (reliability, validity, trustworthiness, credibility, generalisability)
Provide evidence for data management and analysis as well as appropriate justification of the analysis for the research project with some independence
Critically reflect on the results, including limitations and the contribution to developing new understandings in the area of the student's research.
prerequisites: must have completed REHB3007 Health Science Honours Preparation
antirequisites: must not have completed REHB4012 Health Science Honours Thesis at the University of South Australia

title: Clinical Exercise Physiology Practicum 1
overview: This course will enable students to consolidate and apply in a practice environment the knowledge, skills and behaviours developed in the academic program. Contents include Application of knowledge and skills gained in the academic program to the practice setting. Use of self-directed online learning to explore and extend knowledge and issues that arise from the placement experience. Supervised clinical placement will be completed for conditions relating to musculoskeletal, neuromuscular/neurological, cardiopulmonary/metabolic. Clinical hours must involve direct contact with the client such as treatment, assessment, reporting, program development, case reviews and case management or training associated with specific clinical tasks
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate professional and ethical conduct consistent with the scope of practice and code of conduct for an Accredited Exercise Physiologist as defined by ESSA and any other relevant authorities.
Demonstrate skills and knowledge of best evidence based clinical exercise physiology practice.
Demonstrate skills and knowledge of best practice written and verbal communication to support collaborative practice.
Demonstrate suitable skills in interpersonal communication to facilitate client centred, socio-culturally sensitive practice that supports health behaviour change and self-management.
Demonstrate characteristics of a self-motivated learner and reflective practitioner.
prerequisites: Must have completed HLTH4000 Clinical Basis of Chronic Disease Management
corequisites: If the following courses have not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in all of HLTH4001 Clinical Exercise Physiology/PSIO4002 Musculoskeletal Evaluation and Exercise Rehabilitation
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH4012 Clinical Exercise Physiology Practicum 1 at the University of South Australia
assessment: Case Study, Learning Journal, Learning Journal, Discussion – 40%
Placement or Workplace-based Assessment, Placement or Workplace-based Assessment – 20%

title: Clinical Exercise Physiology Practicum 2
overview: This course will enable students to consolidate and apply in a practice environment the knowledge, skills and behaviours developed in the academic program. Contents include Application of knowledge and skills gained in the academic program to the practice setting. Use of self-directed online learning to explore and extend knowledge and issues that arise from the placement experience. Supervised clinical placement will be completed for conditions relating to musculoskeletal, neuromuscular / neurological, cardiopulmonary / metabolic. Clinical hours must involve direct contact with the client such as treatment, assessment, reporting, program development, case reviews and case management or training associated with specific clinical tasks.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate well-developed professional and ethical conduct consistent with the scope of practice and code of conduct for an Accredited Exercise Physiologist as defined by ESSA and any other relevant authorities.

Demonstrate well-developed technical and cognitive skills and knowledge of best evidence based clinical exercise physiology practice to support clients in managing the Accredited Exercise Physiologist target pathologies.
Demonstrate well-developed technical and cognitive skills and knowledge of best practice written and verbal communication to support collaborative well-documented practice.
Demonstrate well-developed skills in interpersonal communication to facilitate client centred, socio-culturally sensitive practice that supports health behaviour change and self-management.
Demonstrate characteristics of a self-motivated learner and reflective practitioner.
prerequisites: Must have completed PSIO4903 Clinical Exercise Physiology Practicum 1
antirequisites: Must not have completed HLTH4013 Clinical Exercise Physiology Practicum 2 at the University of South Australia
assessment: Case Study, Placement or Workplace-based Assessment, Placement or Workplace-based Assessment, Placement or Workplace-based Assessment – 40%

Contents include Application of knowledge and skills gained in the academic program to the practice setting. Use of self-directed online learning to explore and extend knowledge and issues that arise from the placement experience. Supervised clinical placement will be completed for conditions relating to musculoskeletal, neuromuscular / neurological, cardiopulmonary / metabolic.
