Create a comprehensive design project that synthesizes concepts from all modules, demonstrating proficiency in designing for manufacturability, and present the final design with a focus on professional practice and ethical considerations, evaluated through a final project presentation
prerequisites: Must have completed ARCH2005 Industrial Design Studio 4a - Production and Structures
antirequisites: Must not have completed ARCH3004 Industrial Design Production Technology

title: Industrial Design Studio 5a - Systems
overview: Industrial Design Studio 5A (Systems) introduces students to systems thinking, focusing on its application in solving complex societal, cultural, and environmental challenges. The course explores systems design methodologies and human-centred design principles for innovative problem-solving. Students will develop skills in critical thinking, systems analysis, and interdisciplinary collaboration, enhancing their ability to address intricate design issues. This course fosters a deep understanding of industrial design's impact, promotes responsible and ethical practice, and equips students with advanced problem-solving and communication skills.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate systems thinking concepts by analysing case studies of complex systems in various industries, demonstrating a thorough understanding of their relevance to industrial design, with assessments based on critical analysis and synthesis

Apply systems design methodologies and human-centred design principles to real-world scenarios, aligning system designs with user needs and experiences, developing creative solutions, evaluated through practical design projects and presentations

Develop strategies for addressing complex societal, cultural, and environmental challenges through the analysis of complex systems, identification of intervention points and feedback loops, and engagement in creative problem-solving and interdisciplinary collaboration, assessed via group projects and strategic proposal submissions

Create prototypes for systems design proposals and enhance communication skills, culminating in project presentations that include compelling narratives and visuals, while promoting responsible and ethical design practices, measured through the quality and effectiveness of prototypes and the clarity of presentations
prerequisites: Must have completed ARCH2009 Industrial Design Studio 4b - Production and Sustainability
antirequisites: Must not have completed ARCH3006 Industrial Design Studio 5a - Systems

title: Industrial Design Studio 5b - Service
overview: Industrial Design Studio 5B (Service) equips students with advanced skills in human-centered design and systems thinking to create innovative service solutions. The course covers conceptualisation, prototyping, and implementation of services that enhance user experiences and address real-world challenges across diverse industries. Students will gain practical skills and knowledge to develop impactful service designs, preparing them for professional practice in various contexts. This course fosters an understanding of the cultural and societal impact of industrial design, promoting ethical and responsible design practices while enhancing communication skills for diverse audiences.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate service design principles and systems thinking concepts by analysing successful studies and exemplars and applying the derived principles to develop innovative service solutions in various contexts, assessed through written reports, presentations, and case study analyses demonstrating critical thinking and problem-solving skills

Apply user-centred design methodologies and user experience (UX) principles by conducting user research and designing service journeys that enhance user experiences across diverse industries, assessed through project-based assignments, practical work, and oral presentations that showcase research methodologies and design processes

Develop practical skills in service design methodologies, including rapid prototyping and implementation by integrating industrial design practices and tools to produce effective service design outcomes, assessed through hands-on prototyping projects, practical demonstrations, and the use of relevant design tools

Create and present comprehensive service design projects that demonstrate advanced systems thinking, ethical and responsible design practices, and professional communication skills through compelling narratives and visuals, assessed through project-based work, team/group projects, and oral presentations that highlight the complete design process and ethical considerations
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in ARCH3006 Industrial Design Studio 5a - Systems
antirequisites: Must not have completed ARCH3015 Industrial Design Studio 5b - Service

title: Industrial Design Studio 6 - Capstone Project
overview: This capstone course extends and consolidates students' research application, integrating diverse skills and methodologies to create design solutions for complex production contexts. Through comprehensive projects, students will synthesize advanced industrial design principles, critical thinking, and practical application. They will develop innovative, socially responsible, and environmentally sustainable solutions, showcasing their technical and creative skills. The course prepares students for leadership roles in diverse professional contexts, emphasising ethical and professional practice while demonstrating the skills and knowledge learned in the Bachelor of Industrial Design program.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate product ecosystems in complex production contexts by synthesising competitor analysis and research insights to create innovative design solutions, assessed through comprehensive project reports and presentations
Integrate advanced industrial design principles and user-centred research to solve complex design problems and create innovative solutions, assessed through project submissions

Develop environmentally sustainable design solutions by analysing their life cycle impacts and demonstrating an understanding of manufacturing constraints and opportunities through concept screening and scoring, assessed via design prototypes and evaluation reports

Examine the social and ethical implications of design decisions and incorporate ethical considerations into practice by integrating leadership skills into design project management, assessed through project management plans

Create high-fidelity prototypes using advanced prototyping tools and technologies by demonstrating enhanced communication skills through compelling and coherent presentation of design ideas, assessed through prototype demonstrations

Synthesise all learned skills in the capstone project by presenting a production-ready design and defending the decisions made, demonstrating comprehensive integration of technical, creative, and professional skills, assessed through final project presentations
prerequisites: Must have completed ARCH3004 Industrial Design Production Technology OR must have completed GRAP3009 Industrial Design Production Technology AND must have completed ARCH3015 Industrial Design Studio 5b - Service OR must have completed GRAP3015 Industrial Design Studio 5b - Service
antirequisites: Must not have completed ARCH3012 Industrial Design Studio 6 - Capstone Project

title: Industrial Design Practice
overview: This course equips students with practical industrial design skills and knowledge for workplace settings. Through active participation, observation, reflection, and WIL simulations or experience, students strengthen their discipline-specific learning. By course completion, students will have gained core design concepts, ethical awareness, problem-solving skills, and effective communication abilities. The course aligns with program goals related to broad knowledge, ethical responsibility, synthesis, communication, initiative, and self-reflection.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse aesthetic contexts within industrial design projects, considering cultural influences and ethical implications
Apply core design knowledge to analyse design solutions that balance aesthetics, ergonomics, and sustainability.
Analyse and develop sustainable design responses considering environmental impact and material selection.
Effectively communicate the design and professional experience through presentations and visual communication.
Exhibit initiative and judgement in planning, problem-solving, and decision-making within professional practice.
Reflect on ethical responsibilities, accountability, and professional roles in collaborative contexts.
prerequisites: Must have completed ARCH2009 Industrial Design Studio 4b - Production and Sustainability
antirequisites: Must not have completed ARCH3002 Industrial Design Practice

title: Graphic Communication Design Studio 4
overview: This course builds on students’ understanding of design process, embedded in the design studio and its essential role in practice. Teaching and learning in the course emphasise reliance on process through investigative, analytical, iterative and evaluative methods to inform effective development of visual and typographic designs in response to briefs of increased complexity. It introduces students to the challenges of designing effective visual communication systems and platforms suitable for use in two - and three-dimensional contexts, across various media. Students are provided opportunities to develop awareness of temporal dimensions and narrative across time in the context of visual design artefacts and systems. An introduction to the concept of stakeholder engagement is offered, aiming to develop empathic and human-centred design approaches.
learning_outcomes: Research, ideate, and develop innovative design propositions to complex communication problems and scenarios using ethical practices.
Design visual communication systems and structures in response to specific briefs informed by appropriate visual and conceptual development.
Design solutions that demonstrate an understanding of narrative in visual design across media formats.
Identify and discuss appropriate stakeholders and audiences relevant to specific design contexts.
Apply skills and knowledge of visual design, typography and visual narrative to communicate effectively in multimodal, two- and three-dimensional contexts.
prerequisites: Must have completed all of GRAP1004 Digital Design Principles and Methods/GRAP1005 Typography Studio 1/GRAP2006 Graphic Communication Design Studio 3
antirequisites: Must not have completed GRAP2008 Communication Design Studio 3 at the University of South Australia

title: Problem Solving and Programming
overview: In this course you will develop core programming techniques and the problem-solving skills to translate a problem statement into a code solution.
learning_outcomes: Translate a problem statement into a code solution using problem-solving techniques.
Identify and implement the most appropriate programming construct for a programming task.
Describe the behaviour and output of programs.
Debug algorithms and programs to correct defects.
Demonstrate industry programming standards for software development.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Structured Data
overview: The course will equip students with the knowledge and skills required to implement and work with structured data in relational database systems. Through theoretical exploration and practical application, students will learn to capture data accurately, write queries to extract information, and the basics of managing data security. The topics covered will provide students with a solid foundation for real-world data management in business.
learning_outcomes: Explain how data is stored and retrieved from a relational database and the advantages of using the relational model
Design a relational database given a set of data and usage requirements
Design and implement database queries to retrieve specified data from a relational database
Explain how a query interacts with data within a relational database system and the impact design can have on management, retrieval and efficiency
Demonstrate approaches to securing data access within a database
Select for efficiency between alternative query options
antirequisites: N/A

title: Computing Innovations in the Modern World
overview: This course provides students with the skills and knowledge required to successfully implement design thinking. Through experiential learning, the course aims to develop core professional skills in project management, teamwork, ethics, presentation skills and cultural awareness.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and apply an understanding of personal attributes and team dynamics
Demonstrate communication and interpersonal skills to successfully complete a project
Apply a diverse range of Design Thinking capabilities to the creation of an ethical digital innovation
Develop a career plan and the knowledge and skills needed to gain practical work experience
Demonstrate cultural sensitivity and competency when working in Aboriginal contexts.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: A range of assignments designed to support course outcomes – 0%
Critical Analysis, Critical Analysis, Critical Analysis – 30%

title: Information Technology Systems
overview: This course aims to provide students with knowledge of essential information technology concepts and their practical applications. Throughout the course, students will explore topics including computer system modularity, internet architecture, program representation and execution, and discuss IT concepts using appropriate terminology. Additionally, students will gain hands-on experience with workplace productivity applications including word processors, spreadsheets, and presentations.
learning_outcomes: Describe and model the modular nature of computer systems
Apply internet architecture concepts, including protocols, markup languages and web programming concepts
Describe how programs are represented and executed
Discuss IT concepts using appropriate terminology, including current and future trends in IT
Use productivity applications including word processors, spreadsheets & presentations
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration – 10%

title: System Requirements
overview: This course aims to develop students' ability to follow system analysis practices to generate the system requirements for a given problem statement considering technical, human and cultural factors (including international and First Nations people).
learning_outcomes: Describe the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) and the role of requirements in the process.
Apply industry-standard modelling techniques and documentation methods to structure and validate system requirements in alignment with best practices.
Construct user profiles and use cases to assemble the requirements based on stakeholder priorities for a given problem statement.
Apply skills of collaboration, professional communication and stakeholder engagement in team-based setting for capturing and documenting the requirements.
Determine stakeholder needs considering inclusion and diversity factors, ethics and cultural sensitivities.
prerequisites: must have completed all of COMP1002 Problem Solving and Programming/INFO1012 Information Technology Systems
antirequisites: N/A

title: Security Foundations
overview: This course introduces the principal elements of cyber security from an organisational and technical perspective. The aim of the course is to provide students with the foundational knowledge to recognise potential threats and countermeasures and understand the terminology used in the cyber security field.
learning_outcomes: Explain the human, physical, technical and organisational factors impacting security
Describe the contemporary security threat landscape (threat actors, nation state)
Identify key security principles including confidentiality, reliability, and authentication
Identify technical vulnerabilities
Explain the architecture and application of digital signatures including secure e-mail, public key and assymetric key
Identify countermeasures including mitigation approaches and accepting for a given scenario
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Peer Review, Peer Review, Peer Review – 40%

title: Object-Oriented Programming
overview: This course will teach students object-oriented programming building on their imperative programming skills. Students will further develop their programming skills by studying classes, objects,  inheritance and object-oriented programming techniques. In this course they will translate a problem description into a robust object-oriented program.
learning_outcomes: Convert a problem statement into an object-oriented design
Apply object-oriented principles and techniques to solve problems
Analyse the behaviour of object-oriented programs
Develop programs using Model Driven Development
Test and debug to correct code defects
Apply industry programming standards for software development
prerequisites: must have completed COMP1002 Problem Solving and Programming
antirequisites: N/A

title: Unstructured Data
overview: This course aims to develop student capability in extracting meaning from complex unstructured data. In this course students develop skills in extracting meaning from large unstructured data sets – including data wrangling, data integration and fragmentation, unstructured databases: noSQL, document DBs, and techniques for presenting information such as visualisation.
learning_outcomes: Recommend ways to improve current processes and decision making for a given organisation using types and sources of unstructured data.
Determine the use of non-relational database architecture by considering common data storage architectures.
Propose solutions for a business problem by evaluating data technologies and tools.
Appraise the role of legal and ethical requirements in acquiring and handling unstructured data.
Apply analytic techniques to unstructured data sets.
Present data exploration and results of unstructured data analysis through data visualisation.
prerequisites: must have completed all of COMP1002 Problem Solving and Programming/COMP1003 Structured Data
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task – 15%

title: Cloud Platforms
overview: This course provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to develop and implement IT infrastructures using cloud technologies, with a focus on Amazon Web Services (AWS). By exploring cloud concepts, core services and security measures, students will be prepared to evaluate, select, and implement cloud-based solutions that align with organisational requirements.
learning_outcomes: Describe different types of cloud computing models and their applications
Compare cloud computing and traditional on-premises infrastructure
Evaluate and select cloud service offerings from major providers to meet specific organisational needs
Apply core cloud services to develop and manage a functional cloud-based IT infrastructure based on an existing on-premises design
Apply Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) technologies to design and explain a secure cloud infrastructure
Justify a cost-optimised and scalable architecture based on a real-world case
prerequisites: must have completed INFO1012 Information Technology Systems
antirequisites: N/A
assumed_knowledge: Foundational IT knowledge, basic networking, and system architecture concepts

title: Professional Communication and Teamwork
overview: This course enables students to develop skills in professional communication, teamwork, ethics, project management, and IT governance to prepare them for effective ICT practice. This course equips students with essential skills and knowledge to communicate effectively, collaborate in teams, and uphold ethical and professional standards in ICT practice. It explores principles of professional communication, teamwork, and leadership, along with key aspects of project management and IT governance. Through practical applications and case studies, students will develop the competencies required to navigate complex professional environments and contribute to successful ICT projects.
learning_outcomes: Apply effective written, verbal, and digital communication skills tailored to technical and non-technical audiences in professional ICT contexts.
Analyse ethical issues in ICT and privacy and security concerns, using established ethical frameworks and industry standards, and incorporate cultural sensitivities into ICT projects.
Apply best practices for teamwork and conflict resolution techniques to collaborate within diverse ICT projects.
Discuss the responsibilities, expectations, and professional standards of ICT practitioners, adhering to codes of conduct, industry practices and legal requirements.
Apply fundamental PMBOK project management principles to ICT projects.
Explain key IT governance frameworks and compliance requirements, and their impact on ICT decision-making and organisational success.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Data Taming and Prediction
overview: Data is all around us, but often in forms that are messy, incomplete, or difficult to interpret. This course develops foundational skills in data wrangling and analysis, focusing on transforming real-world data into tidy, structured formats suitable for exploration and predictive modelling. Students will learn to work with diverse data types and formats, apply data transformation techniques, and build and evaluate statistical and machine learning models. The course builds both technical proficiency and critical thinking to support data-informed decision making.
learning_outcomes: Describe the principles of data taming and approaches used to tidy data
Compare and critically evaluate the performance of predictive models using appropriate validation techniques and model metrics.
Select from data analysis and visualisation techniques to create a predictive model and make predictions from it
Execute techniques to transform, reduce and summarise data in order to visualise it
Communicate professionally on the application of predictive models through the use of real-world case studies
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of STAT1000 Data Skills for Scientists/STAT5020 Statistical Foundations for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 15%

title: Agile Development and User Experience
overview: This course equips students with the knowledge and skills needed to effectively apply Agile development principles using Scrum, along with Lean UX practices, to enhance the efficiency, collaboration, and user-centricity of software development projects. Participants will learn how to utilise Scrum practices and roles, as well as integrate Lean UX methodologies to streamline the design and development process. Students will also learn how to apply ethical frameworks and professional standards to project decisions and navigate difficult stakeholder interactions using professional communication and conflict management strategies. The course draws on project management principles to support the delivery of high-quality products that meet user needs and business objectives.
learning_outcomes: Apply Agile and Scrum methodologies to plan, execute, and iteratively deliver a team-based IT project, including backlog management, sprint planning, and retrospective analysis.
Demonstrate proficiency with Agile tools and practices, including story writing, estimation, velocity tracking, and stakeholder communication within the Scrum framework.
Design user experiences using Lean UX principles, incorporating iterative feedback and minimal viable product (MVP) thinking to drive customer-focused outcomes.
Employ established UX methods such as empathy mapping, persona creation, and usability evaluation to create accessible and effective user-centred designs.
Apply ethical frameworks and professional standards to assess project decisions involving user privacy, dark patterns, accessibility, and informed consent.

Manage difficult stakeholder interactions, including clients and team members, by applying professional communication strategies, conflict resolution techniques, and emotional regulation practices in a project setting.
prerequisites: must have completed INFO1013 System Requirements
antirequisites: N/A

title: Data Visualisation
overview: The aim of this course is to equip learners with the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively visualise data for the purpose of insightful analysis and impactful communication. Through a combination of theoretical concepts and practical applications, learners will enhance their ability to design clear and compelling visual narratives and leverage various tools and technologies including Python and R to transform raw data into meaningful visual representations. By the end of the course, learners will be able to critically evaluate existing, and create their own, visualisations that facilitate understanding, support decision-making, and engage diverse audiences.
learning_outcomes: Apply the fundamental concepts and principles of good data visualisation to planning and execution of a data visualisation project
Describe and critique common data visualisation approaches to discover insights from data
Create data visualisations using code based tools (e.g., ggplot2 in R)
Assess visualisations for accuracy, clarity, and potential biases, providing constructive feedback and identifying areas for improvement
Construct narrative and communicate insights from data effectively through storytelling with visualisations
prerequisites: must have completed 1 of STAT1000 Data Skills for Scientists/STAT5020 Statistical Foundations for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence/STATX100 Probability and Statistics
antirequisites: N/A

title: Behavioural Analytics and Customisation
overview: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the semantics of customer behaviour and develop skills in data visualization for impactful and meaningful representations of complex information. Content will cover the theoretical foundations of customer behaviour, as well as practical techniques for data visualization and interpretation. Students will learn to create visual representations that effectively communicate insights into customer behaviour, enabling informed decision-making in data-driven contexts. This course aligns with the overall program goal of equipping students with data analytics skills and the ability to apply them in real-world scenarios, enhancing their readiness for careers in data analysis and decision support
learning_outcomes: Describe impact of perception, motivation, attitudes, and lifestyle factors on customer behaviour
Explain customer behaviour clearly and persuasively by written and oral communication
Apply behaviour pattern recognition, optimisation, simulation and linear programming techniques to customer data
Develop predictive models from customer data to recommend strategies for nudging customer behaviour and enhance engagement
Analyse customer behaviour models to real-life business scenarios
Apply customer analytics techniques to areas such as fraud and security and credit risk
prerequisites: must have completed all of INFO1013 System Requirements/STAT1000 Data Skills for Scientists
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 30%

title: Data Governance and Privacy
overview: This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices of data governance, data confidentiality, consent, data ethics, data privacy, and data quality within the context of information technology. Throughout the course, students will explore topics such as legal frameworks for data protection, ethical considerations in data handling, industry standards, best practices, and practical implementation strategies. Through theoretical study and practical application, students will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to effectively manage data-related risks and promote responsible data Stewardship. This course aligns with the overall program goals of equipping students with the technical expertise and ethical awareness needed to succeed in the field of information technology, fostering a commitment to data integrity and privacy in their professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Describe the concepts of data privacy, governance and quality, and explain their benefits
Identify the appropriate data privacy, governance and quality frameworks, mechanisms and tools
Identify risks associated with implementing data privacy, governance and quality at an organisational level and devise strategies to mitigate those risks
Analyse data privacy, governance and quality implications for IT case studies
Criticise existing strategies to raise awareness and to embed data privacy, governance and quality into organisational operational structure
prerequisites: must have completed INFO3003 Unstructured Data
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Problem Solving Task, Multiple Choice Questions, Problem Solving Task – 20%

title: Critical Evaluation in Data Science
overview: Critical appraisal of the design, application and communication of data science.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate the use of basic probability to solve word problems
Critically analyse and improve data collection designs
Compose appropriate graphics to visualise patterns in data
Articulate the importance of statistics in modern scientific research

title: Network Foundations

The course will use a top-down approach to study computer networks by taking the Internet and its protocol stack as the primary examples to illustrate fundamental principles. Introduction to networks with a focus on Internet protocols: Application layer protocols (HTTP-web, SMTP-mail, etc), Transport layer operation: (reliable transport, congestion, and flow control, UDP, TCP); Network layer operations (routing, addressing, IPv4 and IPv6), Data Link layer operations (error detection/correction, access control, Ethernet, 802.11).

title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
overview: The course employs theories, concepts and methods of Comparative Politics to compare and contrast the political systems of major global powers, including the United States, China, India and Russia. Through the analysis of case studies, students are expected to evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of democratic and authoritarian systems, parliamentary and (semi)presidential systems and unitary and federal systems. They should also be able to reflect upon broad issues such as nation- and state-making, colonization, political economy and political culture. The course provides students with a rigorous analytical framework for addressing critical domestic challenges facing major global powers, preparing them to navigate practical and moral dilemmas facing policymakers worldwide and encouraging them to reflect on their values and biases when evaluating policy making.
learning_outcomes: Identify and apply the major approaches and concepts in Comparative Politics.

title: Australia’s Foreign Policy in the Indo-Pacific
overview: This course introduces students to Australia's foreign and security policies and the key domestic and international debates that shape them. It focuses on Australia's interests in its primary area of geostrategic focus, the Indo-Pacific, which bridges the Pacific and Indian Oceans. Using theoretical approaches from both International Relations and Foreign Policy Analysis, this course aims to equip students to critically analyse the challenges and opportunities open to Australia when pursuing its foreign and security interests in this region. Students will examine the concept of the Indo-Pacific, considering whether it describes a coherent strategic, economic and cultural region and questioning why Australia has chosen to focus its strategic policy on this region. They will then consider the interests of key regional powers, including the United States, China, Japan, India and Indonesia, as well as key regions, the Pacific Islands and Southeast Asia, and evaluate how these affect Australia’s interests. The non-traditional and transnational dimensions of security will also be examined, including terrorism, piracy, transnational crime, human security and environmental challenges. Students who successfully complete this course will be able to critically examine how Australian foreign and security policy is made and how Australia pursues its interests in the Indo-Pacific and beyond.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of Australia’s foreign and security policies and the key domestic and international debates that shape them
Understand and use theoretical approaches from both International Relations and Foreign Policy Analysis
Critically evaluate how Australian foreign and security policy is made based on research of primary and secondary sources
Communicate their analysis of Australian foreign and security policy in written and verbal forms to diverse audiences

This course explores these and other related themes, including global political dynamics and policy responses, to provide a comprehensive picture of the post Covid-19 state of the world. The course provides students with a variety of conceptual and analytical tools to interpret and assess the global and multidimensional impact of the Covid-19 pandemic, enhancing their ability to navigate and analyse international systems and policies, and develop the capacity to address global challenges.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a broad picture of the current state of the world
Identify and discuss major post-Covid-19 global challenges
