Pedagogies of inclusion in Languages education, and an introduction to the Australian Curriculum: Languages, including the Framework for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Languages; first, background and additional languages; and Auslan, are investigated and used for planning teaching and learning. The course underpins critical learning pathways aimed at addressing social inequity and shaping a positive future for our state, nation and the world.
learning_outcomes: Explain the knowledge and skills required to work effectively and inclusively with learners with diverse languages and cultures backgrounds and perspectives
Plan curriculum, assessment, and evaluation of learning using curriculum frameworks and evidence-based pedagogical practices relevant to learners of diverse languages backgrounds
Interpret and implement knowledge of culturally responsive teaching that respects and values the rights of Aboriginal children and the sovereignties of Aboriginal First Nations through education
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Design Project – 30%

title: Inclusive Education and Responsive Teaching in Early Years
overview: This course aims to develop critical knowledge and practices in inclusive education to provide for special educational needs of learners of all abilities. It will investigate inclusion strategies, policies and legislation, exceptionality, neurodiversity, partnerships with providers, and person-centred planning and advocacy.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate awareness and application of the principles of inclusive education in early childhood/primary/secondary classrooms and school settings
Demonstrate understandings of the characteristics of students that make up classroom diversity and adopt pedagogical approaches to address such diversity in the mainstream classroom
Demonstrate an understanding of legislation, regulations, policies and obligations related to inclusion including international agreements and legal entitlements
Select from and use a wide range of evidence-based pedagogical approaches to cater for specific needs and disabilities
antirequisites: N/A

title: Learning about Reading in Early Years
overview: This course aims to prepare students to understand developmental stages in learning to read, and teaching and assessing reading in the early years' settings, utilising a range of methods and approaches including phonics-based learning and meaning making strategies, incorporating multimodalities and catering to diverse learner groups with a range of language backgrounds.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of key concepts and metalanguage in theories of reading development and for children to learn to read proficiently and purposefully with increasingly complex texts from a range of modes/contexts.

Demonstrate appropriate subject matter expertise in the effective teaching of literacy, including the explicit teaching of phonological awareness and phonics in early reading, and the explicit teaching of reading and connection to early writing behaviours.
Plan for teaching informed by an understanding of theories and key concepts and of a range of pedagogical strategies including, modelled, dialogic, explicit instruction, embodied and arts based.
Analyse texts in terms of their structural and linguistic features and consider strategies for improving word knowledge, meaning making and comprehension.

Interpret evidence of reading to form judgements about children's reading development and achievement and inform planning for teaching and learning that is responsive to students of diverse groups including to EAL/D and First Nations students.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Learning about Literacies and Text Production in Early Years
overview: This course aims to introduce and examine early literacy theories and practices and multimodal literature for children of diverse backgrounds and experiences, including in English and multicultural and multilingual contexts, and to develop skills in the areas of multimodal text production for children in the early years. Students will learn to use quality literature and writing processes to support learning about literary and imaginative writing.
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC2107 Learning about Reading in Early Years
antirequisites: N/A

title: Exploring Mathematics through Play
overview: This course aims to introduce pedagogical approaches appropriate for assisting young learners to engage in mathematical inquiry and learning, building on their current knowledge and ways they understand mathematical concepts in their everyday play-based activities.
learning_outcomes: Plan for and implement learning experiences using the Early Years Learning Framework
Analyse how young children develop mathematical understanding through play, including multi-modal expressions in revealing children’s mathematical thinking and understandings
Analyse and utilise a wide range of resources, including the use of multi-modal tools and pedagogical documentation to support young children’s mathematical understandings
Demonstrate subject matter expertise in the effective teaching of numeracy, including building fluency, understanding, problem-solving, and reasoning
antirequisites: N/A

title: Humanities and Social Science Education in Early Years
overview: This course introduces the Humanities and Social Sciences (HASS) learning area through the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum: HASS. The course explores how the subjects of history, geography, civics and citizenship and economics and business build the capacity of young people to make sense of their world and participate as active citizens in their everyday lives and into the future.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the curriculum frameworks that underpin the Humanities and Social Science learning area
Knowledge of and skill in planning and sequencing content and tasks so that they become increasingly challenging and incorporate spacing and retrieval practices
Use curriculum frameworks and a wide variety of evidence-based teacher resources to plan inclusive learning experiences in Humanities and Social Sciences
Effectively select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning
Understand and use key Humanities and Social Sciences concepts as they relate to the curriculum frameworks to plan learning experiences that are inclusive of all learners
Critique evidence-based resources that support student engagement and learning while highlighting the importance of student questions within the learning area
antirequisites: N/A

title: Languages Education in Early Years
overview: This course aims to explore pedagogies for working with children from different language backgrounds and working with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the Australian Curriculum: Languages to support teachers of languages and the teaching of languages in early childhood and primary settings.
learning_outcomes: Identify the languages and cultures knowledges children and young people bring to learning sites, their relationship to concepts of self, identity, community and place, and how these impact learning

Analyse languages education policy, frameworks and curricula, including the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the Australian Curriculum: Languages to support learners’ plurilingual capabilities and languages inclusion in classrooms and sites
Apply strategies and pedagogies to promote language development and learning in linguistically and culturally diverse sites, centres and classrooms
antirequisites: N/A

title: Health and Physical Education in Early Years
overview: This course aims to support students to understand how educational psychology and the theories of learning relate to contemporary teaching practices and incorporate this knowledge into their teaching and learning strategies.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the benefits and role of physical activity in children's health and development as well as how biases and assumptions about diverse groups and worldviews affect practices, behaviours, and attitudes to movement and physical activity
Understand and apply range of skills, competencies, knowledge and intercultural development to achieve positive outcomes in the HPE learning area
Identify and apply principles of practice, planning and cultural diversity for physical, cognitive, social and affective learner outcomes in lesson plans
Understand, create and maintain safe, inclusive and developmental learning environments in HPE learning episodes including the valuing of diverse groups including EAL/D and First Nations students
Appraise and critically self-reflect on a model of culturally, socially and physically inclusive practice with the intention to apply these in a practical way

Present and reflect on effective learning experiences in Health and Physical Education for peers and pre-school or school students and engage in critical self-inquiry as a core process for of effective ongoing professional teaching practice
antirequisites: N/A

title: Science and Technologies for Young Children
overview: The aim of this course is to enable students to synthesise current information in science and technology to provide an appropriate program for children aged birth to five years.
learning_outcomes: Discuss and critique contemporary approaches to the design of science and technology learning pertinent to early childhood
Demonstrate an understanding of science pedagogical content knowledge specific to early childhood education
Demonstrate syntheses of knowledge of the processes of working scientifically and plan opportunities for related thinking skill development
Use a variety of observational assessment practices to identify and respond to children's thinking and conceptual understanding
antirequisites: N/A

title: Contemporary Issues, Theories and Practices in Early Childhood Education
overview: This course develops understanding of dominant historical discourses in the field of early childhood education, and introduces multiple perspectives on theory, research and practice as alternative discourses and pedagogical approaches.
learning_outcomes: Extend existing understandings of childhood taking into account how these understandings developed at different historical periods
Critically analyse the historical development of understandings of childhood, how we know about children, and how these understandings resonate in contemporary Australian contexts
Identify contemporary theories that have shaped and continue to shape understandings of children and childhood, diversity, difference and inclusivity

Apply critical, post-structural, feminist and post-human theoretical understandings to critically analyse, reflect and design inclusive professional practice in early childhood care and education settings
Apply knowledge of contemporary theories to respond to contemporary issues in early childhood education concerning equity and social inclusion
antirequisites: N/A

title: Professional Experience 3: Early Childhood Birth to 5
overview: This professional experience course builds capacities for working effectively within an education setting for children prior to schooling.
learning_outcomes: Build effective professional relationships and dispositions with children, families, colleagues and other professionals in an early years setting
Apply knowledge and skills with creativity, initiative and a high level of personal autonomy, accountability and respect while working and leading in a team setting

Apply an advanced body of knowledge of contemporary theories and practice as they engage with curriculum documents, children, families, colleagues, community and other professionals to implement democratic inquiry-based pedagogies in an early years setting
Design and evaluate the use of pedagogical documentation to demonstrate children's learning and provide evidence of developing practices as a teacher

Demonstrate developing capacity to exercise aspects of leadership which demonstrate a commitment to collaborative leadership and teamwork and evaluate their own skills and knowledge relevant to early childhood leadership theory and practice

Reflect on teaching and learning experiences in the light of professional standards, policies, legal and ethical guidelines for the profession and developing beliefs of the role of early-years educators
prerequisites: must have completed all of EDUC1900 Professional Experience 1: Early Childhood Infant and Toddler/EDUC2900 Professional Experience 2: Early Childhood Preschool
antirequisites: N/A

title: Dance and Music, Social Dreaming
overview: This course aims to support students towards their future role as an arts educator by deepening and extending subject knowledge of traditional and contemporary dance and music education. Working with dance and music pedagogies students will gain mastery of these subjects for the primary school learning environment with a focus on the changing nature of dance and music education and its impact on diverse young people in the community.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the role and function of Dance and Music in diverse contemporary communities and their impact on young people
Identify traditional and contemporary approaches to Dance and Music in curriculum decision making and research
Experience and critically reflect on the intrinsic and instrumental value of dance and music in the curriculum
Apply current and appropriate pedagogies for Dance and Music
Identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Dance and Music as intrinsic to Australian cultural knowledge, understanding and communication
Demonstrate reflective practice in working as an active teacher/artist educator
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: A range of assignments designed to support course outcomes – 50%

title: Developing Number Sense
overview: The aim of the course is to develop the mathematical skills and knowledge for teaching mathematics in the primary years of schooling, with a focus on number and developing number sense. This course will focus on developing subject-matter knowledge relevant for Primary mathematics, focusing on mathematical concepts, identifying facts, rules, and relationships in and between these concepts. The content in this course is drawn from the 'Number' content strand of the Australian Curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Select and apply a range of mathematical representations and strategies to solve problems, with a focus on number
Demonstrate appropriate use of a range of tools, including digital technologies, to enable, enhance and extend mathematical understanding in number
Communicate mathematical thinking and reasoning in spoken, written and visual modes
Reflect on and enhance their own mathematical development
antirequisites: Must not have completed MATH1057 Mathematics for Primary Educators 1 at the University of South Australia
assessment: Interactive Questions, Interactive Questions, Interactive Questions – 30%

title: Arts Across the Early Childhood Curriculum
overview: To enable students to design, apply and evaluate arts across the curriculum for children from Birth to 8 years.
learning_outcomes: Create a diverse and balanced arts program appropriate for particular age groups/groupings particular age groups/groupings
Employ a range of arts resources to enhance children's learning experiences in and through the arts curriculum decision making
Apply and explain principles and processes of learning in and through the arts across the curriculum experience in the arts
Describe and discuss children's creative and aesthetic development
antirequisites: N/A

title: Artificial Intelligence in Education and Training
overview: This course aims to equip students with the knowledge and skills to understand, use, and apply artificial intelligence ethically and effectively in a range of educational settings.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of how artificial intelligence functions, its benefits and limitations
Use and apply artificial intelligence for learning and teaching ethically and responsibly
Critically appraise artificial intelligence for supporting learning and teaching
antirequisites: N/A

title: Learners in a Digital Age: Innovative Practices
overview: To critically analyse current global trends in learning with digital technologies.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the impact of digital technology on learners and learning
Analyse a range of contemporary technologies and the trends of development
Analyse how social justice is impacted by technology
antirequisites: N/A

title: Islamic Education: Principles and Praxis
overview: To foster a deep epistemic reflexivity about the need for renewal in Islamic schools. This course centres meta-purpose for Islamic school settings and grounds students in Islamic Pedagogy as a distinct philosophy of education. To examine theories, principles and philosophies of Islamic education as they inform Islamic pedagogy and evaluate the implications for diverse approaches to quality teaching and learning for Muslim students in contemporary classrooms.
learning_outcomes: Explore and critically analyse the relationship between ontology and epistemology and conceptions of education
Critically compare and situate the meta purpose embedded within philosophies of Islamic education to contemporary approaches to Islamic schooling
Engage in epistemic reflexivity aligning what we believe about education with how we educate in Islamic school settings
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC5262 Islamic Pedagogy Principles and Praxis at the University of South Australia

title: Geographical Studies
overview: To develop a deep, conceptual and foundational content knowledge in geographical studies through exploring the concepts and content and skills of the Australian Curriculum: Geography. To develop the capacity to think geographically through geographical concepts and key content areas that underpin the geography curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of geography as a discipline within the HaSS curriculum Foundation to Year 6.
Apply geographical skills of spatial analysis and mapping and undertake quality geographical fieldwork
Apply geographical concepts and thinking to analyse and interpret the world through a geographical lens
Evaluate a geographical challenge related to physical and human environments that involves geographical knowledge, understanding and decision-making skills.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Becoming an Educator with an Arts Specialisation
overview: This course aims to develop deep understanding of traditional, contemporary and emerging arts content and practices, their application to the curriculum and the role/s of a generalist primary school teacher with an arts curriculum specialisation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the role and function of the arts in diverse contemporary communities and their impact upon young people
Identify traditional and contemporary approaches to the arts in curriculum decision making and research
Experience creative body-based learning in physical, digital and virtual spaces
Apply current approaches to technology in working with digital and media arts
Identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander arts as intrinsic to Australian histories and cultural knowledge
Articulate the intrinsic and instrumental value of visual arts, media arts, dance, drama and music in the school curriculum
Demonstrate reflective practice in working as an active teacher/artist educator with young people
antirequisites: N/A

title: Catholic Scriptures: An Introduction
overview: To examine the Christian Scriptures (First Testament and Second Testament) as literature and as sacred texts, while critically analysing methods of Scriptural interpretation and the Catholic pedagogical applications of the Scripture studied. This entails the application of the ‘Three Worlds of the Text’ approach to the study of these sacred texts, with an emphasis on teaching the genres, contexts and contemporary interpretations of the focus texts.
learning_outcomes: Apply the ‘Three Worlds of the Text’ approach to interpreting biblical texts, with a focus on genre, context and contemporary meaning-making in Catholic education
Analyse and apply the major theological themes of the First Testament especially as expressed in the Books of Genesis and Exodus
Evaluate the importance of the Jewish context of the life of Jesus and of the early Christian communities
Analyse the theology of the Gospel of Matthew and its portrayal of Jesus as prophet, teacher and Messiah
antirequisites: N/A

title: Catholic Theology: An Introduction
overview: To introduce students to the active process of 'doing theology' in the Catholic tradition, in educational settings, through the critical examination of core theological topics that bring contemporary human experience, questions and challenges into personal, communal and global dialogue with this Catholic tradition.
learning_outcomes: Engage in contextual theological reflection, analysis and dialogue through the articulation of questions, discussion and personal interaction with the Catholic theological tradition
Analyse contemporary Christology and the ‘person and work’ of Christ; and pedagogical applications

Apply Catholic theological perspectives to the pedagogies and priorities of Catholic schools, in the context of critical educational challenges (for example: ecological conversion, Gospel justice, consumerism, human sexuality education)
Analyse the development of Christian theologies and language about God in their historical contexts, with a focus on educational implications
antirequisites: N/A

title: Design and Production 1
overview: This course will introduce and develop an understanding of the use of computer aided design (CAD) software packages to visualise and design solutions in order to produce designs into a physical project through the use of laser cutting, 3D printing or CNC machining. Pre-service teachers will develop their expertise in operating state of the art machinery and maintaining best workshop practices. Additionally, students are introduced to sustainability in design and production processes while ensuring all practices meet WHS requirements.
learning_outcomes: Apply a design process to research, design and develop innovative products using sustainable materials, processes, technologies and systems
Identify the specific characteristics, properties and appropriate usage of various types of materials and composite materials
Apply WHS knowledge to competently and safely operate a range of state-of-the-art digital equipment as well as hand and power tools and machines to realise products in tangible materials
Apply critical thinking in evaluating products in terms of design, materials and systems production
antirequisites: N/A

title: Food Technology 1
overview: This course aims to introduce preservice teachers to the skills, knowledge and professional expertise associated with teaching and learning in design and technologies food specialisms, in both primary and middle school settings, with a strong focus on integrating both the theoretical and practical aspects of food technologies .
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the latest technologies and design principles in planning and developing relevant and engaging food technology lessons in line with the Australian Curriculum
Identify the societal influences on food production and food choices
Exhibit and critically analyse food preparation and production techniques when designing solutions suitable for primary and middle school classrooms
Apply WHS knowledge in identifying and applying food safety and hygiene practices, as well as safe use of tools and equipment in the food technology classroom
antirequisites: N/A

title: Teaching Linguistically Diverse Learners
overview: This course aims to equip students with theoretical understandings and pedagogical strategies needed to teach learners of English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EALD). Students will enhance their understanding of EALD learners and their learning in mainstream classes; develop pedagogical strategies and assessments; and create resources to support EALD students to access and engage with learning areas across the curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the linguistic, cultural and learning needs of linguistically diverse learners
Analyse the linguistic demands of their teaching context
Critically investigate an approach to teaching linguistically diverse learners in the context of language acquisition research
Evaluate and justify the selection of a range of strategies for making learning accessible to linguistically diverse learners
antirequisites: N/A

title: Teaching and Learning Languages
overview: This course introduces pedagogies and knowledges of languages learning for all languages courses.
learning_outcomes: Understand languages as a theorised field of education for diverse learners and learning contexts
Critically engage with languages curricula for diverse learners
Utilise contemporary perspectives in planning to teach and assess languages learning
antirequisites: N/A

title: Historical Studies
overview: This course aims to develop a deep, conceptual and foundational content knowledge in historical studies through exploring the content and skills of the Australian Curriculum: History. Students will develop the capacity to think historically through historical concepts and key content areas that underpin the history curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply knowledge of the Australian Curriculum: History to plan relevant and engaging learning experiences and quality assessment
Apply historical research skills and demonstrate an ability to think historically in a conceptual and critical manner
Think historically through applying the historical concepts
Understand the pedagogical content knowledge involved in the teaching of HaSS: History
antirequisites: N/A

title: Teaching in Rural and Regional Locations
overview: To build on students' prior professional experiences in education sites and schools and to prepare future graduates for the challenges and opportunities of teaching in rural/regional communities.
learning_outcomes: Understand the rural social space and develop a professional empathy about the implications for rural and regional education
Investigate historical and contemporary issues and policies related to educational provision, specifically with regard to the employment and retention of teachers in rural and regional contexts

Critique of strategies related to how to work collaboratively with colleagues, school support staff, other professionals and community-based personnel to enhance student learning outcomes and wellbeing in rural and regional communities
Explore the opportunities and challenges of teaching in rural and regional contexts particularly in relation to leadership in the school and wider community
Select strategies to work and live productively in a rural or regional context with an appreciation of the significance of place
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Critical Analysis – 40%

title: Teaching Learners with Disabilities
overview: This course aims to develop an awareness and understanding of the types of disabilities of children and young people in Early Childhood, Primary, Secondary schools and special and inclusive settings, and the impact of these disabilities. It further aims to provide the knowledge, resources and strategies to teach and support children with disabilities in any educational sector or school accommodating their right to inclusive education.
learning_outcomes: Identify the need for early identification, intervention and family support for learners with disabilities
Describe the characteristics of particular disabilities and the awareness of diagnostic strategies relevant to addressing them
Implement care, curriculum and teaching/program modifications and reasonable adjustments for learners with disabilities in mainstream and special settings
Critically evaluate the practices which support the successful inclusion of learners with disabilities in school settings
Discuss the current national and international issues concerning the care and education of children with disabilities through an inclusive and special education lens
antirequisites: N/A

title: Learning About Language
overview: The course aims to develop students understanding of theories of language, including developmental theory, sociocultural theory, semiotic theory and systemic functional linguistics.
learning_outcomes: Explain the connections between language, culture, identity and home and community languages
Understand and explain the implications of culturally sustaining and expanding pedagogies to support and value plurilingualism and variation in language learning
Explain that language learning, language development and language practices are influenced by sociocultural contexts, through a functional model of language
Analyse and apply the levels of language (sounds, words, grammar and sentences, register and genre) to texts in various modes to inform teaching
Apply a functional theory of language development and its implications for educational settings
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX105 Learning About Language OR must not have completed EDUC3073 Mathematics Education 1 at the University of South Australia

title: Languages Education
overview: This course aims to explore pedagogies for working with children from different language backgrounds and working with the Australian Curriculum: Languages to support teachers of languages and the teaching of languages in early childhood and primary settings.
learning_outcomes: Identify the languages and cultures knowledges children and young people bring to learning sites, their relationship to concepts of self, identity, community and place, and how these impact learning

Analyse languages education policy, frameworks and curricula, including the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF) and the Australian Curriculum: Languages to support learners’ plurilingual capabilities and languages inclusion in classrooms and sites
Apply strategies and pedagogies to promote language development and learning in linguistically and culturally diverse sites, centres and classrooms
antirequisites: N/A

title: Technologies Education
overview: This course introduces and builds understanding of the Technologies Curriculum to assist students to plan, implement and assess using the Australian Curriculum: Technologies Learning Area.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge and understanding of the Australian Curriculum to design learning sequences specific to the technologies curriculum in various contexts
Demonstrate and justify a range of pedagogical approaches appropriate to design and technologies education
Select, and use resources appropriate to design and technologies
Plan, enact and reflect on a learning experience
Effectively select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC1018 Design and Technology Education at the University of South Australia

title: The Brain and Learning
overview: The aim of this course is to understand how the brain functions and how we learn to better inform teaching practice. The course addresses short and long-term memory, cognitive load, and knowledge processing as well as retrieval and application strategies. The course will also bust a range of neuromyths and common misconceptions in brain research. By the end, students will have a solid understanding of brain processes and optimised learning strategies for teacher education, enhancing their ability to design effective learning experiences.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate Knowledge of what it means to be a ‘novice’ learner in comparison to an ‘expert’ learner
Demonstrate knowledge of the most efficient and effective process of knowledge acquisition in the brain, including the function of memory and the concept of cognitive overload
Explain the process that occurs in a novice brain during progression towards mastery
Demonstrate knowledge of and skill in the need to adjust practice in response to novice and mastery processes
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of common neuromyths and the impact of their perpetuation on education practice
antirequisites: Must not have completed PSYCX200 at a grade of at least The Brain and Learning from the University of South Australia
assessment: Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions, Multiple Choice Questions – 36%

title: Health and Physical Education
overview: This course introduces content knowledge and inclusive pedagogical practices for the Health and Physical Education learning area.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate the benefits and role of physical activity in children's health and development as well as how biases and assumptions about diverse groups and worldviews affect practices, behaviours, and attitudes to movement and physical activity
Understand and apply range of skills, competencies, knowledge and intercultural development to achieve positive outcomes in the HPE learning area
Identify and apply principles of practice, planning and cultural diversity for physical, cognitive, social and affective learner outcomes in lesson plans
Understand, create and maintain safe, inclusive and developmental learning environments in HPE learning episodes including the valuing of diverse groups including EAL/D and First Nations students
Appraise and critically self-reflect on a model of culturally, socially and physically inclusive practice with the intention to apply these in a practical way

Present and reflect on effective learning experiences in Health and Physical Education for peers and pre-school or school students and engage in critical self-inquiry as a core process for of effective ongoing professional teaching practice
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX421 Health and Physical Education OR must not have completed EDUC2006 Health and Physical Education at the University of South Australia
assessment: Skills Demonstration, Skills Demonstration, Professional Simulation – 50%

title: Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher
overview: This course aims to support preservice teachers to develop a professional identity. They will learn about the role of the teacher in the 21st century and explore how this is articulated within frameworks, such as the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers and the Teacher Registration Board’s code of conduct. Preservice teachers will then be expected to act professionally as they engage in their first placement in schools. Key pedagogies, along with the learning theories that underpin them, will be explored. Preservice Teachers will then critically reflect on the pedagogies that they observe while on placement.
learning_outcomes: Reflect on the value of dispositions, attributes, knowledge and skills valued by the teaching profession in the 21st century and articulate their significance for effective and ethical teaching practice.
Identify a range of key pedagogies for student learning and explain how they are grounded in relevant learning theories.
Research and analyse the context of a site and its community to justify choices about key pedagogies for student learning
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC1081 Professional Experience 1 Introduction to Educators' Practices at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed EDUC1100 Introduction to Teaching and Learning at the University of Adelaide

title: Digital Literacy and Artificial Intelligence for Learning and Societal Change
overview: This course aims to equip learners with the knowledge and skills to critically evaluate digital resources and tools and use them effectively for learning. This course involves a practical exploration of how the digital and AI literacies central to modern societal practices are transforming the ways in which we gather and process information and delves into how they can enhance the ways in which we communicate ethically and safely. By examining the issues around these practices, learners will develop the critical thinking and technical skills necessary to create impactful learning environments.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate the utility of digital tools for learning
Select and apply appropriate digital and AI tools for learning
Analyse the ethical and societal issues around the use of digital and AI tools
Create resources that effectively leverage digital and AI tools for learning
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Critical Analysis, Critical Analysis, Critical Analysis – 45%

title: Science Education
overview: To introduce students to key constructs associated with how children learn science as the basis for planning and assessing disciplinary-based learning experiences across the primary years of schooling. Students will develop an understanding of inquiry-based and social constructivist perspectives of learning. Students will investigate current pedagogies, thinking and working scientifically and make links with other curriculum areas. Students will confidently and capably plan, implement and evaluate a unit of work in science that supports the building of inquiry skills, builds understanding of science concepts (embedded in biology, chemistry, earth and space and/or physical sciences) and makes connections to real-world context.
learning_outcomes: Describe key aspects of thinking and working scientifically and the role of scientific inquiry in planning for learning

Design a sequence of science learning experiences that incorporate a range of pedagogical strategies to engage learners in thinking and working scientifically, and to build and assess understanding across all three strands of the Australian Curriculum: Science
Develop, select, and use a range of resources, including digital resources, for teaching and assessing children’s scientific understanding
Understand explicit teaching, modelling and scaffolding practices and explain how these support how a student’s brain learns
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX222 Science Education OR must not have completed EDUC2030 Science Education at the University of South Australia

title: Humanities and Social Science Education
overview: This course introduces the Humanities and Social Sciences (HASS) learning area through the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum: HASS. The course explores how the subjects of history, geography, civics and citizenship and economics and business build the capacity of young people to make sense of their world and participate as active citizens in their everyday lives and into the future.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the curriculum frameworks that underpin the Humanities and Social Science learning area
Knowledge of and skill in planning and sequencing content and tasks so that they become increasingly challenging and incorporate spacing and retrieval practices
Use curriculum frameworks and a wide variety of evidence-based teacher resources to plan inclusive learning experiences in Humanities and Social Sciences
Effectively select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning
Understand and use key Humanities and Social Sciences concepts as they relate to the curriculum frameworks to plan learning experiences that are inclusive of all learners
Critique evidence-based resources that support student engagement and learning while highlighting the importance of student questions within the learning area
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC1902 Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX313 Humanities and Social Science Education

title: Learning About Reading
overview: This course prepares students to understand developmental stages in learning to read and to teach reading in the early years settings, utilising a range of methods and approaches including phonics-based learning and meaning making strategies, incorporating multimodalities and catering to diverse learner groups with a range of language backgrounds.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of key concepts and metalanguage in theories of reading development and for children to learn to read proficiently and purposefully with increasingly complex texts from a range of contexts

DDemonstrate appropriate subject matter expertise in the effective teaching of literacy, including the explicit teaching of phonics in early reading and the explicit teaching of reading and writing in subjects other than English

Plan for teaching informed by an understanding of theories and key concepts and of a range pedagogical strategies including, modelled, dialogic, embodied explicit instruction, modelled, dialogic, embodied and arts based
Analyse texts in terms of their structural and linguistic features and consider strategies for supporting meaning-making and comprehension
Interpret evidence of reading to form judgements about children's reading development and achievement and inform planning for teaching and learning
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX215 Learning About Reading OR must not have completed EDUC2058 English Curriculum at a grade of at least Reading at the University of South Australia

title: Mathematics Education 1
overview: The aim of the course is to develop an understanding of the goals, purposes and strategies for teaching mathematics in the primary years of schooling and build students capacity to plan, resource and teach conceptually developmental mathematical learning experiences. Students will examine the nature of specialised content knowledge for teaching mathematics, and pedagogical practices appropriate for primary mathematics. This course focuses on planning mathematical learning experiences with a clear emphasis on learning intentions, success criteria and formative assessment.
learning_outcomes: Unpack mathematics curriculum content descriptors by identifying key mathematical concepts, relevant terminology, and creating aligned learning intentions with appropriate success criteria
Plan learning experiences and sequences that align with relevant curriculum framework
Select, critique and apply strategies for teaching mathematics in the primary years such as explicit teaching, modelling and scaffolding practices
Select, evaluate, and use a range of resources to engage students in learning mathematics
Plan and sequence content and tasks so that they become increasingly challenging and incorporate spacing and retrieval practice
prerequisites: If undertaking HTPRI Bachelor of Teaching (Primary) (Honours) THEN must have completed EDUC1902 Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX106 Mathematics Education 1 OR must not have completed EDUC3073 Mathematics Education 1 at the University of South Australia

title: Classroom Management in Primary Contexts
overview: The aim of this course is to develop the knowledge, skills, and attitudes to support students to foster positive and safe learning environments by proactively supporting productive student behaviours. This course places creating positive learning environments as an essential pillar of the teaching and learning process.
learning_outcomes: A strong understanding of the role of rules and routines in establishing a structured, safe, and positive classroom environment
A clear understanding of the efficacy of proactive practices in preventing misbehaviour and/or disengagement, including the role of high-quality instruction as a proactive practice

An ability to practise and apply proactive practices, including setting high expectations, building positive relationships, providing structure, and setting ambitious, achievable and personalised goals

An ability to practise and apply techniques that positively and effectively manage behaviour in classroom contexts, including the use of calm, consistent and proportional responses, behaviour modelling and feedback that gives attention to the desired behaviour rather than the undesired behaviour
A foundational understanding of common whole-school behaviour frameworks
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC1902 Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher
antirequisites: N/A

title: Professional Experience 2: Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment
overview: This course supports preservice teachers to develop the knowledge, skills, and professional judgement required to plan, teach, assess, and reflect on learning in Australian school contexts. Throughout the course, preservice teachers will explore how curriculum, learner needs, school context, observation, and assessment inform responsive planning and teaching. During professional experience, they will apply these understandings to support student learning, participation, and wellbeing while continuing to develop their confidence and capability as beginning teachers.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of current school contexts to lesson planning
Sequence learning within and across lessons and evaluate the effectiveness
Use strategies to build positive relationships and classroom management practices effectively
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC1902 Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher AND if undertaking HTPRI Bachelor of Teaching (Primary) (Honours) THEN must have completed EDUCX215 Learning About Reading AND must have completed EDUC1008 Classroom Management in Primary Contexts OR if undertaking HTSEC Bachelor of Teaching (Secondary) (Honours) THEN must have completed  EDUC1119 Classroom Management in Secondary Contexts/as well as at least Curriculum 1 in Major Learning areas, and a minimum of two courses in major discipline area
antirequisites: N/A

title: Effective Pedagogical Practices for Primary Contexts
overview: This course prepares pre-service teachers for teaching by equipping them with knowledge of and skills in effective planning, sequencing of content and tasks, explicit teaching, formative and summative assessment, and feedback practices for Primary contexts. The course also emphasises understanding how children learn, the use of brain-based strategies for instruction, and the design of tasks and assessments that foster long-term retention and mastery.
learning_outcomes: Plan and sequence instruction that aligns with curriculum goals, progressively challenges students, and incorporates strategies such as spacing, retrieval practice, and differentiation to meet diverse student needs.

Understand and apply a range of pedagogical practices, including explicit teaching, modelling and scaffolding practices, to support student learning, promote deep understanding, and minimise cognitive load.
Effectively select and use a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, provide targeted feedback, adjust instruction, and support learning.
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC1005 Learning About Language OR must have completed EDUC5005 Language and Learning AND must have completed EDUC1008 Classroom Management in Primary Contexts OR must have completed EDUC6013 Primary Mathematics Education 1
antirequisites: N/A

title: Professional Experience 3: Planning, Teaching and Assessing for Diversity
overview: This course explores differentiation practices for supporting the varied needs of learners. Preservice teachers will learn how to design diagnostic, formative and summative assessments, so that the needs of all learners are met. They will also explore a range of assessment data that can be used for planning purposes. Ways of incorporating a range of pedagogies into units of work to support the needs of learners in diverse contexts will also be a focus. Preservice teachers will continue to connect theory and practice as they develop skills and knowledge relevant to the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.
learning_outcomes: Address diverse learning needs through differentiation practices for inclusive learning
Apply theories and practices of differentiation to planning, teaching and assessment
Incorporate a range of appropriate teaching practices into learning sequences
Design diagnostic, formative and summative assessments that produce valid assessment data and enable feedback to students and families
Interpret and analyse assessment data to inform planning, teaching, moderation and reporting
Critically reflect on how differentiation and assessment practices support learning for diverse learners
prerequisites: must have completed all of EDUC1902 Professional Experience 1: Professional Identity and the Role of the Teacher/EDUC2901 Professional Experience 2: Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment
antirequisites: N/A

title: Learning about Literacies and Text Production
overview: This course develops students’ English teaching skills in the areas multimodal text production and writing. Students will develop knowledge of text production from a semiotic perspective, inclusive of linguistic and non-linguistic modalities and a range of production technologies. Students will focus on producing texts in a range of genres, including narrative, informational and persuasive genres, using a variety of modes. Students will learn pedagogies for teaching writing and multi-modal text production in diverse classroom contexts, building on knowledge of literacy, language and literature gained in previous English courses. Students will learn to use quality literature and writing processes to support learning about literary and imaginative writing.
learning_outcomes: Understand and critically appraise different theories, models, and practices for literacy learning.
Apply genre theory to the design and production of multimodal texts.
Apply detailed knowledge of the language and literary features and patterns of texts to interpret and create texts.
Design and justify planning and assessment approaches to inform teaching and learning for writing and text production, including the explicit teaching of writing in subjects other than English.
Demonstrate knowledge and understanding different theoretical perspectives of learner difference and the implications for inclusive teaching of English.
Apply, justify and demonstrate a range of strategies for designing teaching learning programs for writing and text production
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUCX215 Learning About Reading OR must have completed EDUC2010 Learning About Reading
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC 3062 English Curriculum Text Production at the University of South Australia

title: First Nations Peoples, Knowledges and Culturally Responsive Teaching
overview: The core focus is to prepare teachers and leaders to develop knowledge and critical understandings of current national and international evidence based research to improve Indigenous students' achievement. Drawing on Australian Aboriginal Education theory and culturally responsive theoretical frameworks, this course investigates how Indigenous Peoples maintain and revitalise local languages and cultural knowledges as they relate to teaching and learning. Approaches will include development of appropriate teaching and learning practices that are relevant to place. Attention will be drawn to the shared responsibilities of all Australians to unlearn deficit racialised beliefs and practices which prevent collective flourishing in schooling
learning_outcomes: Explain the knowledge and skills required to work effectively with diverse Aboriginal learners, families, peoples, perspectives, and histories
Explain and justify assessment, curriculum and evidence-based pedagogical practices relevant to Aboriginal education
Interpret knowledge of culturally responsive teaching that respects and values the democratic rights of Aboriginal children and the sovereignties of Aboriginal First Nations through education
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX107 First Nations Peoples, Knowledges and Culturally Responsive Teaching

title: Understanding Complexities Impacting Families and Communities
overview: This course will focus on the philosophical and evidence-informed approaches to wellbeing in families, society, and communities and how to advance society’s prosperity, wellbeing and cohesion by addressing inequality and trauma in culturally diverse communities. The course explores how to cultivate wellbeing and explore differences between cultural factors, drawing on research from education, psychology, organisational psychology and the social sciences. Students will learn about philosophical approaches to wellbeing and systems-level and community perspectives that contribute to societal wellbeing, resilience and cohesion.
learning_outcomes: Identify social processes impacting children, young people and their families
Understand and critically examine changing family contexts and impacts on children and young people
Identify and explain aspects of child safety, protection and abuse and respond effectively to assist children and young people while maintaining safe, inclusive learning and living environments
Understand and critically apply evidence-based approaches to support children and young people, their families and communities
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX110 Understanding Complexities Impacting Families and Communities

title: Wellbeing for Learning and Teaching
overview: This course aims to promote understanding, agency and advocacy for learner, teacher and school community wellbeing, safety and identity formation within the pre-service teacher’s educational philosophy and practice.
learning_outcomes: Critique the diverse definitions and representations of wellbeing and safety across educational policy and practice informing the development of their own philosophy of embedding learner, teacher and community wellbeing and safety as an early career teacher.

Clearly demonstrate awareness and understanding of research informed evidence of the current wellbeing of learners and teachers and analyse how this is reported, measured and/or evaluated to inform teaching embedding wellbeing and safety into curriculum, pedagogy and assessment and own teacher wellbeing practices

Critically analyse contemporary issues impacting on learner and teacher wellbeing and safety, the protective and risk factors across ecological systems and interconnectedness between learner and teacher wellbeing.

Demonstrate understanding of diverse wellbeing and safety approaches including individual, holistic, whole school and community approaches that are culturally inclusive and contextual, including learning from First Nations approaches to wellbeing and safety.

Reflect deeply on their own teacher wellbeing and identity and demonstrate agency and responsibility in developing a personalised plan to support their transition as an early career teacher for a sustained and teaching future.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Democratic Curriculum: An Inquiry Approach
overview: This course aims to develop critical perspectives on curriculum, pedagogy and assessment and an understanding of their relationships to democratic participation and an inclusive society. Students will critically analyse how curriculum, in alignment with pedagogy and assessment, reproduces and/or transforms schools and society. The course enables students to critically analyse concepts of knowledge and social justice and apply these to specific contexts as they build knowledge through inquiry and dialogue.
learning_outcomes: Articulate a theorised account of democratic curriculum
Explain the role of curriculum in the reproduction and/or transformation of society
Apply concepts of curricular justice to analyse curricular, pedagogical and assessment practices
Critically analyse the forms of knowledge evident in contemporary classrooms and schools
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC3901 Professional Experience 3: Planning, Teaching and Assessing for Diversity OR must have completed EDUC6902 Professional Experience 1: Planning, Teaching, Assessing and Managing the Classroom Environment
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC4212 Critical Perspectives on Curriculum Pedagogy and Assessment at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed EDUC5249 Critical Perspectives of Education at the University of Australia

title: The Importance of Peer Relationships
overview: To develop and extend students knowledge and understanding of the social, emotional, developmental and psychological dimensions of peer relationships in face-to-face and online contexts.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the social dynamic of various environments in terms of peer interactions and relationships
Recognise the importance of positive peer interactions and social competencies for healthy outcomes
Develop strategies for facilitating positive peer interactions and dealing with negative ones in face-to-face and online contexts
Recognise and evaluate the contribution of peer relationships to bullying, aggression, stress, loneliness, depression and suicide
Develop strategies to protect their personal and professional identities online
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC4213 Peers, Relationships in Health at the University of South Australia

title: Dance and Music, Social Dreaming
overview: This course aims to support students towards their future role as an arts educator by deepening and extending subject knowledge of traditional and contemporary dance and music education. Working with dance and music pedagogies students will gain mastery of these subjects for the primary school learning environment with a focus on the changing nature of dance and music education and its impact on diverse young people in the community.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the role and function of Dance and Music in diverse contemporary communities and their impact on young people
Identify traditional and contemporary approaches to Dance and Music in curriculum decision making and research
Experience and critically reflect on the intrinsic and instrumental value of dance and music in the curriculum
Apply current and appropriate pedagogies for Dance and Music
Identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Dance and Music as intrinsic to Australian cultural knowledge, understanding and communication
Demonstrate reflective practice in working as an active teacher/artist educator
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC2076 Dance and Music, Social Dreaming at the University of South Australia
assessment: A range of assignments designed to support course outcomes – 50%

title: Drama and Visual Arts: Story Landscapes (UniSA)
overview: This course will deepen and extend students' traditional, contemporary drama and visual arts subject knowledge for work in school settings.
learning_outcomes: Employ an understanding of the role and function of Drama and Visual Arts in diverse contemporary communities and their impact upon young people
Identify traditional and contemporary approaches to Drama and Visual Arts in curriculum decision making and research
Apply current and appropriate pedagogies for working with Drama and Visual Arts
Identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander storytelling and visual arts as intrinsic to Australian cultural knowledge, understanding and communication
Articulate the intrinsic and instrumental value of Drama, and Visual Arts in the school curriculum
Employ reflective practice in working as an active teacher/artist educator
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUCX202 Becoming an Educator with an Arts Specialisation
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX207 Drama and Visual Arts: Story Landscapes OR must not have completed EDUC3078 at the University of South Australia

title: Production, Presentation and Audience in Arts Education
overview: Preservice teachers will undertake practice-led arts workshops focusing on creative processes and pedagogical content leading to a presentation. Reflective documentation will include application to diverse learning contexts with connections to other key learning areas. Approaches to production include critical thinking with pedagogical strategies for inclusion and design thinking. SUGGESTED CHANGE: This course aims to equip pre-service teachers for their future role as an educational leader for children's arts learning, applying knowledge of arts practices and approaches in arts education and undertaking professional engagement with a site to design and implement an arts project.
learning_outcomes: Critically reflect on the role and function of the arts as a means of communication for young people in diverse contemporary communities
Identify and research traditional and contemporary approaches to production, presentation and audiences within arts curricula
Research and develop arts creative processes and practices to produce and present performance, presentation or display for an audience
Critically analyse current approaches to technologies for working in the arts in relation to production, presentation and audience
Identify cultural knowledge and influences intrinsic to the development and creation of art works
Critically reflect on practice as an active arts educator
corequisites: Must be enrolled in must be final course in the Arts Specialisation
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX219 Production, Presentation and Audience in Arts Education

title: Catholic Theology: An Introduction
overview: To introduce students to the active process of 'doing theology' in the Catholic tradition, in educational settings, through the critical examination of core theological topics that bring contemporary human experience, questions and challenges into personal, communal and global dialogue with this Catholic tradition.
learning_outcomes: Engage in contextual theological reflection, analysis and dialogue through the articulation of questions, discussion and personal interaction with the Catholic theological tradition
Analyse contemporary Christology and the ‘person and work’ of Christ; and pedagogical applications

Apply Catholic theological perspectives to the pedagogies and priorities of Catholic schools, in the context of critical educational challenges (for example: ecological conversion, Gospel justice, consumerism, human sexuality education)
Analyse the development of Christian theologies and language about God in their historical contexts, with a focus on educational implications
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC2049 Catholic Theology at a grade of at least An Introduction at the University of South Australia

title: Catholic Scriptures: An Introduction
overview: To examine the Christian Scriptures (First Testament and Second Testament) as literature and as sacred texts, while critically analysing methods of Scriptural interpretation and the Catholic pedagogical applications of the Scripture studied. This entails the application of the ‘Three Worlds of the Text’ approach to the study of these sacred texts, with an emphasis on teaching the genres, contexts and contemporary interpretations of the focus texts.
learning_outcomes: Apply the ‘Three Worlds of the Text’ approach to interpreting biblical texts, with a focus on genre, context and contemporary meaning-making in Catholic education
Analyse and apply the major theological themes of the First Testament especially as expressed in the Books of Genesis and Exodus
Evaluate the importance of the Jewish context of the life of Jesus and of the early Christian communities
Analyse the theology of the Gospel of Matthew and its portrayal of Jesus as prophet, teacher and Messiah
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC1069 Catholic Scriptures at a grade of at least An Introduction at the University of South Australia

title: Curriculum Design in Catholic Education
overview: To explore and evaluate contemporary principles, approaches, content, pedagogies, resources and assessment practices for designing Religious Education programs and lessons.  Catholic identity and mission, as they impact on Religious Education Curriculum design, will be considered and examined in dialogue with the realities of dynamic contemporary contexts. The course will develop understanding of cultural and religious contexts of students in the RE classroom.  This course offers teachers in Catholic Schools opportunities to develop the skills, knowledge and capabilities needed for designing curricula in Religious Education which can be transferred to other Learning Areas.
learning_outcomes: Understand and appreciate the importance of context for the design of contemporary Religious Education curricula in Catholic Schools
Articulate a philosophy for teaching and learning in the Religious Education learning area relevant to the contemporary Catholic School classroom
Investigate and critique contemporary approaches to Religious Education in a Catholic School
Analyse and critique key elements in designing Religious Education curriculum

Design effective curricula in contemporary Religious Education consistent with an articulated philosophy of Religious Education, drawing on the Crossways Religious Education Curriculum and course perspectives
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EDUCX203 Catholic Scriptures: An Introduction/EDUCX204 Catholic Theology: An Introduction
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC3035 Religious Education in Catholic Schools at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed EDUC5225 Curriculum Design in Catholic Education at the University of South Australia

title: Catholic Schools: Identity, Mission and Practice
overview: This course aims to explore why Catholic Schools exist today, key research and beliefs about learners and teachers in Catholic Schools as well as pedagogies and professional practices that enhance the aims of Catholic Education. Participants will reflect on how Catholic theology contributes to the educator’s beliefs about children, childhood and adolescence, to their personal and professional identity and to choices about educational principles, methods and approaches best aligned to enhancing the mission of contemporary Catholic Schools.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically discuss how Catholic anthropology and Catholic Social Teaching Principles directly shape educational practices in Catholic Schools
Critically reflect on personal and professional teacher identity in the light of Catholic beliefs and values
Examine and critique approaches to teaching and learning in Catholic School classrooms to enhance contemporary understandings of identity and mission of Catholic Schools
Research, create, implement and evaluate a range of transformative practices appropriate for enhancing a contemporary Catholic School’s identity and mission
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUCX203 Catholic Scriptures: An Introduction AND must have completed EDUCX204 Catholic Theology: An Introduction
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC2063 Contemporary Catholic Schools at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed EDUCX500 Catholic Schools: Identity, Mission and Practice

title: Digital Technologies
overview: The course aims to familiarise students with key digital technologies concepts and content as outlined in relevant curricula. Students will develop their knowledge, understanding, and practical skills in planning and implementing digital technology-based learning experiences for students from foundation to year 6.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of concepts, structure and content within the Digital Technologies subject
Plan and design teaching resources to enhance students’ Digital Technologies knowledge, understanding and practice of processes and skills
Develop, apply and critically reflect on the skills and resources required to support teaching in the Digital Technologies learning area
Design effective digital technologies learning experiences for children in Foundation to Year 6, demonstrating understanding of curriculum requirements and innovative teaching strategies
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX206 Digital Technologies OR must not have completed EDUC1084 at the University of South Australia
assessment: Professional Simulation, Professional Simulation, Professional Simulation – 60%

title: Food Technology 1
overview: This course aims to introduce preservice teachers to the skills, knowledge and professional expertise associated with teaching and learning in design and technologies food specialisms, in both primary and middle school settings, with a strong focus on integrating both the theoretical and practical aspects of food technologies .
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the latest technologies and design principles in planning and developing relevant and engaging food technology lessons in line with the SACE framework
Identify and apply concepts around the societal influences on food production and food choices
Apply and critically analyse food preparation and production techniques when designing solutions suitable for a senior school classroom
Apply WHS knowledge in identifying and applying food safety and hygiene practices, as well as safe use of tools and equipment in the food technology classroom
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX208 Food Technology 1 OR must not have completed EDUC1089 at the University of South Australia

title: Technology by Design
overview: This course aims to develop students knowledge, skills, and expertise in, design thinking, enterprise learning, entrepreneurship, STEM and technology-based pedagogies. Through engagement in project based learning and cross-discipline planning, students will apply their skills to meet the needs of a community, industry or organisation and connect their learning to practical STEM and entrepreneurial education practices.
learning_outcomes: Identify, plan and teach aspects of STEM and enterprise learning through a project-based inquiry approach
Apply the design-thinking process to develop critical and creative thinking, when solving complex problems
Select and use resources appropriate to design and technologies
Develop the capacity to work with colleagues to plan for, to evaluate and to improve teaching and learning through technology, entrepreneurial learning and design thinking education
corequisites: Must be enrolled in must be the final course in the Design and Technologies specialisation
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC3070 Technology by Design at the University of South Australia OR must not have completed EDUCX410 Technology by Design

title: Teaching Linguistically Diverse Learners
overview: This course aims to equip students with theoretical understandings and pedagogical strategies needed to teach learners of English as an Additional Language or Dialect (EALD). Students will enhance their understanding of EALD learners and their learning in mainstream classes; develop pedagogical strategies and assessments; and create resources to support EALD students to access and engage with learning areas across the curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Analyse the linguistic, cultural and learning needs of linguistically diverse learners
Analyse the linguistic demands of their teaching context
Critically investigate an approach to teaching linguistically diverse learners in the context of language acquisition research
Evaluate and justify the selection of a range of strategies for making learning accessible to linguistically diverse learners
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX224 Teaching Linguistically Diverse Learners OR must not have completed EDUC1087 at the University of South Australia

title: Grammar Across the Curriculum
overview: This course aims to develop students' understanding and use of English grammar to teach a range of text types across academic disciplines and Year Level curricula. More particularly, it equips students with knowledge of how grammar relates to meaning making and literacy, and how different academic disciplines use grammar to make specialised meanings for their own purposes. Students will also learn how to develop language-aware pedagogical strategies, resources and assessments relevant and effective in promoting learning across academic disciplines and the curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Recognise relationships between English language grammar and meaning making, and explain the importance of teaching grammar explicitly and connecting it to meaning making across the curriculum
Explain the functions of grammatical features and describe how context and purpose influence language choices in different genres (text types)

Apply a range of pedagogical strategies and frameworks to teach grammar relevant to different academic disciplines and across Year Level curricula, including various techniques for gathering, assessing and reflecting on evidence of student learning
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX109 Grammar Across the Curriculum OR must not have completed EDUC2093 Grammar Across the Curriculum at the University of South Australia

title: Growth, Health and Development
overview: This course introduces students to a developmental model of how young people grow and mature together and the inextricable relationship this has on the emergence of movement capabilities. The course focuses on the early childhood to adolescent stages of human growth and motor development and encourages a holistic view of development. The knowledge and skills acquired throughout the course will enhance capabilities to teach the whole child using movement as a valuable medium. A focus on planning and teaching social dance, fundamental athletics skills and general gymnastics in developmentally appropriate ways, to children in the Primary years of school will be explicitly modelled with the opportunity for students to enhance their own abilities.
learning_outcomes: Explain the characteristics and principles of human growth, development and motor behaviour from birth to adolescence.

Understand and describe the complex process of change in human development and motor behaviour that emerges from the interaction of heredity, task requirements and the environment as it relates to teaching.
Use the key terms associated with the study of human growth and development appropriately to contribute to small group discussion and learning activities.
Explain how the periods of life are inextricably linked with the phases of motor development through the Hourglass Model of motor development.
Apply knowledge and understanding of human growth and motor development from birth to adolescence to plan developmentally appropriate and engaging learning sequences for primary-aged students.
Demonstrate teaching skills in the developmentally appropriate activities for the early and primary years of schooling.
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUCX301 Healthy Lifestyles OR must have completed EDUC3016 Healthy Lifestyles
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX209 Growth, Health and Development OR must not have completed EDUC1085 at the University of South Australia

title: Healthy Lifestyles
overview: To explore the place of physical activity in a range of populations from a health and wellbeing perspective. Students will develop an understanding of physical activity and the range of health benefits it offers across the lifespan through participation in a range of physical activities. Key skills will derive from measuring physical activity levels of children, data analysis and digital literacy, through teaching and learning a range of physical activities. Students will also consider the place of physical activity and healthy eating in home lives and will gain knowledge and skills in planning and delivering physical activities in a range of settings, aligned with the primary curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of physical activity, the health benefits of regular physical activity across the lifespan, aligned with the dimensions of wellbeing
Explore and identify participation in physical activity in different cultures and demographics, analysing strategies to promote uptake of regular physical activity
Apply the requisite knowledge and skills to develop and teach an effective series of physical activities to primary years school children
Evaluate pedagogical practices influencing the development of confident and competent movers through a range of physical activities
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX301 Healthy Lifestyles OR must not have completed HLTH1013 at the University of South Australia

title: Pedagogies for Health and Physical Education Specialisation
overview: To prepare pre-service teachers to construct appropriate learning experiences in Health and Physical Education for students in the Primary years of schooling, with a focus on building culturally responsive capabilities.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of breadth in HPE pedagogies and application in planning to enhance learning for diverse student cohorts
Apply curriculum frameworks and a range of teacher resources to plan learning experiences in Health and Physical Education.
Explore the use of community spaces as these relate to promoting engagement and learning in Health and Physical Education.
Demonstrate knowledge of a critical pedagogical inquiry to promote engagement and enhanced learning outcomes for diverse student learners in Health and Physical Education.
prerequisites: Must have completed All prior HPE Specialisation Courses
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX217 Pedagogies for Health and Physical Education Specialisation AND must not have completed EDUC4219 Specialisation in Health and Physical Education at the University of South Australia

title: Geographical Studies
overview: To develop a deep, conceptual and foundational content knowledge in geographical studies through exploring the content and skills of the Australian Curriculum: Geography. To develop the capacity to think geographically through geographical concepts and key content areas that underpin the geography curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply knowledge of the Australian Curriculum HaSS: Geography to plan relevant and engaging learning experiences and quality assessment
Apply geographical skills of spatial analysis and mapping and undertake quality geographical fieldwork
Think geographically through applying the geographical concepts
Understand pedagogical content knowledge involved in teaching HaSS: Geography
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX108 Geographical Studies OR must not have completed EDUC1103 HaSS Geographical Studies Specialisation at the University of South Australia

title: Historical Studies
overview: This course aims to develop a deep, conceptual and foundational content knowledge in historical studies through exploring the content and skills of the Australian Curriculum: History. Students will develop the capacity to think historically through historical concepts and key content areas that underpin the history curriculum.
learning_outcomes: Understand and apply knowledge of the Australian Curriculum: History to plan relevant and engaging learning experiences and quality assessment
