overview: The aim of this course is to provide an understanding of the effects of radiation in vivo, operational health physics, radiation protection and epidemiological methods appropriate for practice as a medical or health physicist.
learning_outcomes: Explain basic concepts and principles of radiation biology and radiation protection.
Discuss biological effects of radiation.
Explain basic concepts and principles of radiation therapy.
Discuss legislation regarding radiation protection.
Apply accepted/recommended models to calculate risks associated with radiation exposure in straightforward situations.
Use the tools, methodologies, language and conventions of physics to communicate ideas and explanations.
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task – 40%

title: Radiotherapy Physics
overview: In this course, students are introduced to the production of radiation cancer treatment and procedures for quantifying the dose delivered to tumours and normal tissue. They develop an understanding of quality control of radiotherapy equipment and the use of sealed and unsealed sources.
learning_outcomes: Describe the radiobiological basis for radiotherapy.
Explain the principles of radiotherapy equipment and define the characteristics of clinical beams and their measurement.
Explain the need for and principles of quality control of equipment in radiotherapy.
Discuss a range of radiotherapy treatment techniques including the use of sealed and unsealed sources.
Discuss the principles of dose calculation and apply them in different radiotherapy techniques.
Discuss sources of uncertainties and their potential impact in radiotherapy.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Medical Radiation Physics Research Project A
overview: Students will commence an independent research project in the field of medical physics under academic supervision. The course aims to develop specialised knowledge and capabilities for independent scientific research.
learning_outcomes: Design, implement, and document scientific research to test hypotheses or develop new insights, maintaining accurate records and a robust data management plan.
Use specialised analytical, interpretation and evaluation skills and techniques necessary to carry out research in an advanced topic in medical physics.
Effectively present scientific research findings in both written and oral forms, tailoring communication to both specialist and general audiences.
Understand and apply ethical principles and regulatory requirements relevant to medical physics, and professional standards essential for conducting responsible scientific research.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Medical Radiation Physics Research Project B
overview: Students will complete an independent research project in the field of medical physics under academic supervision. The course aims to develop specialised knowledge and capabilities for independent scientific research.
learning_outcomes: Design, implement, and document scientific research to test hypotheses or develop new insights, maintaining accurate records and a robust data management plan.
Use specialised analytical, interpretation and evaluation skills and techniques necessary to carry out research in an advanced topic in medical physics.
Effectively present scientific research findings in both written and oral forms, tailoring communication to both specialist and general audiences.
Understand and apply ethical principles and regulatory requirements relevant to medical physics, and professional standards essential for conducting responsible scientific research.
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in BIOL6900 Medical Radiation Physics Research Project A
antirequisites: N/A

title: Radiation Safety in the Workplace
overview: This course aims to provide learners with an overview of radiation safety across several sectors. Learners will experience radiation safety firstly in medicine, industry and research, before delving deeper into the safety aspects across mining and the processing of raw radioactive materials. Through examining the procedures and activities that apply safety across various sectors, this course aligns with the program’s intent to provide real world, practical knowledge for the effective management of radiation and radioactive materials.
learning_outcomes: Explain the radiation safety practices across the medical, industrial, agricultural and research sectors
Describe the radiation safety practices across the nuclear sector and compare the differences and similarities between the power and defence sectors
Explain the radiation safety practices across the mining, milling, and refining sectors
Prepare a radiation safety management plan based on a specific scenario highlighting radiation safety and management principles and procedures
Translate the safe management of radiation, radioactive materials, and radioactive sources, across a broad audience spectrum including scientific, industrial, and members of the public
prerequisites: Must have completed all of EART5007 Radioactivity, Radiation Detection and Dosimetry/EART5008 Radiation Biology and Incident Response
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in EART5009 Radiation Management and Regulatory Control
antirequisites: N/A

title: Optics and Photonics 3
overview: This course provides students with a knowledge of optics and photonics.
learning_outcomes: Describe and explain the paraxial scalar wave equation, and the integral, Gaussian and guided mode solutions;
Apply wave optics to a range of problems;
Describe, explain and apply the Fresnel equation for the reflection and transmission of light for isotropic and anisotropic non-conducting media;
Describe and explain the operation of common optical components;
Describe and explain the structure and operation of simple lasers;
Use the tools, methodologies, language and conventions of physics to test and communicate ideas and explanations
prerequisites: Must have completed all of MATHX202 Differential Equations/MATHX203 Multivariable Calculus/PHYS2002 Electromagnetism 2/PHYS2003 Solid State Physics and Photonics 2
antirequisites: Must not have completed PHYSICS 3540 at the University of Adelaide

title: Mineral Systems
overview: This course covers the processes that control the formation of ore deposits and mineral resources. Mineral resource forming processes are examined in the framework of the tectonic, petrogenetic and geochemical evolution of the Earth's crust on local, regional and global geological scales.
learning_outcomes: Explain the critical features of the mineral system concept and its application to mineral deposit formation
Identify and describe the essential characteristics of different mineral deposit styles
Demonstrate proficiency in rock and mineral identification and the use of digital datasets and their application to mineral deposit formation
Apply the mineral system approach to create an exploration strategy through a project case study
prerequisites: Must have completed EART5011 Exploration and Resource Development 1: Geology and Geochemistry
antirequisites: Must not have completed EART3031 Mineral Resources III

title: Life-of-Asset Sustainability
overview: This course introduces the concept of life-of-asset sustainability and delivers skills and practical tools, that can be implemented from resource project concept to asset closure to ensure sustainable outcomes. The course builds on concepts presented in Global Georesources and Human Perspectives of the Resources Industry with specific focus on measurement, monitoring and management of environmental and cultural heritage factors. Case study examples will be used to illustrate the importance of gathering baseline data relevant to ESG, from the earliest stages of exploration, through delivery of product to market and, eventually to asset ‘closure’.
learning_outcomes: Understand georesource project economics from a quadruple-bottom-line perspective, including traditional economic analysis plus environmental, social and governance factors (E+ESG)
Understand and critique techniques for quantifying diverse E+ESG data into unified ‘Sustainability metrics’
Understand practical considerations for developing a sustainable resource project

Recognise the link between life-of-asset sustainability and inherent resource project characteristics and design a data capture and analytical program to identify key characteristics and inform a life-of-asset sustainability model
Communicate complex ESG issues to a broad audience
prerequisites: Must have completed 1 of BIOL5001/BIOL6005 Social Licence to Operate
antirequisites: N/A

title: Exploration and Resource Development 1: Geology and Geochemistry
overview: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to geological and geochemical surveying for resource exploration, from camp to deposit/prospect scales. Students learn how to acquire, process, and interpret geological and geochemical datasets to resolve geological relationships at a variety of scales. They will synthesise these data into two-, three- and four-dimensional models that guide further exploration for geological resources. Students will be equipped with the knowledge and skillset to judge which techniques are appropriate for achieving resource exploration objectives within a variety of terrains.
learning_outcomes: Describe the characteristics of the major mineral deposit types and explain how they are formed
Identify common rock types and minerals found in and around ore deposits and demonstrate how they are used to assist with mineral exploration targeting
Design geological and geochemical survey acquisition plans that target resource exploration objectives at camp to deposit/prospect scales
Plan and execute field work to undertake geological and geochemical surveys and mapping
Compile, process and interpret geological and geochemical survey data and communicate the results to inform further exploration or resource development plans
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Data Collection and/or Analysis – 40%

title: Advanced Field Geoscience
overview: This course aims to develop advanced knowledge in Advanced Field Geoscience, and to develop the skills required for the practice of independent scientific research. It complements the Honours Field Geoscience Project course to provide professional development training relevant for a career in the chosen discipline, or for further study along a research training pathway.
learning_outcomes: Identify, measure and record a wide variety of geological features using discipline and industry standards
Develop detailed knowledge of the geological setting and development of continental plate margins
Plan and undertake a field investigation to document and characterise the geological evolution of a terrane through time
Integrate a wide variety of geological data and observations to construct 3D and 4D geological models in the form of maps, cross-sections, time-space plots and schematic diagrams
Synthesise research knowledge with observations made in the field and communicate these results to peers
prerequisites: Must have completed 144 units of undergraduate study or equivalent
antirequisites: N/A

title: Exploration and Resource Development 2: Geophysics
overview: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to geophysical surveying for resource exploration and development, from regional to mine site scales.
learning_outcomes: Design geophysical survey acquisition plans that target resource exploration and development objectives at regional to mine site scales
Process and/or transform raw geophysical survey data into regularised, interpretable form
Interpret processed or regularised geophysical survey datasets to reveal underlying geological rock type architecture or resource development phenomena
Simulate the geophysical response of idealised or interpreted geological model architectures
Plan geophysical monitoring strategies under resource development scenarios based on baseline geophysical survey data
Characterise resource model uncertainty determined from a variety of geophysical survey datasets
prerequisites: Must have completed EART2018 Geophysics II
antirequisites: Must not have completed GEOLOGY2515
assessment: Problem Solving Task, Problem Solving Task, Report – 75%

title: Georesources Industry Project
overview: This course introduces students to a wide variety of techniques and methods used by the earth sciences industry. Students will be provided with knowledge and a framework to use selected techniques to address specific industry challenges. Students will generate new geological, geophysics and/or geochemical data to develop integrated geologic models to advance scientific knowledge and understanding of industry challenges.
learning_outcomes: Identify a relevant Georesources industry challenge and develop a project proposal to investigate this challenge
Identify, evaluate and develop appropriate methods of techniques to feasibly address the Georesources industry
Analyse and interpret a range of geological, geophysical and/or geochemical datasets to produce meaningful insights, making evidence-based conclusions with industry applications
Implement and manage research activities effectively, demonstrating project planning, time management and initiative
Design and demonstrate methods for communication of the project approach and outcomes tailored for diverse audiences
prerequisites: Must have completed all of BIOL6005 Social Licence to Operate/EART5002 Mineral Systems/EART5003 Life-of-Asset Sustainability/EART5011 Exploration and Resource Development 1: Geology and Geochemistry/EART5012 Advanced Field Geoscience/EART6002 Geoscience Data Analysis and Interpretation/EART6003 Geoscience Communication/EART6006 Exploration and Resource Development 2: Geophysics
antirequisites: N/A

title: Contemporary Practice Theories for Social Work
overview: This course will develop students' knowledge of contemporary social work practice theories and their application. Students will develop knowledge of contemporary social work practice theories including individual focused theories, critical and structural theories, and theories influenced by postmodernism.
learning_outcomes: Apply a specialised range of practice theories and intervention strategies to professional case situations.
Critically analyse the appropriateness of particular contemporary social work practice theories for use in working with specific individuals, groups and communities.
Analyse and demonstrate a culturally competent approach to social work practice.
Articulate an ethical decision-making framework and apply in contemporary practice situations.
Articulate and apply a broad socio-political framework to specialised social work intervention.
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5098 Contemporary Practice Theories for Social Work at the University of South Australia

title: Social Work Practice Skills
overview: This course will develop students' knowledge and skills in social work intervention, interviewing skills and group work required for professional practice with a diverse range of individuals, families and groups. Students will develop specialised professional knowledge of the social work practice skills in social work interviews and group work. Students will practice and apply these skills in diverse contexts by developing cognitive and technical skills in reflective accountable practice using ethical decision-making contexts.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate appropriate interviewing skills and analyse the different applications of purposeful social work interviewing and a range of approaches to group work with diverse clients, including Indigenous Australians and culturally and linguistically diverse clients.
Critically analyse and demonstrate the stages of an interview and the skills and techniques used for ethical practice applied in each.
Identify and demonstrate appropriate roles, skills and techniques relevant to group work.
Demonstrate advanced skills to plan, lead and facilitate group processes and group outcomes using ethical approaches.
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5104 Social Work Practice Skills at the University of South Australia

title: Social Work Practicum 1
overview: This course will enable students to develop specialised social work practice skills in a practice setting. Students will undertake supervised placement where they will develop specialised practice skills through the application of theory to a particular practice context. Students will utilise their skills as a reflexive practitioner to develop cognitive and technical skills in ethical reflection and decision making, professional relationship building, social work supervision and client engagement, intervention planning, implementation and evaluation. Students will examine the notion of social work as an agent of change at the individual and broader systemic level.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the values and ethics of social work in the practice setting
Differentially engage with clients in specialised social work interventions that demonstrate the purpose of social work involvement
Demonstrate competence to develop and critically reflect upon an intervention plan
Effectively utilise professional supervision and demonstrate a reflective approach in the practice environment
Articulate the implications of intervention and as a reflexive practitioner demonstrate an appreciation of the limitations of the intervention and the need for broader social change
Meet the AASW Practice Standards to the required level.
prerequisites: must have completed all of INDG5005 Aboriginal Health and Wellbeing/SOWK5000 Social Work and Policy Practice/SOWK5001 Contemporary Practice Theories for Social Work/SOWK5002 Social Work Practice Skills
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in SOWK5005 Ethical Decision Making
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5105 Social Work Practicum 1 at the University of South Australia

title: Ethical Decision Making
overview: This course will enable students to apply specialised professional and ethical practice frameworks to shape strategies for practice, research, advocacy and systems change. Students will use skills as an ethical and reflexive practitioner to explore the relationship between self as a social worker, practice frameworks and social science knowledge. Students will develop and evaluate knowledge of recent developments in evidence-based practice and the re-creation of social work knowledges.
learning_outcomes: Create a personalised social work practice framework that incorporates social work knowledge, value and ethical perspectives and orientation.
Examine the concept of professional judgement and ethical decision making in the practice context.
Critically analyse the place of practice research and demonstrate the skills for researched informed practice.
Apply specialised knowledge of social work knowledge of social work theory and practice skills as an ethical and reflexive practitioner.
prerequisites: must have completed all of SOWK5000 Social Work and Policy Practice/SOWK5001 Contemporary Practice Theories for Social Work/SOWK5002 Social Work Practice Skills
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in SOWK5004 Social Work Practicum 1
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5096 Ethical Decision Making at the University of South Australia

title: Innovation and Research
overview: In this course students will examine and apply research methodologies and align them to social issues to inform and recreate social work practice, knowledge and research. Students will develop contemporary knowledge of the traditions and philosophical underpinnings of traditional and new social science research methodologies with a specialised knowledge of constructing research problems and questions, analysing methodologies, data and qualitative methods. Students will utilise this knowledge to relate data to social questions and present data in a research context.
learning_outcomes: Critically align research methodologies and their theoretical underpinnings to social questions and issues.
Critically use social science research methodologies that explore multiple aspects of lived experience through tools like visual methodologies and narrative and memory.
Demonstrate the cognitive, technical and creative skills to utilise research findings to develop social work practice, knowledge and research.
Develop high level strategies for communicating and developing research findings.
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5101 Innovation and Research at the University of South Australia

title: Innovative Social Work Practice with Children and Families
overview: This course will advance students’ specialist knowledge of practice theories and skills for innovative social work with clients with special needs in a range of practice settings. Students will develop knowledge of the diffusion of innovation in relation to new and emerging programs, policies and practices for working with children and families. The course will explore contemporary approaches in social work assessment and intervention. Students will develop specialised knowledge about intervention and preventative strategies in child abuse and child and family well-being. This includes how abuse and neglect affects child/human development risks, as well as resilience and child and family developmental opportunities in major life stage transitions. Students will critically analyse the impact of child protection policies in the context of historical policies that affect Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander families and communities.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse the social and cultural constructions of child/human development, child abuse and neglect and the impact of these on social policy and service provision to clients and their families.
Explore the place of evidence based practice and diffusion of innovation in the development of social work interventions in child protection.
Develop and promote a preventative approach to child abuse with particular reference to the cultural and linguistic diversity of our community.
Critically explore the impact of child protection policy and service provision on Indigenous Australians.
Utilise specialised professional knowledge to identify indications of child abuse and neglect and what constitutes an appropriate response.
prerequisites: must have completed SOWK5004 Social Work Practicum 1
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5102 Innovative Social Work Practice with Children and Families at the University of South Australia

title: Mental Health and Social Work Practice
overview: This course will enable students to build and critically explore specialist professional knowledge of mental health in social work and apply models of intervention in practice. Students will deepen their knowledge of the diverse lived experiences of individuals with mental health problems and the implications for practice, the historical constructions of mental illness, theories of mental health and illness from social work and other helping professions, and the legal, ethical, social and policy contexts of mental health and illness. The course explicitly focuses on populations at high risk of mental health problems including Indigenous people, young people, women and people from culturally and linguistically diverse communities. The course also examines how gender, culture and socio-economic disadvantage play out in experiences of mental health and illness. Students will develop practice skills in using models of mental health intervention (including recovery models), culturally diverse approaches to mental health intervention (including working with Indigenous people and communities) and mental health assessment in social work (involving studio-based practice).
learning_outcomes: Understand and critically examine medical, psychological and sociological discourses of mental health.
Explore and analyse the contemporary policy context of mental health and its implications for social work practice.
Explore and apply evidence-based models of intervention in mental health and inter-professional practice in mental health.
Engage with consumer and carer voices and explore ways of incorporating them into practice.
Demonstrate a working knowledge of the legal and ethical aspects of mental health practice.
Critically explore culturally diverse approaches to mental health, including with Indigenous people.
prerequisites: must have completed SOWK5004 Social Work Practicum 1
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5108 Mental Health and Social Work Practice at the University of South Australia

title: Human Rights Based Practice and Community Development
overview: In this course, students will gain the ability to critically analyse constructions of human rights and their application to social work and community development. Students will develop an understanding of international and Australian human rights laws and treaties including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and Australian human rights legislation, organisations, policies and practices and community development theories and frameworks. Students will critically analyse philosophies, concepts and theories of human rights, culture, gender, community development, social justice and advance a human rights-informed framework for social work practice with disadvantaged sectors including women, children, refugees, migrants, vulnerable older people, people with mental or physical illness or disability and Indigenous Australians.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse human rights concepts, frameworks and policies as they relate to social justice and social action
Critically analyse Australia's engagement with international human rights legislation and conventions
Critically analyse relevant policies and practices as they apply to disadvantaged groups and communities, including Indigenous Australians, from a human rights perspective
Demonstrate a specialist understanding of relevant community development theories, frameworks and practices in social work from a human rights perspective.
Demonstrate an understanding of how human rights concepts, frameworks and policies can be activated in social work with disadvantaged groups and communities, including Indigenous Australians.
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5100 Human Rights Based Practice and Community Development at the University of South Australia

title: Leadership in Social Work
overview: This course will develop students’ ability to critically analyse and provide leadership in the social work and human service context. Students will critically engage with concepts of ethical leadership and the distinction between leadership and management in the human service context. Students will develop the reasoning and technical skills to demonstrate research informed practice in the management of people and relationships, in the creation of positive workplace cultures, in identifying and resolving conflict, and in generating and managing change. Students will develop the skills and understanding required to practice effectively in interprofessional settings and contexts.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse models of leadership and identify the contribution of gender, culture and class to leadership styles
Analyse and evaluate the social policy context within which social work leadership occurs.
Apply appropriate professional skills to the management of relationships and people in the creation of positive workplace cultures.
Develop leadership skills to identify and resolve conflict.
Critically analyse current policy, practice and processes necessary to generate and manage change within communities, organisations and groups.
Develop the knowledge and skills required for collaboration in interprofessional practice contexts.
prerequisites: must have completed SOWK5004 Social Work Practicum 1
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in SOWK6005 Social Work Practicum 2
antirequisites: must not have completed WELF5103 Leadership in Social Work at the University of South Australia

title: Social Work Practicum 2
overview: This course will consolidate students' competency in professional practice reflecting the integration of social work values, knowledge and skills, and through an independent piece of research contribute to the social work body of knowledge. Students will undertake a supervised placement opportunity to further develop their social work skills, practice and knowledge, and will apply advanced research skills to a research project of relevance to the professional mission of the host organisation.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate advanced social work practice and professional judgement in a selected setting.
Develop appropriate and integrated specialised social work intervention strategies and applying these with a diverse group of clients.
Work collaboratively and inter-professionally within and across organisational boundaries on behalf of clients to achieve social change.

Demonstrate knowledge of research principles and cognitive and technical skills in the planning and execution of a substantial research-based project to advance the host organisation's social justice mission.
Meet the Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW) Practice Standards to the required level.
prerequisites: The student must have achieved at least 72 units prior to enrolment
corequisites: If the following course has not already been completed THEN must be enrolled in SOWK6004 Leadership in Social Work
antirequisites: Must not have completed WELF5106 Social Work Practicum 2 at the University of South Australia

title: Calculus for Statisticians
overview: This course builds core strengths in calculus need for statistical theory and applications. It covers analytic and numeric techniques, integration, series and differentiation. Applications will be chosen based on relevance to core statistical techniques and theory, with a focus on tools need to progress further in these fields.
learning_outcomes: Manipulate single and multivariable functions using standard techniques
Apply key findings of series and limits in calculus and statistics
Differentiate and integrate single and multivariable functions
Use calculus techniques to solve statistical problems
Communicate mathematical derivations and findings
prerequisites: Must have completed MATH1000 Foundations in Mathematics OR must have completed SACE Stage 2 Mathematical Methods or equivalent
antirequisites: N/A
assessment: Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions, Short Response Questions – 10%

title: Strategic Communication Contexts
overview: Strategic Communication Contexts lays the foundation for the development and application of professional communication in a range of sectors through knowledge of strategic communication and public relations theory and practice.
learning_outcomes: Apply key communication and public relations theories to strategic communication development in verbal and written communication
Develop strategic communication for use in corporate, promotional, and political and social movement contexts
Examine changing technological contexts of communication from mass communication to social media communication
Plan and develop strategic communication to help organisations reach their communication objectives using a range of media platforms
Analyse the cultural context of communication and the ethical dimensions of the interplay between communication, culture and power
antirequisites: N/A

title: Campaign Planning
overview: The course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the strategic process involved in planning and developing effective communication campaigns. Students will learn how to identify specific communication goals and objectives, conduct thorough research and analysis, and develop innovative campaign strategies and tactics to achieve desired outcomes. The course emphasises the importance of aligning communication campaigns with organisational objectives and stakeholder needs.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and analyse the strategic communication needs of organisations
Analyse and classify key publics, audiences and stakeholders in relation to organisations
Apply advanced communication research and campaign planning to support organisational goals
Identify and produce creative solutions to complex communication challenges
Apply analytical skills to evaluate and measure communication effectiveness
antirequisites: N/A

title: Transmedia Storytelling
overview: This course explores the theory and practice of transmedia storytelling as a strategic communication approach for brands, organisations, and social causes. Students will learn how to develop immersive narrative experiences that engage audiences across multiple platforms and channels. The course covers key concepts such as world-building, audience engagement, platform mapping, and measuring the impact of transmedia campaigns. Through case studies and hands-on projects, students will gain skills in crafting compelling transmedia narratives aligned with specific communication goals.
learning_outcomes: pply transmedia storytelling theories and concepts to develop comprehensive narrative worlds (story worlds) and immersive brand experiences for strategic communication purposes
Analyse and evaluate existing transmedia storytelling campaigns and narratives across various contexts and industries
Critically examine and discuss the role of transmedia storytelling in contemporary popular culture, marketing, and strategic communication contexts
Design audience journeys and map narratives across multiple platforms and channels for effective engagement
Create original transmedia content tailored to specific platforms, leveraging the unique affordances and storytelling techniques of each medium
Develop and present a comprehensive transmedia storytelling strategy and campaign proposal for a brand, organisation, or specific communication goal
antirequisites: N/A

title: Managing Digital Design
overview: This course will provide a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices of digital and visual design. It aims to equip students with the necessary skills to effectively use design tools, evaluate and implement visual communication strategies, and assess the impact of new digital technologies on an organisation's communication efforts. Students will learn about visual design tools, digital platforms and audio-visual production, and the briefing processes involved in design projects. Learners will conceptualise and create designs for branding and promotion, evaluate the form, functionality and effectiveness of digital design, and critique the impact of design decisions on user experience.
learning_outcomes: Apply theoretical principles and design conventions to analyse digital and traditional forms of communication
Critically appraise the form, functionality and effectiveness of digital design outputs across multiple platforms
Applies the principles of user-experience to critique the impact of design decisions on audiences
Create digital design solutions that enhance stakeholder communication and engagement and provide branding and promotion of organisations
antirequisites: N/A

title: Risk, Issues and Crisis Communication
overview: This course focuses on the role of strategic communication in managing situations of risk and crisis. Students will consider risk and crisis communication in local, national and international contexts and across NGO, government and corporate sectors. They will identify issues and strategies for managing crises, plan effective communication strategies and examine how new technologies and a changing media environment can influence the response of stakeholders. Students will explore the ethical and legal requirements for communication professionals in different cultural contexts. On completion, students will understand the role of strategic communication in crisis situations and how to develop crisis communication plans.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically evaluate contemporary issues and trends in risk and crisis communication, including the impact of emerging technologies and media platforms
Analyse and explain the implications of crises for publics and stakeholders, drawing on key theories, concepts, and frameworks of risk and crisis communication
Apply theoretical knowledge of risk and crisis management to mitigate crises
Produce a range of risk and crisis communication materials and messages
Develop an evaluation plan to measure the effectiveness of crisis communication, including ethical decision-making and outcomes
antirequisites: N/A

title: Media Management
overview: This course introduces students to the advanced theory and management of media relations. Media relations is used to earn positive attention for an individual, group, idea or organisation to enhance its reputation. Management of this practice is central to the communication strategies of not-for-profit, government and corporate sectors. In this course, students will develop advanced knowledge of media relations theories, strategies and tactics across a variety of contexts. This includes analysing and evaluating media campaigns and developing a strategic campaign media management plan.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the role of media management strategies and tactics in shaping contemporary communication practices across not-for-profit, government and corporate sectors
Understand the relationship between media management and news media and how media management is used to influence an organisation’s positive reputation in the media
Build knowledge of advanced media relations theories to understand how to apply them in the development of media relations strategies, tactics and campaigns
Analyse established and emerging media management strategies, campaigns and tactics, and learn how to apply them to different contexts using traditional, social and hybrid media

Apply media management skills in research, writing and strategy to the production of strategic plans, and critically reflect on the role of media relations in addressing contemporary communication issues
antirequisites: N/A

title: Researching Strategic Communication and Media
overview: This course equips learners with the knowledge and skills required to undertake advanced communication and media research in a professional setting. Students will build a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices of research design and implementation, including the research methodologies and ethical research practices used in communication and media, utilising qualitative and quantitative data collection methods, and approaches to both manual and computational data analysis. Students will have a solid foundation on which to expand and apply advanced understanding of research processes to their research endeavours.
learning_outcomes: Explain and analyse how research processes and practices are used in professional communication and media contexts, including ethical considerations
Apply knowledge of communication and media research principles to develop methodologically and ethically sound research design.
Analyse and interpret research outputs using clear and concise language to explain their design implications for communication research and practice.
Report the results of communication and media research using different formats relevant to the sector, and for distribution across a variety of platforms
antirequisites: N/A

title: Leadership in Strategic Communication
overview: Building on the skills and knowledge gained in previous courses, students develop strategic communication leadership knowledge and advanced planning skills. Students undertake an industry internship or industry-focused project, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to become an effective and persuasive strategic communication leader. Students also examine the relationship between effective leadership and communication styles, and the role of the strategic communication professional in leadership communication.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate and critically reflect on knowledge of industry trends, career paths and workplace leadership practices in strategic communication

Apply work-integrated learning principles and professional development best-practice to engage with contemporary industry challenges, employment opportunities and career planning in strategic communication sectors and roles

Apply knowledge of strategic communication leadership in industry settings and environments, and communicate professionally and ethically through a range of genres, contexts, and outputs relevant to the sector.
Critically assess, consolidate and synthesise academic and industry learning.
Critically form and reflect on personalised learning objectives and achievable career plans for ongoing professional development.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Strategic Communication Extended Research Project
overview: In the strategic communication extended research project, students will undertake advanced level research in the discipline of media and communication. Working with an assigned supervisor on an agreed topic of their choice, they will develop and design an independent research project. Students will extend and apply the academic and industry knowledge they have gained throughout their coursework subjects to traditional or practice-based research. This body of work serves as a stepping stone to a professional industry pathway or a research higher degree.
learning_outcomes: Design and conduct an appropriate and achievable research project in the discipline of Media and/or Communication
Identify and address an industry-relevant issue or problem through the critical analysis of an issue or case study
Locate, evaluate and synthesise relevant industry and academic literature related to the agreed topic
Critically analyse the agreed issue or topic through the identification and application of key theories and concepts in Media and/or Communication
prerequisites: must have completed MDIA5008 Researching Strategic Communication and Media
antirequisites: N/A

title: Languages Education and First Nations Knowledges
overview: This course aims to develop critical understanding and pedagogical approaches to Languages Education, to ensure culturally responsive approaches to First Nations people's knowledges and perspectives. It will develop strategies and pedagogies for linguistic and cultural inclusivity for learners of all backgrounds. Pedagogies of inclusion in Languages education, and an introduction to the Australian Curriculum: Languages, including the Framework for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Languages; first, background and additional languages; and Auslan, are investigated and used for planning teaching and learning. The course underpins critical learning pathways aimed at addressing social inequity and shaping a positive future for our state, nation and the world.
learning_outcomes: Explain the knowledge and skills required to work effectively and inclusively with learners with diverse languages and cultures backgrounds and perspectives
Plan curriculum, assessment, and evaluation of learning using curriculum frameworks and evidence-based pedagogical practices relevant to learners of diverse languages backgrounds
Interpret and implement knowledge of culturally responsive teaching that respects and values the rights of Aboriginal children and the sovereignties of Aboriginal First Nations through education
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX107 First Nations Peoples, Knowledges and Culturally Responsive Teaching OR must not have completed EDUC2061 Teaching and Learning in Aboriginal Education if a transition student only from University of South Australia
assessment: Data Collection and/or Analysis, Design Project – 30%

title: Exploring Mathematics through Play
overview: This course aims to introduce pedagogical approaches appropriate for assisting young learners to engage in mathematical inquiry and learning, building on their current knowledge and ways they understand mathematical concepts in their everyday play-based activities.
learning_outcomes: Plan for and implement learning experiences using the Early Years Learning Framework
Analyse how young children develop mathematical understanding through play, including multi-modal expressions in revealing children’s mathematical thinking and understandings
Analyse and utilise a wide range of resources, including the use of multi-modal tools and pedagogical documentation to support young children’s mathematical understandings
Demonstrate subject matter expertise in the effective teaching of numeracy, including building fluency, understanding, problem-solving, and reasoning
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC3089 Mathematics Education (Early Childhood) at the University of South Australia

title: Language and Learning
overview: The course aims to develop students’ understanding of theories of language, including developmental theory, sociocultural theory, semiotic theory and systemic functional linguistics. Students will learn about the contextualisation of language development and learning within home, community and educational contexts. Students will gain an understanding of the importance of phonological awareness, phonemic awareness, phonics, issues associated with difficulties acquiring language, and pedagogical implications. Language in this course is understood to be inclusive of oral and written language and to include English as a first language, English as an additional language, bilingualism and multilingualism and the practices of translanguaging, and to be integrally related to identity.
learning_outcomes: Explain the connections between language, culture, identity and home and community languages
Understand and explain the implications of culturally sustaining and expanding pedagogies to support and value plurilingualism and variation in language learning
Explain that language learning, language development and language practices are influenced by sociocultural contexts, through a functional model of language
Analyse and apply the levels of language (sounds, words, grammar and sentences, register and genre) to texts in various modes to inform teaching
Apply a functional theory of language development and its implications for educational settings
antirequisites: Must not have completed  EDUCX105 Learning About Language/EDUCX300 Curriculum Connections

title: Pedagogies in Early Childhood
overview: The aim of this course is to prepare students for teaching in early childhood settings by exploring key early childhood pedagogical practices as informed by key policy, theory, and research. This course is organised in three modules that explore (1) Introduction to curriculum, pedagogy, and assessment in the early years, (2) Explores key early childhood pedagogies and (3) Examines everyday pedagogical choices. This course strongly aligns with the EYLF and ACECQA requirements for early childhood education.
learning_outcomes: Connect key aspects of the EYLF planning cycle to pedagogical practices
Critically reflect on and implement effective planning and teaching strategies within early childhood settings
Identify core components of creating a positive learning environment for all learners through guiding behaviour and engaging young learners
Apply theoretical knowledge of engaging young learners and guiding behaviour in positive learning environments
Explore, implement and analyse alternative pedagogies that are core to early childhood education
corequisites: Must be enrolled in EDUC6900 Professional Experience 2: Preschool Pedagogies and Practices
antirequisites: N/A

title: Arts and Technologies Education
overview: This course introduces interdisciplinary pedagogies and content knowledge for Arts Education and Technologies Education in the Early Childhood and Primary contexts.
learning_outcomes: Develop an understanding of the core ideas, skills, and practices in Arts, Design & Technology, and Digital Technologies, and their role in fostering creativity and critical thinking
Learn how to plan, implement, and integrate Arts and Technology education within the Australian Curriculum, applying effective teaching strategies for student engagement
Gain skills in using design thinking and the creative process to solve problems and encourage innovation in both arts and technology projects.
Understand the importance of reflective practice for continuous improvement as both a learner and educator in the arts and technology fields.
Explore the ethical considerations in Arts and Technology education, including cultural sensitivity, sustainability, and promoting student wellbeing.
Learn how to apply arts and technology concepts in classroom activities that foster hands-on learning, collaboration, and student-driven exploration.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC5253 Curriculum and Pedagogy 3 (Arts and Technologies) at the University of South Australia

title: Classroom Management and Inclusive Education
overview: The aim of this course is to develop critical knowledge, skills, and attitudes to support PSTs to foster positive, safe and inclusive learning environments by proactively supporting productive student behaviours, and implementing inclusive teaching practices to provide for special educational needs of students of all abilities. It investigates policies and legislation, a range strategies to support behaviour and learning, exceptionality, neurodiversity, stakeholder partnerships, and student-centred planning. This course places creating positive learning environments as an essential pillar of the teaching and learning process.
learning_outcomes: A strong understanding of student diversity, possible impacts on student achievement and teacher obligations
A strong understanding of the role of rules and routines in establishing structured, safe, and inclusive classroom environment
A clear understanding of the efficacy of proactive practices in supporting student engagement, including the role of high-quality instruction as a proactive practice

An ability to practise and apply and proactive practices, including setting high expectations, building positive relationships, providing structure, and setting ambitious, achievable and personalised goals

An ability to practice and apply techniques that positively and effectively manage behaviour in classroom contexts, including the use of calm, consistent and proportional responses, behaviour modelling and feedback that gives attention to the desired behaviour rather than the undesired behaviour
A foundational understanding of common whole-school behaviour frameworks
A strong understanding of the legislation, regulations, policies and obligations related to inclusion and what they mean for the work of teachers.
antirequisites: N/A

title: Reading and Literacies
overview: This course provides an advanced examination of the theories, research and pedagogy underpinning reading development and instruction. Students will critically evaluate evidence on reading acquisition, phonics, multimodality and comprehension, and design sophisticated, inclusive approaches to teaching reading that respond to diverse learner needs across primary settings.
learning_outcomes: Critically synthesise and evaluate theoretical frameworks and current research on reading development, constructing advanced understandings of the linguistic, cognitive and contextual dimensions of reading proficiency across diverse text types and learner groups.
Appraise and apply subject matter expertise in literacy instruction and reading pedagogies, including phonics and the explicit teaching of reading in subjects other than English

Design and critically evaluate sophisticated, theoretically justified instructional plans that integrate a wide repertoire of pedagogical strategies; including explicit, dialogic, embodied, multimodal and arts-based approaches to meet the needs of all learners

Critically analyse classroom texts using metalinguistic and structural frameworks, constructing and justifying evidence-based strategies for supporting meaning-making and comprehension for diverse learners.

Interpret and critically evaluate multiple forms of reading assessment data to make judgements about learner development and generate evidence-based plans for the teaching of reading in diverse contexts.
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC5005 Learning About Language
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX215 Learning About Reading

title: Primary Science Education
overview: This course examines key constructs in how children learn science as the basis for planning and assessing learning experiences across the primary years. Students will critically evaluate inquiry-based and social constructivist perspectives on learning, investigate current pedagogies for thinking and working scientifically, and design, justify and evaluate units of work that build inquiry skills, develop conceptual understanding across the science disciplines, and connect to real-world contexts.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse key aspects of thinking and working scientifically and the role of scientific inquiry in planning for learning across diverse primary contexts

Design a sequence of science learning experiences that incorporate a range of pedagogical strategies to engage learners in thinking and working scientifically, and to build and assess understanding across all three strands of the Australian Curriculum: Science
Critically evaluate, select and apply a range of resources, including digital resources, to support and assess children's scientific understanding, justifying choices.

Understand explicit teaching, modelling and scaffolding practices and explain how these support how a student’s brain learns and critically evaluating the evidence base that underpins these approaches and their application across diverse primary science contexts
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX222 Science Education

title: Primary Mathematics Education 1
overview: This course provides an advanced analysis of the goals, theories and research underpinning mathematics education in the primary years. Students will critically evaluate pedagogical approaches and design conceptually rich mathematical learning experiences that respond to learner diversity, leverage digital tools, and embed formative assessment within curriculum frameworks.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and deconstruct mathematics curriculum content descriptors, generating learning progressions with theoretically justified learning intentions, success criteria and differentiation strategies.
Design and evaluate conceptually developmental learning sequences that align with curriculum frameworks and respond to the mathematical needs of all learners.
Appraise and integrate digital technologies and manipulatives as pedagogical tools, critically evaluating their impact on student conceptual understanding in mathematics.
Synthesise evidence from formative assessment data to make informed, adaptive decisions about mathematics instruction that improve outcomes for diverse learners.
Design and evaluate instructional sequences that embed spacing, retrieval practice and progressive challenge, using cognitive load research to justify sequencing decisions.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX106 Mathematics Education 1

title: Professional Experience 2: Preschool Pedagogies and Practices
overview: This course aims to build pre-service teachers capacities to collaborate on, codesign and enact inquiry-based pedagogies and documentation in preschool contexts.
learning_outcomes: Display effective professional relationships and dispositions with children, families, colleagues and other professionals in a preschool setting
Apply knowledge and skills with creativity, initiative and a high level of personal autonomy, accountability and respect while working in a team setting within the field and on campus

Apply an advanced body of knowledge of contemporary theories and practice as they engage with curriculum documents, children, families, colleagues, community and other professionals to implement democratic inquiry-based pedagogies in a preschool setting
Design and evaluate the use of pedagogical documentation to demonstrate children's learning and provide evidence of developing practices as a teacher
Manage the daily tasks, routines and administrative duties associated with the work of teachers in a selected educational setting

Reflect on teaching and learning experiences in the light of professional standards, policies, legal and ethical guidelines for the profession and developing beliefs of the role of early-years educators
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUCX215 Learning About Reading
corequisites: Must be enrolled in Part-time students at a grade of at least Prerequisite or concurrent enrolment required
antirequisites: Must not have completed  EDUC6049 Early Childhood Professional Experience and Reflection (inquiry into Practice) at the University of South Australia

title: Professional Experience 1: Planning, Teaching, Assessing and Managing the Classroom Environment
overview: This course supports preservice teachers to understand the curriculum frameworks commonly used in Australian schools and to use these curricula to plan effective lessons and units of work during placement.
learning_outcomes: Apply knowledge of current school curricula in Australia to lesson and unit planning
Sequence learning within and across lessons and evaluate the effectiveness
Use a range of appropriate classroom management practices that build positive relationships with students to facilitate wellbeing and engagement
Plan for and implement a range of teaching practices including differentiation for diverse learning communities

Design diagnostic, formative and summative assessments based on curriculum frameworks that enable feedback to students and produce effective assessment data for informing planning, teaching and reporting
prerequisites: If undertaking MATPR Master of Teaching (Primary) THEN must have completed EDUC6008 Classroom Management and Inclusive Education/EDUCX105 Learning About Language AND must have completed EDUCX103 Effective Pedagogical Practices AND if undertaking MATSE Master of Teaching (Secondary) THEN must have completed  EDUC6119 Play, Learning and Development/ EDUCX103 Effective Pedagogical Practices/and at least one (1) curriculum course
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC5904 Reflexive Practice and Professional Experience 1 at the University of South Australia

title: Primary Health and Physical Education
overview: This course provides an advanced critical examination of the theoretical, pedagogical and curricular foundations of Health and Physical Education. Students will synthesise research and literature on physical activity, inclusive pedagogy and cultural diversity to design, evaluate and lead appropriate HPE learning experiences, as well as develop critical professional capacity to advocate for equitable, evidence-based HPE practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically synthesise and evaluate research and literature on physical activity, health and development, constructing informed arguments about the role of HPE in addressing inequity and challenging biases affecting diverse learner groups.
Appraise and integrate intercultural competencies, disciplinary knowledge and professional judgement to lead equitable, culturally responsive outcomes across the HPE curriculum.
Embed theoretically justified principles of inclusive practice, cultural diversity and holistic learner development across physical, cognitive, social and affective domains.

Construct, lead and critically evaluate HPE lessons and units to be safe, inclusive and developmentally appropriate as well as responsive to the needs of EAL/D, First Nations and diverse learner groups.
Conduct and lead rigorous critical self-reflection into HPE practice, generating evidence-based models of culturally, socially and physically inclusive teaching for ongoing professional improvement.
Design, facilitate and critically evaluate rich HPE learning experiences for peers and students, demonstrating capacity for self-directed professional inquiry and innovation in HPE.
antirequisites: Must not have completed 1 of EDUC2006 Health and Physical Education at the University of South Australia/EDUCX421 Health and Physical Education

title: Humanities and Social Science Education
overview: This course introduces the Humanities and Social Sciences (HASS) learning area through the Early Years Learning Framework and the Australian Curriculum: HASS. The course explores how the subjects of history, geography, civics and citizenship and economics and business build the capacity of young people to make sense of their world and participate as active citizens in their everyday lives and into the future.
learning_outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the curriculum frameworks that underpin the Humanities and Social Science learning area
Knowledge of and skill in planning and sequencing content and tasks so that they become increasingly challenging and incorporate spacing and retrieval practices
Use curriculum frameworks and a wide variety of evidence-based teacher resources to plan inclusive learning experiences in Humanities and Social Sciences
Effectively select a range of evidence-based assessment practices to evaluate progress, adjust instruction, provide targeted feedback, and support learning
Understand and use key Humanities and Social Sciences concepts as they relate to the curriculum frameworks to plan learning experiences that are inclusive of all learners
Critique evidence-based resources that support student engagement and learning while highlighting the importance of student questions within the learning area
antirequisites: N/A

title: Professional Experience 2: Inquiry into Practice
overview: This course is designed to support preservice teachers to be successful in the Graduate Teacher Performance Assessment (GTPA) and the final placement in their program. Preservice teachers will draw on knowledge and skills from across their program as they engage in cycles of planning, teaching, assessing, reflecting and appraising growth in learning. These cycles will inform preservice teachers’ inquiries into practice during placement and the completion of the GTPA. On placement, preservice teachers will undertake the teaching load of a graduate teacher and demonstrate that they are performing at the graduate level of the Australian Professional Standards for Teachers.
learning_outcomes: Collect, interpret and use a range of data when planning for teaching and learning and when making adjustments to teaching and assessment practices
Apply the official curriculum, other resources and knowledge of prior learning to design connected teaching and learning sequences and effective assessments
Differentiate planning and teaching to meet the needs of all learners
Critically analyse and evaluate pedagogical and assessment decisions, and the progress of student learning, with reference to literature and theory
Maintain a safe and inclusive learning environment over a sustained time
prerequisites: Must have completed EDUC6902 Professional Experience 1: Planning, Teaching, Assessing and Managing the Classroom Environment
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX412 Professional Experience 2: Inquiry into Practice

title: Health and Physical Education for Secondary Teaching 1
overview: This course examines pedagogy, learning sequence design, and assessment in Health and Physical Education (HPE) within the Australian Curriculum. It focuses on the development of professional practice, leadership, and evidence-based reflective evaluation to promote transformative teaching and learning.
learning_outcomes: Plan extended learning sequences by synthesizing information on the diversity of learner needs, contextual constraints, complex pedagogical content knowledge, assessment and the Australian Curriculum (HPE).
Apply & justify the use of inclusive, collaborative & dialogic pedagogies when planning for the holistic development of diverse learners in Health and Physical Education.
Plan and teach lesson sequences aligned with the Australian Curriculum (HPE) that demonstrate safe, engaging, success-orientated movement experiences for learners with varying experiences and needs.

Demonstrate & justify teaching capacities to influence learning by establishing a positive learning environment, interacting with learners in a professional and engaging manner, and clearly communicating expectations.
Reflectively evaluate practice using evidence-based inquiry to transform teacher capabilities and progress student learning.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX210 Health and Physical Education for Secondary Teaching 1

title: Mathematics for Secondary Teaching 1
overview: This aim of this course is to extend preservice teachers' capacity for self-reflection to support their personal growth and development as teachers of mathematics. Students will critically examine the domains of mathematical knowledge for teaching and research-informed strategies that emphasise teaching for understanding, evaluate research on mathematical learning, and design, justify and evaluate learning experiences for diverse learners .
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate and apply research-informed strategies for teaching mathematics in the middle years, justifying pedagogical choices in response to learner needs and contexts.

Critically examine and reflect on personal and professional assumptions about the nature of mathematics taught in schools, analysing how these inform and shape development as a teacher of mathematics.
Critically evaluate, select and apply a range of resources to support and enhance student learning in mathematics, justifying choices with reference to research and learner needs.
Design, justify and evaluate learning experiences and sequences for particular contexts and purposes, aligned with relevant curriculum frameworks.
Observe, analyse and interpret teacher practice in mathematics classrooms using research-informed frameworks, connecting observed approaches to evidence on student learning.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX216 Mathematics for Secondary Teaching 1 OR must not have completed EDUC5184 Mathematics for Secondary Teaching 1 at the University of South Australia

title: Humanities and Social Sciences for Secondary Teaching 1
overview: This course critically examines the disciplinary and pedagogical foundations of Humanities and Social Sciences in the secondary years, developing students' capacity to evaluate, design and justify curriculum and teaching approaches across History, Geography, Civics and Citizenship, and Economics and Business.
learning_outcomes: Critically evaluate Humanities and Social Sciences as a specialisation in a secondary school context, synthesising curriculum frameworks, pedagogical approaches and resources to justify evidence-based practice.
Design and critically evaluate lesson plans and learning sequences that integrate advanced, evidence-informed pedagogies to support diverse learners in Humanities and Social Sciences.

Design, justify and critically evaluate an out-of-school learning experience that is achievable, engaging and accessible for diverse learner groups, drawing on place-based and experiential learning research.
Apply advanced skills of critical reflection and analysis to evaluate and refine teaching and learning sequences, generating evidence-based recommendations for improved practice.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX236 Humanities and Social Sciences for Secondary Teaching 1

title: Science for Secondary Teaching 1
overview: The aim of this course is to extend preservice teachers' critical understanding of the nature of scientific knowledge and the purpose of teaching science in the secondary school context. Students will critically examine learning theories, evaluate research on science education and curriculum frameworks, and design, justify and evaluate inquiry-based and laboratory learning experiences for diverse learners across the secondary years.
learning_outcomes: Critically examine personal and disciplinary assumptions about the nature of science, drawing on science education research and theoretical perspectives to inform curriculum thinking
Critically evaluate and apply strategies for teaching science in the middle years, justifying pedagogical choices in response to learner needs and contexts.
Analyse the origins and persistence of alternative conceptions in science, developing evidence-informed strategies to identify and address them.
Observe, analyse and interpret science teaching practice, connecting observed approaches to evidence on student learning and providing informed feedback to peers.
Design, justify and evaluate science learning experiences that are contextually appropriate, inclusive and grounded in principles of inquiry and safe laboratory practice.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX237 Science for Secondary Teaching 1

title: English for Secondary Teaching 1
overview: This course examines English curriculum content, design, literary pedagogy and assessment for the secondary years. Pre-service teachers will critically evaluate theoretical frameworks and research underpinning English education, design sophisticated and inclusive learning sequences, and develop the professional capacity to lead transformative English teaching practice in middle secondary contexts. They will evaluate and reflect critically on aspects of their professional practice.
learning_outcomes: Critically synthesise and apply advanced literary knowledge to the selection and appraisal of literary texts relevant for study in English at secondary level.
Evaluate and critique a range of English pedagogical approaches constructing evidence-based arguments for inclusive and culturally responsive practice.
Design and justify complex, theoretically grounded English lessons that respond to diverse learner needs, identities and backgrounds in secondary contexts.
Critically evaluate the scope and sequence of secondary English curricula
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUCX419 English for Secondary Teaching 1

title: Languages for Secondary Teaching 1
overview: This course provides an advanced critical examination of the theoretical, curricular and pedagogical foundations of Languages education in Australian secondary contexts. Students will synthesise research and policy to design, implement, evaluate and advocate for high-quality multilingually oriented Languages teaching that promotes proficiency and intercultural understanding for diverse learners.
learning_outcomes: Critically analyse and synthesise research to design, implement and evaluate intercultural and multilingual learning experiences secondary education.
Synthesise theory and curriculum frameworks to design, justify and evaluate Languages learning sequences that respond to diverse learner needs and contemporary challenges.
Critically evaluate, adapt and apply language teaching methodologies and pedagogies to address complex educational challenges across diverse Australian education contexts.
Critically appraise, adapt and justify resources and technologies for language teaching, addressing varied learning needs and educational contexts.

Engage in critical reflection and scholarly inquiry into contemporary theory and practice in languages education, to inform ongoing development of learners, users and teachers of languages in secondary education contexts.
antirequisites: Must not have completed EDUC1027 Foundations in Languages Education OR must not have completed EDUC2089 Teaching and Learning a New Language at the University of South Australia

title: AI for Business
overview: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is changing the world, it is impacting every industry and is forecast to be a multi-trillion dollar industry by the end of the decade. Many of the world's largest companies, including Microsoft, Google, Facebook and Amazon, heavily utilise AI throughout their businesses to outpace their competitors. But what is Artificial Intelligence? And how can it be leveraged to improve a business? This course aims to answer these questions through exploring the types of AI that exist, how AI is currently being used to create value within businesses, and how this transformative technology can be implemented effectively to create new products and services. Throughout the course we will also explore the practical implementation challenges alongside the societal, economic and ethical questions that arise when applying AI in business.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish the different types of AI and how they are applied in a business context
Identify the different types of datasets and data sources and how they can be leveraged to gain strategic advantage with AI
Assess an organisation's existing data sources and business processes to identify opportunities to gain strategic advantage using AI
Analyse and develop implementation strategies for AI solutions in business contexts, considering viability, scalability, and organisational readiness
Communicate the social, economic and ethical implications of applying AI in real world applications
antirequisites: N/A

title: Tech eChallenge (Advanced)
overview: The Tech eChallenge (Advanced) embraces technology innovation and with the emphasis on product or service design leveraging technology. The development of a prototype that has market relevance for different streams including not limited to EdTech, AgTech, MedTech, DeepTech and FinTech. Receiving instruction and guidance from experienced mentors, underpinned by theory, students develop prototypes that address a market need and then present these to a panel of industry judges where they receive feedback about their innovations.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically evaluate potential entrepreneurial opportunity by applying the Jobs to Be Done framework to systematically uncover an unmet need in the market.
Develop a Prototype to satisfy the market needs leveraging enabling technologies.
Build an effective entrepreneurial team to develop strategies to exploit the entrepreneurial opportunity.
Communicate and present the new entrepreneurial venture to persuade relevant stakeholders including investors.
antirequisites: N/A

title: eChallenge (Advanced)
overview: This course aims to critically assess the viability of innovative project ideas, an indispensable skill across all career paths, and not solely for those embarking on an entrepreneurial journey. Research underscores that the university period is pivotal for cultivating such expertise. Tailored for a postgraduate audience, this eChallenge course is meticulously structured to enable students to critically analyse customer-related challenges and opportunities, innovate solutions through strategic frameworks, and rigorously test these concepts through deep engagement with customers, mentors, and industry professionals. Students will have the opportunity to present their refined ideas to a panel of investors from the industry. Moreover, this course facilitates extensive networking opportunities during interactions with industry leaders. In addition to practical skills, the course offers a range of cash and in-kind prizes, with the culmination at a prestigious black-tie awards dinner attended by industry veterans and investors. This course not only marks the beginning of many successful entrepreneurial careers but also enriches your academic and professional trajectory with profound personal and intellectual growth.
learning_outcomes: Identify and critically evaluate a potential innovative project as an entrepreneurial opportunity using a systematic process
Determine a practical and innovative resource strategy to exploit the entrepreneurial opportunity in an innovative manner, employing critical thinking
Build an effective entrepreneurial team to develop strategies to exploit the entrepreneurial opportunity
Communicate and present an entrepreneurial opportunity as a new venture concept to relevant stakeholders including investors
antirequisites: N/A

title: New Venture Creation
overview: This course is aimed at exposing the students to modern approaches to new venture creation; placing the entrepreneurial team at the centre of the process. It is designed for anyone who needs to assess and develop potential business or project opportunities that are mainly, but not exclusively, based on a technological concept or a social innovation. Screening techniques are introduced that will address the new venture value proposition: including analysis of the underlying business concept, the base technology, benefits to customers, and fit with potential markets. Models for new venture development which include consideration of the resourcing requirements, team development and future strategies will be treated in depth; and a comprehensive model for new venture validation will be developed during the course.
learning_outcomes: Identify the difference between a business idea and a potential innovative business opportunity
Articulate a new venture value proposition and communicate ideas and concepts effectively
Build an assessment process for a new venture to determine its desirability, feasibility, viability, and sustainability
Develop practical strategies for exploiting business opportunity and resourcing new venture creation and development
Prepare a comprehensive validation for a potential new venture of your own design and recommend future strategy
antirequisites: N/A

title: Leading the Family Enterprise
overview: Family enterprises—including family-owned businesses as well as broader wealth, governance, and entrepreneurial activities—are central to economies worldwide. This course provides an advanced understanding of their distinctiveness, equipping students to critically evaluate complex issues and strategies for their long-term continuity. Drawing on real-world case studies, students will integrate and apply relevant theories and frameworks to examine governance, succession, innovation, entrepreneurship, and sustainability across both business and non-business family assets. Emphasis is placed on developing and evaluating strategies that foster leadership and transgenerational success. The course also builds interpersonal and communication skills for influencing diverse audiences as leaders or advisors.
learning_outcomes: Evaluate and synthesise the relevant theories and frameworks to explain the uniqueness of family enterprises.
Integrate and critically apply relevant theories and frameworks to evaluate complex family enterprise issues.
Develop and critically evaluate strategies for fostering leadership, entrepreneurship, and sustainability within the broader family enterprise context.
Apply the interpersonal skills and processes required to influence and enhance effectiveness in team environments.
